The front of the decanter features a 24-karat gold-plated ornament with a fine patina finish, brought to life as a jovial, accordion-playing Catrina dancing to her own music.

This moveable artisanal piece was handcrafted at the Milagros de Latón artisan workshop in Tesistán, Jalisco. A highly intricate work, it is composed of almost 40 individual parts cast from 10 separate molds.

clase-azul-25th-anniversary.title: Clase Azul Reposado Tequila
clase-azul-25th-anniversary.bodyHtml:
Clase Azul Reposado Tequila is an ultra-premium tequila made from 100% Blue Weber Agave, harvested in the highlands of Jalisco, Mexico. Cooked slowly in traditional brick ovens and distilled twice in copper pot stills, it is aged for eight months in American whiskey casks. This aging process imparts a silky texture, rich hazelnut and vanilla flavors, and a smooth profile. Encased in Clase Azul's iconic, hand-painted ceramic decanter featuring cobalt blue feather designs, it stands as an international symbol of luxury and Mexican craftsmanship.

Food Pairing: Pairs exceptionally well with slow-cooked pork carnitas, grilled ribeye steak, aged cheeses such as Manchego, mole poblano, dark chocolate desserts, or vanilla bean ice cream.

Tasting Notes : Intense amber color with copper highlights and a smooth, rich, medium-to-full body with a silky mouthfeel.

Nose : Agave nectar, vanilla, candied orange peel, toasted oak, hazelnut, and subtle hints of cinnamon.

Palate : Smooth and complex with rich flavors of cooked agave, toasted oak, vanilla, clove, hazelnut, and soft caramel.

Finish : Long, warm, and elegant finish with lingering notes of sweet agave, vanilla, toasted wood, and gentle baking spice.

Serve : Serve neat at room temperature in a tulip-shaped glass or Tequila Riedel glass to fully appreciate its aromas and flavor profile.

clase-azul-mezcal-guerrero.title: Clase Azul Guerrero Mezcal
clase-azul-mezcal-guerrero.bodyHtml:
Clase Azul Guerrero Mezcal is an ultra-premium mezcal crafted from 100% wild Papalote Agave (Agave cupreata), native to the rugged mountain slopes of Guerrero, Mexico. Produced through traditional artisanal methods including pit-roasting, stone-milling, and copper-still distillation, it delivers a uniquely delicate and complex flavor profile that beautifully balances crystal-clear agave sweetness with subtle floral, herbal, and smoky character. Encased in an iconic, handcrafted green ceramic decanter adorned with intricate handcrafted copper work and sea-shell-inspired motifs, this expression pays homage to the coastal culture, natural beauty, and heritage of Guerrero.

Food Pairing: Pairs exceptionally well with grilled seafood, ceviche, roasted pork carnitas, fresh goat cheese, citrus-based salads, and key lime or tropical fruit desserts.

Tasting Notes : Crystal-clear body with bright silver highlights and a smooth, medium-to-full body with a silky, delicate mouthfeel.

Nose : Grapefruit peel, fresh rosemary, peanut shell, butter, and subtle damp forest floor notes with delicate herbal and floral aromas.

Palate : Smooth and complex with flavors of sweet roasted agave, fresh seaweed, lemon juice, light tobacco, and a gentle wood smoke undertone.

Finish : Long, clean, and elegant with lingering notes of herbal spice, light citrus zest, and soft, sweet smoke.

Serve : Serve neat at room temperature in a wide-rimmed glass or traditional mezcal copita to fully appreciate its delicate aromas and flavor profile.

scribe-carneros-pinot-noir.title: Scribe Los Carneros Pinot Noir 2023 750ml
scribe-carneros-pinot-noir.bodyHtml: Fermented with native, wild yeast in concrete or steel then aged in neutral oak barrels for about six months. The Carneros Pinot expresses a soft, delicate touch and feel. Expect spicy and tart notes of bay laurel, cranberries and pink peppercorn.

scribe-atlas-west-napa-valley-cabernet.title: Penfolds Bin 704 Cabernet Sauvignon 2019
scribe-atlas-west-napa-valley-cabernet.bodyHtml:
Penfolds Bin 704 Cabernet Sauvignon 2019 is a modern, beautifully sculpted, and sophisticated Napa Valley red wine that showcases classic Californian terroir interpreted through Penfolds’ historic winemaking lens. Named as a reverse mirror image of its Australian counterpart Bin 407, it represents a French oak-matured expression of pure Cabernet Sauvignon. In the glass, it reveals a dense ruby-purple hue with a brilliant crimson rim. The aromatic profile is rich and layered, presenting ripe blackcurrant, dark plum, glazed cherries, and blackberry compote, underscored by subtle notes of cocoa powder, bay leaf, cedarwood, and delicate French oak spice. On the palate, it is full-bodied, supple, and focused, offering concentrated dark fruit balanced by lively, mouthwatering acidity, fine-grained graphite minerality, and polished, silky tannins that carry through to an expansive, enduring finish.

Food Pairing: Grilled prime ribeye steak, rosemary garlic roasted rack of lamb, braised beef short ribs, venison medallions, and aged sharp cheddar.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This Napa wine from the Australian-based producer over delivers on its price point, offering tremendous flavor, complexity and approachability in its youth. Expansive in dense black and red fruit, cocoa powder and silky tannin, it offers breadth and depth and is intensely compelling.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The fruit for the 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon Bin 704 is from across Napa Valley, and the classy fruit is shaped by French oak (40% new) and firm tannins through the finish. This is supple and sweet and shows blood plum, raspberry, red licorice and even cocoa. The wine is long and lingering and shapely. Sophisticated.

no-9-cabernet-sauvignon-wonderland.title: The Wonderland Project No.9 Cabernet Sauvignon 2022
no-9-cabernet-sauvignon-wonderland.bodyHtml:
On the nose, it opens with rich aromas of blackcurrant, ripe plum, and blackberry compote, accented by subtle notes of cedar, tobacco leaf, and vanilla from well-integrated oak aging. The palate is plush and layered, offering concentrated dark fruit flavors balanced by graphite, cocoa, and a touch of dried herbs. Medium to full-bodied with velvety tannins, it maintains impressive freshness through a core of lively acidity. The finish is long and polished, leaving lingering hints of mocha and cassis. This wine beautifully combines structure and elegance, showcasing modern Napa craftsmanship with classic Cabernet depth.

Goes well with red meats, grilled steaks, aged cheeses, and rich pasta dishes.

the-kraken-attacks.title: The Kraken Attacks Ontario
the-kraken-attacks.bodyHtml: As dark as your mood sitting in traffic, The Kraken is a spiced Caribbean rum blended with natural flavors and caramel color. No longer confined to the depths of the Pacific, its tentacles have been spotted across the Golden State, from San Diego to Shasta, destroying taco trucks and panning for gold. This limited edition Kraken Attacks California bottle carries the original 94-Proof recipe.

rebel-yell-10-year-single-barrel.title: Rebel 10 Year Old Single Barrel Bourbon
rebel-yell-10-year-single-barrel.bodyHtml:
Aged in charred oak barrels for 10 years, this bourbon boasts a unique flavor profile specific to each batch. It’s one-of-a-kind, just like the rebels who drink it.

TASTING NOTES

Hints of caramel and citrus on your first sips. But continue drinking and it morphs into a velvety oak flavor with unabashed spice.


INGREDIENTS

Corn, wheat, and malt

last-mountain-release-1-3-wood-rye.title: Last Mountain Distillery Release #1 3 Wood Rye
last-mountain-release-1-3-wood-rye.bodyHtml: Last Mountain Distillery Release #1 3 Wood Rye is a Canadian rye whisky from Last Mountain Distillery in Lumsden, Saskatchewan, which describes itself as the province's first micro-distillery. Bottled at 45% ABV in a 750ml bottle.

perrier-jouet-belle-epoque-rose-1.title: Perrier-Jouet Belle Epoque Rose 2012 1.5L Magnum
perrier-jouet-belle-epoque-rose-1.bodyHtml:
Perrier-Jouët Belle Époque Rosé 2012 is an iconic prestige cuvée Champagne of extraordinary elegance, finesse, and complexity. Presenting a luminous pale salmon-pink hue with copper highlights in the glass, it opens with a delicate and refined bouquet of wild strawberries, red currant, white peach, and orange blossom, layered with nuances of warm brioche, pink grapefruit, and subtle mineral flint. On the palate, it is medium- to full-bodied, precise, and beautifully balanced, featuring a silky, fine-grained mousse. Vibrant natural acidity frames rich flavors of fresh red berries, candied citrus, and subtle baking spice, culminating in a long, crisp, and mouthwatering saline finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs magnificently with pan-seared duck breast with cherry reduction, roasted wild salmon, butter-poached lobster, fresh langoustines, and delicate berry tartlets.

96 Points - James Suckling

This has complex notes of praline, beeswax, raspberries, oyster shells, grapefruit and apricot tarts. Elegant and thoughtfully integrated, with very fine and silky bubbles alongside intense yet delicate layers. Long and saline at the end. Drink now.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This is an iconic rosé, clean and pure with its light color and textured, structured fruits. It has plenty of the perfumed character and the mineral acidity to balance hints of fresh-baked bread and spice. Drink from 2025. Roger Voss

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Smoky notes of toasted brioche play off of minerally accents of oyster shell and wet chalk on the nose and palate of this rich rosé Champagne. Meshed with a spine of lively acidity and a juicy profile of nectarine, raspberry and Mandarin orange fruit flavors, this is long and creamy on the well-spiced finish. Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Pinot Meunier. Drink now through 2032.

chateau-anseillan-2018.title: Chateau Anseillan Pauillac 2018 750ml
chateau-anseillan-2018.bodyHtml: Anseillan Pauillac 2018 comes from the Rothschild family of Château Lafite Rothschild. The vineyard lies around the village of Anseillan, east of Lafite between the château and the Gironde, on north-facing, cooler and more clay-rich soils than Lafite's classic terroirs, suited to Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Petit Verdot. The 2018 season brought relentless rain from December to July, then intense summer heat that restored the vines; new batch selection was introduced at Anseillan this year. The blend is 48% Merlot, 39% Cabernet Sauvignon and 13% Petit Verdot, fermented in wood, concrete and steel and aged about 16 months in French oak. The estate notes cherry, smoky oak and Petit Verdot spice, and a peak between 2023 and 2028. 750 ml, 13.5%.

yellowstone-limited-edition.title: Yellowstone Bourbon Limited Edition 2022
yellowstone-limited-edition.bodyHtml:
Yellowstone Limited Edition 2022 is a Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey hand-selected by Limestone Branch Master Distiller Stephen Beam. It blends 7, 15 and 16 year old bourbons, with the 7 year old barrels finished in Marsala Superiore casks, a fortified Sicilian wine that adds dried fruit and citrus character. Released in the brand's 150th anniversary year, it is bottled at 101 proof (50.5% ABV) in a custom embossed 750ml bottle with a natural cork.

Tasting Notes: Dried apricot, honey, brown sugar and walnut.

Nose: Dried apricot and honey with hints of tobacco.

Palate: Dark brown sugar, dried fruit, walnut and dates, with a hint of vanilla.

Finish: Lingering, with palm sugar and tamarind.

Serve: Neat or with a splash of water.

pappy-van-winkle-12-year-old.title: Van Winkle Special Reserve 12 Year Old Lot B
pappy-van-winkle-12-year-old.bodyHtml:
Van Winkle Special Reserve 12 Year Old Lot B is a Kentucky straight bourbon bottled by the Old Rip Van Winkle Distillery in Frankfort, Kentucky. Aged 12 years and bottled at 90.4 proof (45.2% ABV), it is described by the family as the perfect combination of age and proof – a sweet, full-bodied whiskey some have called 'nectar', with a rich, deep character that can rival a fine cognac as an after-dinner drink. Brilliant amber-orange in the glass. 750ml.

Nose: Luscious, complex toffee.

Palate: Round, supple entry leading to a dry, expansive medium body with caramel, nuts and brown spices.

Finish: Lengthy and enveloping.

Serve: Neat, as an after-dinner pour.

wine-enthusiast-package.title: Enthusiast Package
wine-enthusiast-package.bodyHtml:
Explore the world of wines with our Enthusiast package, offering a delightful selection of vintages perfect for those looking to explore new flavours and expand their palate. Gain a deeper understanding of the complexity and variety of wines with an array of vintages selected to entice and educate adventurous palates.

  • Delightful wines from around the world
  • Handpicked by our team of experts
  • 6 Bottles of Red & White option includes 4 Reds and 2 Whites, while the 12 Bottles of Red & White option includes 8 Reds and 4 Whites.
  • Product information, taste notes, reviews and ratings, and best food pairing suggestions are included.

piper-heidsieck-brut-2012.title: Piper-Heidsieck Cuvee Brut
piper-heidsieck-brut-2012.bodyHtml:
Piper-Heidsieck Cuvée Brut is a quintessential and vibrant non-vintage Champagne that perfectly embodies the signature style of this historic house. Pouring a brilliant golden color with a lively, fine-beaded mousse, it opens with an expressive and fruit-forward bouquet. Inviting aromas of crisp green apple, fresh pear, and bright starfruit are beautifully intertwined with warm nuances of toasted almond, fresh hazelnut, and subtle baked brioche. On the palate, it is remarkably crisp, well-structured, and harmonious, driven by a dominant core of Pinot Noir that provides depth and character. The juicy orchard fruit flavors and refreshing acidity are perfectly balanced by a creamy, mouth-filling texture, culminating in a clean, elegant, and persistent finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs beautifully with freshly shucked oysters, crispy fish and chips, delicate fried calamari, light sushi rolls, and soft goat cheese.

91 Points - Wine Spectator

Creamy and well-balanced, this lively Champagne offers flavors of ripe black currant and black cherry, candied lemon peel, and brioche, plus fragrant notes of anise and clove. Pinot Noir, Pinot Meunier and Chardonnay.

90 Points - James Suckling

Croissants, sliced apples and lemon pastries on the nose of this creamy Champagne. It’s rounded and soft with attractive pastry character.

90 Points - Wine Enthusiast

The Champagne is balanced between a soft Brut character and crisper lemon flavors. That balance gives a fine wine, open and easy, but with a fine bite of acidity at the end.

glen-grant-1962-archive-release-4405.title: Gordon & MacPhail Archive Release Glen Grant 56 Year Old 1962 First Fill Sherry Butt 54.6% ABV
glen-grant-1962-archive-release-4405.bodyHtml:
Rich Sherry influences, dark fruits, dried figs and blackcurrant with spicy cloves. Thick treacle notes give way to polished oak and aged leather. The palate has fruitcake, intense spices , Seville orange and charred oak flavours. Morello cherries and liquorice give way to a charred edge and subtle coffee grounds. The finish is long and full bodied with plenty of spice and oak.

DISTILLED: 17th September 1962
BOTTLED: 18th September 2018
AGE: 56 Years Old
CASK TYPE: 1ST Fill Sherry Butt
CASK #: 4415
COLOUR: Darkest Mahogany
STRENGTH: 54.6%

bread-butter-reserve-napa-cab-sauv.title: Bread & Butter Reserve Cabernet Sauvignon 2021
bread-butter-reserve-napa-cab-sauv.bodyHtml:
A lush and expressive Cabernet Sauvignon with enticing aromas of mocha and blackberries. Flavors of black cherry, plum and savory baking spice complement a soft, rich mouthfeel, leading to a lingering finish.

90 Points - Wine Enthusiast

A savory intensity of flavor combining dark fruits, wet tobacco, clove and nutmeg, beef bouillon and spiced cocoa powder in this generous Cabernet Sauvignon combines palate coating tannins and mouthwatering acidity for a sticky, ample finish with a lot of length.

nicolas-catena-zapata-malbec-argentino.title: Catena Zapata Argentino Malbec 2023
nicolas-catena-zapata-malbec-argentino.bodyHtml:
Catena Zapata Argentino Malbec 2023 is a magnificent, iconic, and deeply complex high-altitude Argentine red wine crafted from century-old pre-phylloxera massal selection vines from the historic Angélica and Nicasia vineyards. Visually displaying an intense dark violet-purple core, it opens with a beautifully perfumed nose featuring wild blackberries, black cherries, and underripe plums, intricately interwoven with notes of crushed violets, dried herbs, dark cocoa, and fresh flinty minerality. On the palate, it exhibits full-bodied richness and effortless elegance, balanced by vibrant natural acidity and ultra-fine, chalky tannins that carry a dense core of blue and dark fruit toward a long, expressive, and harmonious finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs brilliantly with grilled prime ribeye, prime bife de lomo, braised lamb shanks, roasted game meats, mushroom risotto, and aged Gouda.

95 Points - James Suckling

This has an intriguing combination of violets, crushed stones, underripe plums and a subtle touch of pepper on the nose. The palate is firm, with blue fruit, tight focused tannins and impressive concentration and depth. Structured yet long and beautiful. So harmonious. Drink now or hold.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

A decidedly riper and more forward style than many of Catena Zapata's offerings, the 2023 Malbec Argentino combines ungrafted massal selections from two polar-opposite vineyard sources: the Angélica Vineyard in Maipú's Lunlunta district and Paraje Altamira's Nicasia Vineyard. It was vinified entirely in foudre with 20% whole clusters and aged for 12 months. The nose is deep and dark-fruited, welcomely lifted by a lovely floral component that builds with oxygen exposure. On the palate, it is velvety and rich yet impressively buoyant, transitioning to an explosive, ripe and powerful finish dominated by luscious fruits.

villa-real-reserva-red.title: Vila Real Grande Reserva Douro Red
villa-real-reserva-red.bodyHtml:
Vila Real Grande Reserva Douro DOC Red is a premium Portuguese red wine crafted from a rigorous selection of classic Douro grape varieties. Rich layers of black fruit, spice, and subtle oak are supported by firm tannins and excellent structure, leading to a long, elegant finish with impressive aging potential.
 
Food Pairing: Pairs best with grilled beef, roast lamb, game, hearty stews, and aged hard cheeses.

robert-mondavi-private-pinot-noir.title: Vint By Robert Mondavi Private Selection Cabernet Sauvignon
robert-mondavi-private-pinot-noir.bodyHtml: This rich and elegant red wine is a modernized expression of a California classic, crafted with fruit from cool-climate vineyards where slow ripening encourages complexity and depth of flavor. It opens with an inviting bouquet of black cherry, blackberry, and toasty oak, complemented by decadent aromas of vanilla, coffee, and dark chocolate. On the palate, the wine is ripe and elegant, featuring soft red and black fruit flavors supported by gentle tannins and well-integrated oak from aging in a combination of American and French barrels.

giffard-creme-de-cacao-brun-liqueur.title: Giffard Creme de Cacao Brun
giffard-creme-de-cacao-brun-liqueur.bodyHtml:
Giffard Crème de Cacao Brun is the brown cocoa liqueur from Giffard, the liqueur house in Angers in the Loire Valley that has been making liqueurs since 1885. It is made from cocoa extract and bottled at 25% ABV, here in a 500ml bottle. Deep brown in colour, it opens with a very strong cocoa aroma coated in vanilla and chocolate, and delivers an intense, smooth chocolate taste that recalls roasted cocoa beans. Giffard lists it as vegan, gluten free and lactose free, with no preservatives. It is a classic bar ingredient for chocolate cocktails such as the Alexander, and can also be poured over crushed ice.

Tasting Notes: Intense roasted cocoa, vanilla and chocolate.

Nose: Very strong cocoa with vanilla and chocolate.

Palate: Strong, smooth chocolate reminiscent of roasted cocoa beans.

Serve: Neat over crushed ice, or in chocolate cocktails.

nso-cabernet-sauvignon.title: NSO Cabernet Sauvignon 750ml
nso-cabernet-sauvignon.bodyHtml: The NSO Cabernet Sauvignon 750ml is a full-bodied red wine known for its rich and complex flavors, including dark fruit, oak, and spice notes. It typically exhibits aromas of blackberry, cassis, and vanilla, with a palate featuring ripe dark fruits, velvety tannins, and a touch of spice. This wine is often described as having a masculine character with firm tannins and a long aging potential.

brilla-rose-prosecco-doc.title: Brilla Prosecco Rose
brilla-rose-prosecco-doc.bodyHtml:
Critic tasting note: "The aroma is defined by a delightful blend of red cherries, white flowers, and a hint of orchard fruits. Ripe strawberry, delicate notes of peach, and a bright, lively, effervescent finish shape the palate of this easy-to-enjoy sparkler." - Wine Enthusiast

88 Points - Wine Enthusiast
"A vibrant and playful rosé Prosecco with lively notes of wild strawberry and citrus. Crisp, refreshing, and slightly fruity, perfect for festive occasions."

haymans-smith-cross-rum.title: Smith & Cross Traditional Jamaica Rum Navy Strength
haymans-smith-cross-rum.bodyHtml:
Smith & Cross Jamaica Rum contains only Wedderburn and Plummer pot still distillates, famous for their notes of exotic fruits and spice. The incomparable complexity of this rum delivers a tour de force of flavour that historically made it a cornerstone of classic rum drinks. We have chosen not to chill filter this spirit in order to retain its full flavour.

The mark of Smith & Cross traces its lineage to one of England’s oldest producers of sugar and spirits. Its history dates back to 1788 with a sugar refinery located at No. 203 Thames Street, by the London Docks. Over time, the firm and its partners became prominent handlers of Jamaica rum, with extensive underground cellars along the River Thames.

lindores-the-casks-of-lindores-lowland.title: Lindores The Casks of Lindores Bourbon
lindores-the-casks-of-lindores-lowland.bodyHtml:
We’re incredibly excited about this latest limited edition release, launched as part ‘The Casks of Lindores’ series, which has been created to showcase the award winning spirit of Lindores Abbey Distillery. This, the first release has been exclusively matured in ex-bourbon casks and bottled at 49.4% vol, which is a higher strength than the core single malt release at the distillery.

Tasting NotesLindores The Casks of Lindores – Bourbon Producer Notes

Colour: Pale Gold

Nose: Mellow fruity, red apples and pears combined with sweet vanilla, butterscotch and custard with citrus touches.

Palate: Vanilla mixed with orchard fruits like green cooking apples, citric pith with a hint of bitterness covered with oaky woody notes and spicy peppery touches.

Finish: Medium length lingering finish

john-walker-sons-king-george-cny-2023.title: John Walker & Sons King George V Lunar New Year 2023 Angel Chen Edition
john-walker-sons-king-george-cny-2023.bodyHtml: Drawn from extremely rare, precious casks, including irreplaceable whiskies from the now silent distillery of Port Ellen. This elegant rich and creamy whisky has rarity reflected in every drop, and its new limited-edition design, created by fashion designer Angel Chen, is the perfect gift to give to the once who never walks alone and to mark this year.

gran-coramino-cristalino.title: Gran Coramino Reposado Cristalino Tequila
gran-coramino-cristalino.bodyHtml: From our centuries old distilling process to our handcrafted methods, Gran Coramino™ honors dedication and grit. We plant and harvest the finest blue agaves in the heart of the Tequila Valley, cook them at peak maturity in traditional brick ovens before careful distillation in copper pot stills. Aged in Eastern European oak barrels, the tequila is then finished in California Cabernet wine casks. As a final step, it is meticulously filtered for flawless clarity and unparalleled smoothness, revealing subtle notes of caramel, honey, vanilla and berries.

tio-pepe-en-rama-sherry.title: Gonzalez Byass Tio Pepe Fino En Rama NV 750ml

hundred-acre-ark-cabernet-sauvignon-2019.title: Hundred Acre Ark Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon 2019
hundred-acre-ark-cabernet-sauvignon-2019.bodyHtml:
Stunning with a deep garnet color and aromas of blueberry pie and baked plums layered with savory notes of grilled meats, roasted lamb and tilled earth. The full-bodied palate has opulent black fruit with a firm, velvety body that finishes long and fresh.

99 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon Ark Vineyard features beguiling scents of Montreal-style smoked meat backed by waves of black cherries and cassis. It's full-bodied, rich, plush and expansive on the palate, captivating for its mix of savory and fruity flavors. Offering tons of fun in the glass, this finishes long and tannic but also smoothly silky. It's a complete wine by any measure.

chateau-margaux-2019.title: Chateau Margaux 2019 750ml
chateau-margaux-2019.bodyHtml:
The Grand Vin of Château Margaux 2019 is an excellent vintage and one of the precious wines we have been lucky enough to produce this decade, in 2015, 2016, 2018 and now 2019. Cabernet Sauvignon still forms the heart of the Château Margaux, accounting for 90% of the assemblage. Merlot accounts for 7%. In addition to our emblematic parcels, this year we have added the Merlots from the Haut du Jardin parcel which bring body and charm to the wine as a whole. The Cabernet Franc (2%) and the Petit Verdot (1%) complete the assemblage. Château Margaux represents 37% of the harvest.

100 Points - James Suckling

Amazing aromas of crushed stones and wet soil with fresh mushrooms, then going on to violets and other flowers. Dark fruit, too. Full-bodied, yet agile and fine, with a linear flow of tannins that run through the center of palate. The finesse of the tannins is exceptional, like raw silk and changing all the time. Cool and energetic, yet reserved. Zen-like. 37% of the production and 90% cabernet sauvignon, 7% merlot, 2% cabernet franc and 1% petit verdot.

100 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Another utterly heavenly wine from this estate is the 2019 Château Margaux, a blend of 90% Cabernet Sauvignon, 7% Merlot, 2% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Petit Verdot coming from a selection of just 37% of the total production. Deep purple, with an incredible array of ripe currants, blueberries, sweet tobacco, sandalwood, and toasted spices, it hits the palate with medium to full-bodied richness, a seamless, powerful, yet incredibly sexy mouthfeel, polished tannins, and a great, great finish.

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Is the 2019 Château Margaux the wine of the vintage? A strong case in its favor could certainly be made. Soaring from the glass with aromas of blackberries, raspberries, rose petals, violets, pencil shavings and vine smoke, it's full-bodied, layered and sensual, with a strikingly vibrant core of fruit that's framed by ripe, powdery tannins and bright acids, concluding with a penetrating, mouthwateringly saline finish of almost interminable duration. Complex, elegant and utterly compelling, this is a brilliant Bordeaux that anyone with the requisite disposable income is going to want to own. Best after 2029.

100 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This wine, packed with Cabernet Sauvignon, is dense but shows a majestic structure. By contrast and equally stunning, it has such perfumed fruits that are poised between power and elegance. The balance of this magnificent wine is there, bringing together black currant fruit and rich, sumptuous tannins. There is amazing aging potential here.
Barrel Sample: 98-100

98 Points - Decanter
This expands sideways, vertically and downwards, with a creamy mid palate and a rose petal, peony, raspberry and cassis collision on the nose. This is chewy in its tannic structure, full on and yet delicate and sappy. Fresh, elegant, perfumed and concentrated - clearly will age for decades. This is close in character to the 2009 or 2015, two exceptional vintages at Margaux and classic to the graceful yet concentrated signature of the property. 1% Petit Verdot to complete the blend, 100% new oak although barely discernible already. 37% of overall production in the 1st wine this year.
Barrel Sample: 98

chateau-mouton-rothschild-2010.title: Chateau Mouton Rothschild Le Petit Mouton 2016
chateau-mouton-rothschild-2010.bodyHtml:
A luxurious Pauillac with aromas of blackcurrant, blackberry, violet, cedar, graphite, and dark chocolate. Richly textured with velvety tannins, vibrant freshness, and remarkable concentration, it delivers exceptional depth, precision, and an elegant, persistent finish worthy of long cellaring.

Food Pairing: Pair with beef Wellington, grilled ribeye, roast lamb, venison, duck breast, truffle dishes, aged Comté, or mushroom risotto.

 

96 Points - James Suckling

This is a very powerful Petit Mouton with so much rich fruit and power. Full-bodied, tannic yet polished and long. Muscular for the second wine of Mouton.
94 Points - Decanter
Petit Mouton always shows charm in a rich, seductive expression, even in muscular vintages like 2016. It has the most wonderful sweetness to it, a highly seductive mix of the austerity of 2016 with the natural joy and exuberance of Petit Mouton, showing lovely rich damson fruit and huge persistence. It need time in the glass to open up.
93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate
The 2016 Le Petit Mouton is a blend of 62% Cabernet Sauvignon, 35% Merlot and 3% Cabernet Franc. It has a deep garnet-purple color and gives up an intensely plummy nose with cigar box and fallen leaves scents leading to aroma layers of kirsch, red and black currants and tilled soil. Medium-bodied with a racy line of freshness cutting through the muscular fruit and a good, firm frame of grainy tannins to support, it finishes on a lingering menthol note.
93 Points - Wine Enthusiast
This wine has structure and a generous fruity character from the ripeness of the Merlot in the blend. It is full in the mouth, with a smoky character on the palate and acidity coming through on the close
92 Points - Wine Spectator
The gently steeped plum and red currant fruit allows light anise, iron and cedar notes to enter slowly before taking hold on the slightly taut, savory-tinged finish. The iron element lingers longest in the end, giving this a sense of refinement. Best from 2022 through 2035.

grace-family-cabernet-sauvignon.title: Grace Family Cabernet Sauvignon 2011 3L Double Magnum
grace-family-cabernet-sauvignon.bodyHtml:
Grace Family Vineyards was planted with cuttings from the famed Bosché vineyard and first harvested in 1978. Those first grapes were handpicked by family and friends and taken to Caymus Winery in the back of a station wagon. This Napa Valley vineyard sure has come a long way over the past 30 years, but their wines still have that personal, family touch.

 

94 Points - James Suckling

A beautiful red with superb concentration for the vintage, featuring currants, berries and light milk chocolate. Full and silky, with a soft texture and a delicately fruity aftertaste. Dick Grace is a guru of classic Napa cab each vintage.  

93 Points - CellarTracker

carvalhas-memories-very-old-tawny-port.title: Quinta das Carvalhas 20 Year Old Tawny Port
carvalhas-memories-very-old-tawny-port.bodyHtml:
Rich and beautifully matured, this 20 Year Old Tawny offers layers of dried fruit, toasted nuts and warm spice with elegant oak complexity. The palate is smooth and concentrated, balanced by vibrant acidity that keeps the sweetness fresh through a long, refined finish.

Food Pairing: Almond tart, crème brûlée, toasted nuts, Comté, Gruyère, and other semi-hard aged cheeses.

morgans-way-cabernet-sauvignon-2019.title: Mayacamas Cabernet Sauvignon 2019 750ml
morgans-way-cabernet-sauvignon-2019.bodyHtml:
The 2019 Mayacamas Mt. Veeder Cabernet Sauvignon opens with lilac, dried sage, and graphite. Wild mountain blueberry, maraschino cherry, and blackberry round out the fruit profile. A very elegant wine with wonderful detail and nuance.


97 Points by Vinous
The 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon is a pretty rich, bombastic wine, especially for Mayacamas. A blast of dark fruit, incense, tobacco, licorice, spice and mocha hits the palate. I would give the 2019 at least a few years in bottle to settle down, as it is quite the powerhouse today. This is an unusually flamboyant wine with plenty of richness and a bit less in the way of subtlety. The opulence of the vintage comes through loud and clear.

96 Points by Wine Spectator
Loaded with character and energy, this version reveals heavy notes of zesty sweet bay leaf and sassafras that infuse a core of steeped red currant and mulberry fruit, all carried by bright acidity and iron-laced tannins. The long finish pulls everything together, with the fruit, savory and mineral elements in harmony. Showing an old-school touch, this has a long life ahead. Best from 2025 through 2045.

94 Points by Robert Parker's Wine Advocate
The 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon remains true to the winery's historic style, offering complex notes of dried herbs and mixed berries, carried across the palate by a wine that's medium-bodied, crisp and somewhat lean by modern Napa standards. It finishes long and dusty, promising well for the future.

chateau-montrose-2020.title: Chateau Montrose 2020 750ml
chateau-montrose-2020.bodyHtml:
The result of rigorous selection at each stage of production, in both the vineyard and the winery, this great, predominantly Cabernet Sauvignon wine is typical of the Saint-Estèphe appellation. Structured and tannic but with all the elegance and refinement of a Grand Cru Classé, with time it develops a delicate and complex bouquet.

Blend: 71% Cabernet Sauvignon, 23% Merlot, 6% Cabernet Franc, 1% Petit Verdot

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Surpassing the 2019 and rivaling the 2016 as this estate's finest vintage of the last few decades, the 2020 Montrose is a monument in the making. Wafting from the glass with aromas of violets, dark berries, licorice, loamy soil, black truffle and subtle spices, it's full-bodied, deep and layered, with a seamless, elegantly muscular profile, terrific purity and energy, beautifully powdery tannins and a long, resonant finish. It checks in at 13.7% alcohol, the same as the superb 2009, but it is even deeper, more vibrant and more complex than the 2009.

99 Points - James Suckling
The nose is really fantastic with lead pencil shavings, iron shavings, blackcurrants and lavender. Full- to medium-bodied with ultra-fine tannins that run the length of the wine. Wonderful persistence and personality. Juicy and savory finish. Always classy and sophisticated at the end.

98 Points - Decanter
Scented and perfumed on the nose with a delicate charm. Striking, full, round, juicy and crisp - this has bite and a sense of strictness in the frame that keeps things relatively narrow at this point but comes with excellent definition of elements. Great classicism with lots of freshness. Really very seductive, the black and blue fruit, graphite and touch of smoke grow and expand with richness and intensity but staying friendly at the same time thanks to the soft sweetness and juicy acidity. I just love the interplay between being serious and generous, structured but racy, intense yet precise. Such purity, and focus. Energetic and pent up, this is raring to go to show off its beauty but just being held back. Effortless, complex and compelling. I loved it a tiny bit less than the 2019 but it’s still one of the best in 2020.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck
The Grand Vin 2020 Chateau Montrose is brilliant and unquestionably in the lineup of the truly greats from this chateau, including the 1989, 1990, 2009, 2010, 2015, 2018, and 2019. With an IPT of 80 and a natural alcohol of 13.4%, its deep, saturated purple hue is followed by quintessential Saint-Estephe notes of pure cassis, graphite, tobacco leaf, acacia flowers, and loamy earth. Full-bodied, concentrated, and powerful, it nevertheless stays incredibly pure, elegant, and seamless, with perfectly ripe tannins. A blend of 71% Cabernet Sauvignon, 23% Merlot, 5% Cabernet Franc, and the rest Petit Verdot, is shines even today for its purity and balance, and it should be in the early stages of its prime drink window within a decade.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

Gorgeously rendered for the vintage, with a well-endowed core of loganberry, mulberry and cassis flavors that roll through and are laced with a cast iron hint, while tobacco, warm stone and black tea accents swirl in the background. The long, authoritative finish steadily melds the fruit with the cast iron edge. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot.

chateau-la-mission-haut-brion-2015.title: Chateau La Mission Haut-Brion 2016 750ml
chateau-la-mission-haut-brion-2015.bodyHtml:
Chateau La Mission Haut-Brion wine is definitely bewitching. It possesses a great intensity that will delight you with its complexity (a mixture of red fruits) and the signature of its terroir in its empyreumatic notes (Havana cigars, chocolate, roasting, cedar wood and so on). On the palate, the wine is spherical and generous without a trace of aggressiveness. It lengthens on silky tannins, making this wine so obvious that the taster succumbs to its charm.

Blend: 57.5% Merlot, 42.5% Cabernet Sauvignon 

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2016 La Mission Haut-Brion is a blend of 57.5% Merlot and 42.5% Cabernet Sauvignon. Deep garnet-purple in color, it is just a little muted to begin, soon unfurling to reveal slowly growing scents of crushed blackcurrants, black cherries, dark chocolate and candied violets with nuances of crushed rocks, tobacco leaf, forest floor and fragrant earth plus a hint of bergamot. Medium-bodied and exquisitely elegant, the palate offers perfectly ripe, fine-grained tannins and tons of freshness with layer upon layer of perfumed fruit and a very long, ferrous-laced finish.
Rating: 98+

98 Points - Decanter

This is a wonderful wine, it’s absolutely precise, finely wrought and gorgeously balanced between richness and elegance, with notes of damson, black cherry, slate and rosemary. Silky soft tannins highlight the concentration of the fruit and the grilled oak notes that are La Mission’s signature, with a fresh core that stretches out the palate. A low pH gives tension through the palate, and is highly seductive. No Cabernet Franc this year.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2016 La Mission Haut-Brion checks in as a Merlot-heavy blend, 57.5% Merlot and 42.5% Cabernet Sauvignon. About as pure and seamless (yet sexy) as they come in the vintage, it offers awesome notes of dried flowers, sweet currants, cedarwood, forest floor, and exotic spices. With a flawless texture, medium to full body, and ultra-fine tannins, this beauty builds incrementally on the palate with terrific mid-palate depth and a stunning finish. It’s sexier and more charming compared to the more backward Haut Brion, yet I suspect it will age just as long.

97 Points - James Suckling

Regal wine, showing alluringly ripe and dark plums, that carries a wealth of complexity in its DNA - fine spices, leaves, graphite, violets and more. The palate has very precise drive and super focused style and delivers authoritative tannins that are arranged in linear fashion. Power with elegance. Try from 2024.

97 Points - Wine Spectator

This is super vivid, offering cassis, blackberry, raspberry and blueberry compote flavors that bristle with energy while a mouthwatering frame of anise and apple wood adds electric energy. This is borderline rambunctious but it's bridled well enough and when the fruit and wood sides mesh fully, this will be a rock star. Best from 2025 through 2040.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast
As so often with this estate, this is a generous, opulent wine. This year a strong tannic element gives the wine a good structure. Smoky, textured and powerful, it needs many years to mature. Do not drink this wine before 2026.
Cellar Selection

glengoyne-legacy-series-chapter-two.title: Glengoyne The Legacy Series Chapter Two
glengoyne-legacy-series-chapter-two.bodyHtml:
Glengoyne The Legacy Series Chapter Two is a Highland single malt Scotch whisky from Glengoyne, the second release in the distillery's Legacy Series, which explores the history, people and place behind the Glengoyne way of making whisky. First released in September 2020, it marries spirit matured in two distinct cask types: first-fill ex-bourbon casks and refill sherry casks. Chapter Two moved the series from a cardboard tube to a box and introduced the new Glengoyne logo. Like Chapter One, it is bottled at 48% ABV, with natural colour from the oak casks; this listing is the 750ml bottle.

Serve: Neat, or with a splash of water.

chateau-palmer-2016.title: Chateau Palmer 2016
chateau-palmer-2016.bodyHtml:
The 2016 vintage is a blend of 47% Merlot, 47% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 6% Petit Verdot. This wine exhibits a deep garnet-purple color and opens with compelling notes of blueberry compote, warm cassis, and kirsch, with emerging hints of violets, cigar box, black tea, sandalwood, and Sichuan pepper. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied, rich, and concentrated, featuring super-ripe, velvety tannins and fantastic freshness, finishing long with floral and earthy sparks.

100 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Powerful tannins and hugely rich fruit balance together in this superb wine. The velvet texture belies the power behind the concentrated, ripe black-fruit flavor, with vibrant acidity giving ample lift. The wine’s structure will ensure aging for many years. Drink from 2024.

98 Points - James Suckling

Such attractive fruit and alluring ripeness that it draws you in from the get-go. The discreet power here is delivered with a very astute touch. Assorted dark-berry aromas, as well as red plums, abound on the nose. The richness and depth in the mouth is stunning. The tannins are super polished and layered and they draw pristine dark fruit flavors deep into the finish in effortless mode. This is a star of the vintage. A blend of 47 per cent merlot, 47 per cent cabernet sauvignon and six per cent petit verdot. Try from 2024.

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2016 Palmer is a blend of 47% Merlot, 47% Cabernet Sauvignon and 6% Petit Verdot. Opaque garnet-purple colored, it slowly glides out of the glass with compelling notes of blueberry compote, warm cassis and kirsch with emerging hints of violets, cigar box, black tea, sandalwood and Sichuan pepper. Medium to full-bodied, wonderfully rich, concentrated and packed with latent energy, the palate literally grows in the mouth, revealing layer upon layer of black, blue and red fruits and tons of floral sparks, framed by super ripe, incredibly fine-grained tannins and finishing with epic length. It’s a wine that makes you wanna drape yourself languidly over a chaise lounge, glass of Palmer in hand, sighing with deep satisfaction, “This is so wonderfully Palmer.”

94 Points - Wine Spectator
This is a very solid rendering, with a core of steeped blackberry, black currant and fig fruit flavors that are juicy and well-defined. The back end picks up lots of graphite, tobacco, anise and violet notes while maintaining focus and energy. Shows latent depth as the fruit echoes steadily. Best from 2023 through 2038.

chateau-haut-brion-grand-cru-classe-2016.title: Chateau Lamothe-Bergeron Cru Bourgeois 2016
chateau-haut-brion-grand-cru-classe-2016.bodyHtml:
Château Lamothe-Bergeron Cru Bourgeois is a classic Haut-Médoc showcasing aromas of blackcurrant, blackberry, cassis, cedar, graphite, tobacco, and toasted oak. Concentrated fruit, polished tannins, lively acidity, and balanced oak deliver a refined, full-bodied wine with remarkable structure, elegance, and excellent aging potential.

Food Pairing: Pair with grilled ribeye, roast lamb, braised beef, duck breast, mushroom risotto, aged Gruyère, or herb-crusted pork tenderloin.

 

91 Points - Wine Enthusiast

The rather grand château of this estate dates to the 19th century, a turreted affair very much in the Médoc tradition. The wine is classic as well, offering balanced acidity, black-currant fruit and a layer of tannins to support everything. The 30% new barrels have added to the wine's richness as well as giving a spicy aftertaste. Drink from 2022. Roger Voss.

91 Points - James Suckling

This has a plush array of fine tannins and delivers an impressively structured palate with assertive and lively tannins, carrying plush and elegant, red-berry flavors in fresh resolve. Try from 2021.

chateau-pavie-2010.title: Chateau La Mission Haut-Brion 2016 1.5L Magnum
chateau-pavie-2010.bodyHtml:
Chateau La Mission Haut Brion is one of Bordeaux's greatest wines, revered for its extraordinary power, elegance, and longevity. Aromas of blackcurrant, blackberry, graphite, cedar, cigar box, violet, and exotic spice unfold into a concentrated palate with velvety tannins, exceptional depth, and a remarkably persistent finish.

Food Pairing: Pair with beef Wellington, roast lamb, venison, duck breast, truffle dishes, or aged Comte for an unforgettable Bordeaux experience.

 

98 Points - Decanter

This is a wonderful wine. It’s absolutely precise, finely wrought and gorgeously balanced between richness and elegance, with notes of damson, black cherry, slate and rosemary. Silky soft tannins highlight the concentration of the fruit and the grilled oak notes that are La Mission’s signature, with a fresh core that stretches out the palate. A low pH gives tension through the palate and is highly seductive. No Cabernet Franc this year.

It’s sexier and more charming compared to the more backward Haut-Brion, yet I suspect it will age just as long.

98 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2016 Château La Mission Haut-Brion is a blend of 57.5% Merlot and 42.5% Cabernet Sauvignon. Deep garnet-purple in color, it is just a little muted to begin, soon unfurling to reveal slowly growing scents of crushed blackcurrants, black cherries, dark chocolate and candied violets with nuances of crushed rocks, tobacco leaf, forest floor and fragrant earth, plus a hint of bergamot. Medium-bodied and exquisitely elegant, the palate offers perfectly ripe, fine-grained tannins and tons of freshness with layer upon layer of perfumed fruit and a very long, ferrous-laced finish.

97 Points - James Suckling

Regal wine, showing alluringly ripe and dark plums that carry a wealth of complexity in their DNA—fine spices, leaves, graphite, violets and more. The palate has very precise drive and a super-focused style, delivering authoritative tannins arranged in linear fashion. Power with elegance. Try from 2024.

97 Points - Wine Spectator
