cava-de-oro-plata.title: Cava de Oro Extra Añejo Tequila
cava-de-oro-plata.bodyHtml:
Cava de Oro Extra Anejo Tequila is an exceptionally rich and decadent sipping tequila produced by Tequilera Puerta de Hierro. Aged for a remarkable five years in French oak barrels that previously held red wine, this expression takes on a profound complexity and a luxurious, dessert-like profile. Its stunning dark amber hue gives way to an incredibly smooth and viscous mouthfeel, making it a favorite among those who appreciate sweeter, barrel-forward spirits reminiscent of fine cognacs or aged rums.

Food Pairing: This rich, sweet tequila is a perfect digestif and pairs flawlessly with decadent desserts like vanilla bean flan, crème brûlée, or dark chocolate truffles. For savory pairings, serve it alongside roasted pork glazed with sweet and spicy sauces, or with a platter of aged gouda and blue cheese.

TASTING NOTES - A remarkably smooth, heavy-bodied tequila with a dark amber color and a viscous, syrupy texture that elegantly coats the glass.

NOSE - Pronounced aromas of sweet vanilla, caramel, maple syrup, toasted French oak, cinnamon, and subtle hints of red berries.

PALATE - Incredibly smooth and sweet on the tongue, bursting with flavors of burnt sugar, maple, vanilla cream, butterscotch, and roasted agave, balanced gently by oak spices.

FINISH - Long, sweet, and velvety smooth, leaving lingering notes of caramel, vanilla, and gentle oak.

SERVE - Best served neat in a snifter, Glencairn glass, or tequila flute at room temperature to fully appreciate its rich qualities.

chateau-lions-de-batailley-2016.title: Château Batailley Lions de Batailley 2016
chateau-lions-de-batailley-2016.bodyHtml:
The Château Batailley Lions de Batailley 2016 is the third vintage of the estate's second wine, representing a selection that typically accounts for roughly 30% of the total production. It is crafted to be more approachable than the Grand Vin while maintaining the classic, structured identity of Pauillac. The 2016 vintage is noted for its concentration and firm tannins, offering a profile of blackberry, tobacco, and characteristic graphite aromas.

93 Points - James Suckling

The blackcurrant and blueberry aromas pop out of the glass. Medium to full body, linear and refined tannins and a currant, coffee and smoke aftertaste. Second wine of Batailley. Try after 2022.

90 Points - Wine Spectator

This takes a relatively gentle and perfumy approach, with slightly high-toned cherry, red currant and damson plum fruit, inlaid with sleek tannins and hints of sandalwood and cedar. Best from 2021 through 2030.

domaine-santa-duc-habemus-papam.title: Domaine Santa Duc Habemus Papam Chateauneuf-du-Pape 2019
domaine-santa-duc-habemus-papam.bodyHtml:
The plots are found at Le Pradel and La Font du Pape, respectively to the east and center of Châteauneuf-du-Pape. Certified Biodynamic, Certified Organic.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Stylish and silky, relying on higher-toned red currant, cherry and raspberry fruit aromas and flavors, with red tea, savory and subtle mineral details throughout. Features a late echo of worn leather, which adds nice contrast on the finish. Grenache and Syrah. Best from 2023.

domaine-santa-duc-aux-lieux-dits.title: Domaine Santa Duc Gigondas Aux Lieux-Dits 2019 750ml
domaine-santa-duc-aux-lieux-dits.bodyHtml:
The Southern Rhône region of Gigondas extends northwest from the notably jagged wall of mountains called the Dentelles di Montmirail, whose highest point climbs to about 2,600 feet. The region and its wines have much in common with the neighboring Chateauneuf-du-Pape except that the vineyards of Gigondas exist at higher elevation and its soils, comprised mainly of crumbled limestone from the Dentelles, often produce a more dense and robust Grenache-based red wine.

The region has a history of fine winemaking, extending back to Roman times. But by the 20th century, Gigondas was merely lumped into the less distinct zone of Côtes du Rhône Villages. However, it was first among these satellite villages to earn its own appellation, which occurred in 1971.

Gigondas reds must be between 50 to 100% Grenache with Syrah and Mourvèdre comprising the bulk of the remainder of the blend. They tend express rustic flavors and aromas of wild blackberry, raspberry, fig, plum, as well as juniper, dried herbs, anise, smoke and river rock. The best are bold but balanced, and finish with impressively sexy and velvety tannins.

The Gigondas appellation also produces rosé but no white wines.

domaine-santa-duc-les-quatre-terres.title: Domaine Santa Duc Cotes Du Rhone Les Quatre Terres 2020 750ml
domaine-santa-duc-les-quatre-terres.bodyHtml: Domaine Santa Duc C™tes Du Rh™ne Les Quatre Terres 2021 750ml

ca-del-baio-barbaresco-autinbej.title: Ca del Baio Autinbej Barbaresco DOCG 2023
ca-del-baio-barbaresco-autinbej.bodyHtml:
Ca' del Baio Autinbej Barbaresco 2023 is an elegant Italian red wine from the prestigious Barbaresco appellation in Piedmont, Italy. Produced by the family-owned Ca' del Baio estate, this wine is crafted entirely from Nebbiolo grapes, showcasing the distinctive character, finesse and winemaking heritage of the Langhe region. Autinbej is known for its expressive floral character, vibrant red fruit and refined structure. This Barbaresco offers an inviting profile of ripe cherries, raspberries, rose petals and violets, complemented by delicate notes of liquorice, dried herbs and subtle spice. On the palate, lively acidity and structured tannins create a harmonious balance, leading to a persistent, elegant finish.

Food Pairing: Braised beef, roasted lamb, duck breast, veal, wild mushroom risotto, truffle pasta, porcini mushrooms, aged Parmigiano Reggiano, Pecorino and traditional Piedmontese dishes.

 

93 Points - James Suckling

Overt and fruity, showing subtle roses and violets, red cherries and pomegranate. A hint of licorice and mint enhances complexity, with layered citrus flavors. Medium-bodied, this has crisp tension and firm, velvety tannins that turn dustier in the polished, chewy finish. Drink or hold.

messias-colheita-port-1964.title: Messias Colheita Port 1964 750ml
messias-colheita-port-1964.bodyHtml:
The 1964 Messias colheita port from the outstanding 1964 vintage has been aged in a barrel until bottling in 2015. The port has a beautiful amber colour with greenish hints indicating that this is a colheita of great age, The aroma has dried fruit and balsamic notes, the palate is intense and well balanced.

The extended barrel aging has given this wine a complex fusion of dried fruit and cedar notes. On the palate the wine is smooth and full bodies with plenty nuts and sweet fruit on the palate, fine balance. A tremendous finish which goes on forever. There's no question about the quality on display here.

mordoree-la-dame-rousse-lirac-rouge-ac.title: Domaine De La Mordoree La Dame Rousse Lirac 2019 750ml
mordoree-la-dame-rousse-lirac-rouge-ac.bodyHtml:
Domaine de la Mordorée 'La Dame Rousse' Lirac 2023 is a vibrant, aromatic, and organically farmed Southern Rhône red wine crafted by the Delorme family in Tavel. Sourced from estate vineyards planted on clay-limestone soils covered with rounded galets roulés stones and silica, this classic blend of Grenache and Syrah is hand-harvested and destemmed before undergoing temperature-controlled fermentation and aging in stainless steel tanks to preserve pure, expressive fruit character. In the glass, it displays a luminous, deep ruby-purple hue. The bouquet opens with lifted aromas of ripe blackberries, wild strawberries, and black cherries layered with Mediterranean garrigue herbs, crushed violets, and subtle black pepper. On the palate, it delivers a medium-to-full body marked by juicy dark fruit, refreshing natural acidity, and supple, fine-grained tannins that carry through to a clean, persistent, and spicy finish.

Food Pairing: Grilled lamb chops, herb-roasted pork tenderloin, braised beef short ribs, ratatouille, or aged Comté and Manchego cheeses.

coppola-directors-cabernet-sauvignon.title: Francis Coppola Director's Cut Sonoma County Cabernet Sauvignon 2023
coppola-directors-cabernet-sauvignon.bodyHtml:
Francis Coppola Director's Cut Sonoma County Cabernet Sauvignon 2023 is a full-bodied, elegantly crafted red wine that brilliantly captures the bold and nuanced character of Sonoma County's renowned Alexander Valley. Pouring a deep, intense ruby hue, the nose is highly aromatic and inviting, revealing rich layers of roasted blackberry, dark plum, and cassis, gracefully intertwined with warm notes of toffee, espresso, cinnamon, and toasted oak. On the palate, it delivers a silky, beautifully textured mouthfeel, offering a robust core of juicy black cherry and dark chocolate flavors. Supported by fine, melting tannins and a bright, refreshing natural acidity, the wine culminates in a smooth, lingering finish framed by subtle hints of cedar and black pepper.

Food Pairing: Pairs flawlessly with robust, savory dishes such as a classic grilled ribeye steak, roasted rack of lamb, hearty venison or game, rich pasta with traditional meat sauce, and firm, mature cheeses.

san-felice-pugnitello.title: San Felice Pugnitello 2022
san-felice-pugnitello.bodyHtml:
San Felice Pugnitello 2022 is an intriguing, deeply colored Italian red wine crafted entirely from Pugnitello, an ancient, rare Tuscan grape variety revived and cultivated by Agricola San Felice. Sourced from estate vineyards in Castelnuovo Berardenga, it offers intense, layered aromatics of dark plum, blackberry, leather, sweet tobacco, and crushed herbs. On the palate, it exhibits a robust, full-bodied structure supported by firm, fine-grained tannins, fresh acidity, and a long, savory, spice-tinged finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with roasted wild boar, grilled Florentine Bistecca, braised beef short ribs, rich game stews, and well-aged Pecorino Toscano cheese.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

Dark and brooding, this is packed with black cherry, blackberry, plum and tar flavors. Surprisingly supple, given its somber character, with refined tannins and a lively, earthy finish. Drink now through 2033.

masi-vaio-armaron-2001.title: Serego Alighieri Vaio Armaron Amarone della Valpolicella Classico 2013
masi-vaio-armaron-2001.bodyHtml:
Opaque ruby red. Intense and elegant, with hints of fruit preserved in spirit, dried plums and cocoa. Well-structured, well-balanced, with silky tannins and a long finish revealing ripe cherries and sweet spices.

Perfect with red meat, game, quails, roasts and full-flavored dishes. Excellent match for mature cheeses with bite, such as Parmesan or Pecorino.

93 Points - James Suckling

A linear, bright Amarone with purple fruit, lavender and sandalwood throughout. It’s full-bodied with a tight, integrated palate. Fine and pretty

92 Points - Wine Spectator

An elegant, medium- to full-bodied red, fresh and well-knit, offering an appealing, satiny texture and a pure beam of dried cherry flavors, with hints of red licorice, ground espresso and rich, loamy earth. Delicate notes of exotic spice, saffron and mineral play on the finish. Drink now through 2028. Tasted twice, with consistent notes.

92 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

From a historic estate that was a residence of the family of Italy's language and literary genius Dante Alighieri, the Masi Serego Alighieri 2013 Amarone della Valpolicella Classico Vaio Armaron is a generous and hearty wine. The bouquet is quite opulent, although there is a note of worn leather or cured meat that you notice straight off. This points to the more evolved state of this cooler vintage with fruit picked eight years ago. Those warm savory tones segue to baked fruit and dried blackberry. The wine finishes long with hints of sweetness and smoky spice. The overall effect is one of intensity and boldness. The wine is great now, but I'm concerned that those leathery and animal notes could worsen with time. I have shortened the drinking window as a result.

shift-red-blend.title: Ridge Lytton Springs Red Blend 2022
shift-red-blend.bodyHtml:
Ridge Lytton Springs Red Blend 2022 is an iconic, full-bodied heritage field blend crafted by Ridge Vineyards from old-vine plantings in Sonoma County's Dry Creek Valley. Marking its 50th anniversary release, this wine is fermented on native yeasts and aged in 100% American oak barrels. In the glass, it yields an intense ruby color with vibrant aromas of boysenberry, wild blackberry, purple flowers, cigar box, and sage. The palate is rich, seamless, and finely structured, offering flavors of dark plum, black cherry, dark chocolate, licorice, and black pepper supported by supple, powdery tannins and lively acidity that extend into a long, persistent finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with slow-cooked lamb stew, barbecued pork ribs, grilled ribeye steak, braised beef short ribs, and sharp aged cheddar cheese.

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

The densely packed nose of this legendary old vine field blend of Zin, Petite Sirah, Carignane, and Alicante gives aromas of crushed blackberry, purple flowers and rich earthy spices, while the palate brings black cherry, olive and licorice flavors in a framework of opulent tannin that will age effortlessly for more than a decade.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

The densely packed nose of this legendary old-vine field blend of Zin, Petite Sirah, Carignan and Alicante gives aromas of crushed blackberry, purple flowers and rich earthy spices. The palate brings black cherry, olive and licorice flavors in a framework of opulent tannin that will age effortlessly for more than a decade.

95 Points - James Suckling

This is the kingpin of Ridge’s Sonoma County heritage blends and it doesn’t disappoint. Equal parts fruity, spicy and savory on a full body braced by moderate tannins. Judicious oak spices like cedar and cigar box complement pure, ripe blackberries and raspberries and a dash of black pepper. Known to age well for decades.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

Like a beast that's been tamed, this red is genteel and polished on the outside but dark and fervent deep down, with expressive flavors of blackberry, briar patch, savory anise and pepper. Zinfandel, Petite Sirah, Carignane and Alicante Bouschet.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2022 Lytton Springs 50th Anniversary is composed of 67% Zinfandel, 19% Petite Sirah, 11% Carignane and 3% Alicante Bouschet. It opens with initial touches of glossy new American oak—dill and toasted coconut—and gives way to kaleidoscopic black and red plums, cherries and berries, plus accents of hibiscus and potpourri. The full-bodied palate features generous, spicy flavors. It’s structured by abundant, powdery tannins and lively acidity and has a long, detailed finish. Winemaker Shauna Rosenblum says this 2022 was crafted using only American oak, a shift from the blend of French and American oak used in the past. It has resulted in a particularly pure, transparent expression that opens dramatically with air, and this 2022 Lytton Springs will benefit from several years in the cellar.

perano-rialzi-chi-clas-gr-selezione.title: Frescobaldi Tenuta Perano Chianti Classico Rialzi Gran Selezione 2016 750ml
perano-rialzi-chi-clas-gr-selezione.bodyHtml:
Bright ruby colour with a delicate garnet rim. Subdued yet precise nose of masterfully carved out notes of raspberry and black cherry, inviting. Extremely juicy, bags of crunchy cherry, supported by finely-knit tannin, lingering for quite some time.

91 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Mature dark-skinned fruit, French oak, coconut and blue-flower aromas are front and center on this 100% Sangiovese. On the linear palate, vanilla, espresso and licorice notes accent a core of black cherry and blackberry extract. Assertive, close-grained tannins provide the framework. It's still very much on its oak and needs time to fully integrate. Drink 2024–2031.

cote-rotie-chateau-de-montlys-2014.title: Christophe Semaska Chateau De Montlys Cote-Rotie 2014
cote-rotie-chateau-de-montlys-2014.bodyHtml:
The cultivation of vines here began with Greek settlers who arrived in 600 BC. Its proximity to Vienne was important then and also when that city became a Roman settlement but its situation, far from the negociants of Tain, led to its decline in more modern history. However the 1990s brought with it a revival fueled by one producer, Marcel Guigal, who believed in the zone’s potential. He, along with the critic, Robert Parker, are said to be responsible for the zone’s later 20th century renaissance.

Where the Rhone River turns, there is a build up of schist rock and a remarkable angle that produces slopes to maximize the rays of the sun. Cote Rotie remains one of the steepest in viticultural France. Its varied slopes have two designations. Some are dedicated as Côte Blonde and others as Côte Brune. Syrahs coming from Côte Blonde are lighter, more floral, and ready for earlier consumption—they can also include up to 20% of the highly scented Viognier. Those from Côte Brune are more sturdy, age-worthy and are typically nearly 100% Syrah. Either way, a Cote Rotie is going to have a particularly haunting and savory perfume, expressing a more feminine side of the northern Rhone.

cote-rotie-fleur-de-montlys-2013.title: Christophe Semaska La Fleur De Montlys Cote-Rotie 2013
cote-rotie-fleur-de-montlys-2013.bodyHtml:

paolo-conterno-anforti-toscana-igt.title: Paolo Conterno Anforti 2020
paolo-conterno-anforti-toscana-igt.bodyHtml:
Paolo Conterno "Anforti" Toscana 2020 is a bold, velvety Super Tuscan blend crafted by a renowned Barolo producer from high-altitude vines just north of Florence. Marrying the plushness of Merlot with the rustic edge of Sangiovese, it delivers an intense, concentrated profile that beautifully captures the warmth of the 2020 vintage. In the glass, it pours a deep ruby-red color with purple reflections. The nose is highly expressive, opening with aromas of sour cherries, dark wild berries, and dried violets, layered with notes of vanilla and sweet baking spice. On the palate, it is full-bodied and robust, showing a smooth, fleshy texture filled with flavors of plum and smoked pepper. This rich fruit profile is balanced by firm, chewy tannins and a fresh line of acidity that leads into a long, earthy finish.

Food Pairing: Grilled ribeye steak, slow-braised wild boar ragù, roasted duck, or rich pasta dishes with savory meat sauces.

garzon-balasto.title: Bodega Garzon Balasto 2020 750ml
garzon-balasto.bodyHtml:
Garzón Balasto is a richly spiced wine with aromas of fresh red and black fruit, licorice, graphite, and a hint of tobacco. The palate is vibrant and full-bodied, with juicy tannins and subtle minerality that give way to a long, textural finish.

Garzón Balasto, with its robust character and rich flavors, is an ideal companion for a variety of dishes. It pairs beautifully with grilled meat, juicy roasts, and rich stews.

Blend: 42% Tannat, 39% Cabernet Franc, 19% Petit Verdot

Professional Ratings

  • 96 Points James Suckling
    The aromatics are impressive, with orange blossoms, sliced oranges and black fruit. Hints of tar with some minerals, fresh spices and chiles. Medium-bodied with very fine tannins that run the length of the wine. They are polished and curated. Chewy at the end but there’s a finesse, tension and focus. 42% tannat, 39% cabernet franc and 19% petit verdot. Drinkable now, but better from 2027.
  • 94 Points Wine & Spirits
    Garzón’s granite formed before Pangaea started to break apart 200 million years ago: Managing Director Christian Wiley says geologists trace the soil back 2.5 billion years, and that no vines arrived to feed on that soil until 2008, when Alejandro Bulgheroni decided to plant vineyards rather than a windfarm near Pueblo Garzón. “In the past, people just fished and worked with cows,” says Wiley, who oversees this vast project for the Argentine billionaire. The winegrowing team, headed up by Germán Bruzzone (from an Uruguayan winegrowing family) and lead consultant Alberto Antonini, had to train the local workers in viticulture, and have planted 625 acres of vines since the project began. Balasto, named for the clay-free granite in which those vines grow, is the team’s most ambitious wine. For this taster, the 2020 is the year they got it right. A blend of 42 percent tannat, 39 percent cabernet franc and 19 percent petit verdot, this fermented in 8,000-liter cement tulips then aged in untoasted French oak barrels. The wine achieves a complex dynamic between oak tannins and musky dark cherry fruit, all the while holding to its cool, oceanic provenance. Both luscious and fresh, this is an elegant wine at the beginning of its life. It will be fascinating to open the 2020 in 2030 and 2040, to find out where its power and dynamism will lead.
  • 90 Points Wine Spectator
    Opens with subtle leather, spice and graphite notes, offering good density to the plum and brambly berry flavors. Picks up spiced chocolate notes on the finish, where there is a firm grip of tannins, so patience is required. Tannat, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot. Best from 2025 through 2033.

meg-malbec-cabernet-sauvignon.title: Vasse Felix Tom Cullity Cabernet Sauvignon Malbec
meg-malbec-cabernet-sauvignon.bodyHtml:
Refined and deeply expressive, with cassis, blackberry and red fruits layered with violets, savoury herbs, graphite and earthy complexity. The palate combines concentrated fruit with freshness, exceptionally fine tannins and elegant structure, carrying into a persistent, poised finish.

Food Pairing: Pair with roast lamb, grilled beef, venison, braised short ribs, wild mushrooms, aged cheddar, or herb-crusted meats.

chat-santenay-mercurey-vieilles-vignes.title: Philippe Le Hardi Mercurey Vieilles Vignes Rouge 2023
chat-santenay-mercurey-vieilles-vignes.bodyHtml:
Philippe Le Hardi Mercurey Vieilles Vignes Rouge 2023 is an elegant French red wine from the prestigious Mercurey appellation in Burgundy's Côte Chalonnaise region. Produced by Domaine du Château Philippe le Hardi, this wine is crafted from Pinot Noir grapes grown on mature vines, showcasing the distinctive character, finesse and complexity of traditional Burgundian winemaking. The 2023 vintage offers expressive aromas of ripe red cherries, raspberries, wild strawberries and redcurrants, complemented by delicate floral notes, subtle earthy undertones and gentle spice. On the palate, the wine is refined and beautifully balanced, featuring juicy red fruit, fresh acidity, silky tannins and a touch of mineral complexity. Its elegant structure and lingering finish make it an excellent choice for Burgundy enthusiasts and those seeking a sophisticated, food-friendly Pinot Noir.

Food Pairing: Roasted duck breast, herb-crusted lamb, grilled chicken, pork tenderloin, beef bourguignon, mushroom risotto, truffle pasta, roasted vegetables, Brie, Camembert and Comté cheese.

chat-santenay-meursault.title: Domaine Marquis d'Angerville Meursault-Santenots 2015 750ml
chat-santenay-meursault.bodyHtml:
A rare white Burgundy from a domaine best known for its reds, the 2015 Meursault Santenots 1er Cru is a powerful yet refined expression of Chardonnay. Grown in the prestigious Santenots vineyard, this wine opens with elegant aromas of ripe citrus, white flowers, and toasted almonds, underpinned by subtle hints of oak and mineral. On the palate, it is full-bodied and richly textured, delivering layers of stone fruit, lemon curd, and delicate spice, balanced by a vibrant acidity and a long, focused finish.

This vintage showcases remarkable depth and aging potential, making it a standout for collectors and enthusiasts alike. Best enjoyed with lobster, roasted poultry, or creamy mushroom risotto.

chat-santenay-pommard-petit-clos.title: Chateau De Santenay Petit Clos Monopole Pommard 2017 750ml
chat-santenay-pommard-petit-clos.bodyHtml:
Representing some of the darkest, deepest and sturdiest Pinot Noir of Burgundy, Pommard is one of the two villages in Côte de Beaune—along with Volnay—that is recognized for its impressive Pinot Noir. While it can’t boast any Grands Crus vineyards, its extraordinary Premiers Crus vineyards are aplenty.

Les Pézerolles, Les Épenots, Clos des Épeneaux, Les Chanlins, Les Jarolières, Les Fremiers and particularly Les Rugiens are among the most outstanding Premiers Crus.

The best Pommards will be concentrated in flavors such as black cherry, blackberry and dark chocolate, have dazzling aromas of violets, menthol or wild herbs and a firm and powerful finish. They typically demand some time in the bottle to reach their peak.

boschendal-elgin-pinot-noir.title: Boschendal Appellation Series Elgin Pinot Noir 2018
boschendal-elgin-pinot-noir.bodyHtml:
Boschendal Appellation Series Elgin Pinot Noir 2018 is an elegant South African red wine from the cool-climate Elgin region of the Western Cape. Crafted from carefully selected Pinot Noir grapes, this refined wine showcases vibrant red fruit flavours, delicate floral aromas, and subtle earthy undertones. Its silky texture, balanced acidity, and gentle tannins create a sophisticated drinking experience, making it an excellent choice for special occasions, fine dining, or enjoying with a beautifully prepared meal.

Food Pairing: Perfectly complements roasted duck, grilled salmon, mushroom risotto, herb-roasted chicken, pork tenderloin, and soft cheeses such as Brie and Camembert.

karrawatta-christos-paddock-cabernet.title: Josh Cellars Cabernet Sauvignon 2022
karrawatta-christos-paddock-cabernet.bodyHtml:
Josh Cellars Cabernet Sauvignon 2022 is an incredibly round, juicy, and highly approachable Californian red wine crafted as a comforting tribute by founder Joseph Carr in honor of his father. Sourced from premier vineyards across California's diverse growing regions, this vintage highlights the approachable and expressive potential of the state's signature red grape. In the glass, it pours a deep, rich dark ruby hue with a full coating rim. The forward and incredibly aromatic nose opens with inviting scents of ripe blackberry, dark cherry, and black currant, masterfully integrated with subtle undertones of toasted hazelnut, cinnamon, warm vanilla, and sweet toasted oak. On the palate, the wine is medium-to-full-bodied and beautifully balanced, displaying a soft, velvety fluid coherence where its core of juicy dark forest fruit effortlessly intertwines with fine-grained, round tannins and a moderate spine of natural acidity, concluding with a long, smooth finish accented by lingering hints of mocha and subtle wood spice.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with charcoal-grilled gourmet beef burgers, slow-braised pork short ribs, rosemary-infused roasted lamb chops, and a block of mature sharp cheddar cheese.

90 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Aromas are notes of ripe dark berries, coriander, sage, florals, and toasty oak on the nose. The flavors are Blackberries, boysenberries, vanilla cream, nutmeg, and mocha with silky tannins on the finish.

louis-latour-volnay-en-chevret-2017.title: Louis Latour Volnay 1er Cru En Chevret 2017
louis-latour-volnay-en-chevret-2017.bodyHtml:
Louis Latour Volnay 1er Cru En Chevret 2017 is an elegant Premier Cru Pinot Noir from Burgundy's prestigious Côte de Beaune. Sourced from the east-facing En Chevret vineyard in Volnay, this refined wine is matured for 10–12 months in French oak barrels, including 35% new oak. Delicate aromas of ripe cherries, wild berries, violets, and subtle spice lead into a beautifully structured palate with silky tannins and vibrant acidity. Its graceful balance of fruit, minerality, and oak showcases the finesse of this distinguished Burgundy vineyard.

Food Pairing: Roasted duck, veal with morel mushrooms, beef Bourguignon, game birds, mushroom risotto, aged Comté, and herb-roasted lamb.

bourdy-savagnin.title: Jean Bourdy Savagnin Cotes Du Jura 2014 750ml
bourdy-savagnin.bodyHtml:
Cotes du Jura is regional appellation of the Jura wine region of eastern France. Introduced in 1937, it is easily the region's largest appellation in terms of geographical scope. Quantitatively, it is the second most important after Arbois.

From the white blended wines of the northern Rhône to the Torrontés wines made in Argentina's high-altitude vineyards, this is a broad group of often very complex wines.
  
The Alsace region is particularly associated with this style. White wines from most varieties grown here are often richly textured and aromatic, with Gewurztraminer slightly ahead of Pinot Gris and Riesling.

Characteristics

  • Flowers, perfume, spice
  • Honey, oiliness
  • Aromas and tastes of table grapes (especially Muscat family)

chateau-pavie-decesse-2016.title: Chateau Pavie-Decesse 2016 750ml
chateau-pavie-decesse-2016.bodyHtml:
Marked by its historic fortified village—perhaps the prettiest in all of Bordeaux, the St-Émilion appellation, along with its neighboring village of Pomerol, are leaders in quality on the Right Bank of Bordeaux. These Merlot-dominant red wines (complemented by various amounts of Cabernet Franc and/or Cabernet Sauvignon) remain some of the most admired and collected wines of the world.

St-Émilion has the longest history in wine production in Bordeaux—longer than the Left Bank—dating back to an 8th century monk named Saint Émilion who became a hermit in one of the many limestone caves scattered throughout the area.

Today St-Émilion is made up of hundreds of independent farmers dedicated to the same thing: growing Merlot and Cabernet Franc (and tiny amounts of Cabernet Sauvignon). While always roughly the same blend, the wines of St-Émilion vary considerably depending on the soil upon which they are grown—and the soils do vary considerably throughout the region.

The chateaux with the highest classification (Premier Grand Cru Classés) are on gravel-rich soils or steep, clay-limestone hillsides. There are only four given the highest rank, called Premier Grand Cru Classés A (Chateau Cheval Blanc, Ausone, Angélus, Pavie) and 14 are Premier Grand Cru Classés B. Much of the rest of the vineyards in the appellation are on flatter land where the soils are a mix of gravel, sand and alluvial matter.

Great wines from St-Émilion will be deep in color, and might have characteristics of blackberry liqueur, black raspberry, licorice, chocolate, grilled meat, earth or truffles. They will be bold, layered and lush.

Prior to the 2022 vintage, this wine was classed as Grand Cru Classe.

Critic tasting note: (2016 vintage) "Opulent, rich, ripe and already allowing some of its floral, licorice, dark cherry and smoky plums to poke through, the wine is full-bodied, concentrated and will request 7-8 years in the cellar, or more, before its fully developed. 94 Points" - 94/100, Jeff Leve, The Wine Cellar Insider

les-pagodes-de-cos-2016.title: Chateau Cos d'Estournel Les Pagodes de Cos 2016
les-pagodes-de-cos-2016.bodyHtml:
Château Cos d'Estournel Les Pagodes de Cos 2016 is an elegant Bordeaux red blend from the prestigious Saint-Estèphe appellation on Bordeaux's Left Bank. Produced as the second wine of Château Cos d'Estournel, this exceptional 2016 vintage combines Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Petit Verdot, and Cabernet Franc. Rich blackcurrant, ripe plum, cedar, and subtle spice complement its silky tannins and vibrant acidity. Beautifully balanced and refined, it offers an approachable expression of the estate's celebrated winemaking style, with excellent ageing potential.

Food Pairing: Roasted lamb, grilled ribeye steak, braised short ribs, duck breast, venison, mushroom risotto, and aged cheeses.

 

94 Points - James Suckling

A red with very deep and intense fruit character, yet rich tannins to back it all up. Full-bodied, layered and powerful. The second wine of Cos d’Estournel is serious again in 2016. Try from 2025.

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Dense and full of dark fruits, this second wine from Cos d’Estournel comes from specific parcels. With blackberry fruits and rich, generous tannins, the wine has weight and concentration. The freshness at the end is so typical of the vintage. Drink from 2023.


92 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate
The 2016 Les Pagodes de Cos is blended of 50% Cabernet Sauvignon, 46.5% Merlot, 3% Petit Verdot and 0.5% Cabernet Franc. It has a deep garnet-purple color and opens with notions of warm cassis, black cherries and smoked meats giving way to scents of charcoal, underbrush and cloves plus a waft of new leather. Medium to full-bodied, it fills the palate with generous black fruits and some compelling red fruit sparks, supported by ripe, grainy tannins and finishing long and spicy.

91 Points - Wine Spectator
This has good energy, with a light briar note through the mix of raspberry, plum and cherry paste flavors. Subtle chalk and iron streaks add texture and cut on the finish. Best from 2021 through 2031.

chateau-langoa-barton-2016.title: Chateau Langoa Barton 2016
chateau-langoa-barton-2016.bodyHtml:
An icon of balance and tradition, St. Julien boasts the highest proportion of classed growths in the Médoc. What it lacks in any first growths, it makes up in the rest: five amazing second growth chateaux, two superb third growths and four well-reputed fourth growths. While the actual class rankings set in 1855 (first, second, and so on the fifth) today do not necessarily indicate a score of quality, the classification system is important to understand in the context of Bordeaux history. Today rivalry among the classed chateaux only serves to elevate the appellation overall.

96 Points - James Suckling

Beautiful aromas of flowers and berries, intermingled in fresh and brambly mode with a cedary edge. This is very fresh. The tannins carve an exceptionally deep, long line through the dark berries and cassis and deliver a very powerful, unwavering finish. This is in great form. Very powerful and focused. Try from 2024.

95 Points - Wine Spectator

Sappy and dense, with kirsch, plum reduction, mulled açai berry and warmed fig fruit showing impressive range, while licorice snap, ganache and roasted apple wood notes jostle behind them. Mouthwatering acidity should give this plenty of time to round into form. Best from 2025 through 2040..

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Big and packed with spice and smokiness, this wine is full of rich black fruits and juicy acidity. Wood aging adds a light touch of toastiness at this stage but will integrate to give a ripe wine ready to drink from 2024.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2016 Langoa Barton is medium to deep garnet-purple colored and opens with cedar, red and black currants, kirsch and menthol with smoked meats. The palate is medium to full-bodied, firm, grainy and packed with youthful, energetic fruit, finishing long and perfumed.

chateau-du-tertre-2016.title: Chateau Du Tertre 2016 750ml
chateau-du-tertre-2016.bodyHtml:
Fifth Growth. Cinquieme Grand Cru Classe in 1855.

Critic tasting note: (2016 vintage) "Flowers, spicy red berries and forest notes are in your glass as soon as the wine hits the glass. Medium bodied, elegant, fresh and dynamic, the wine is silky, sweet, juicy and pure from start to finish. 92 Points" - 92/100, Jeff Leve, The Wine Cellar Insider.

Producer Notes
The Château du Tertre dominates the vineyard, which enjoys a superb position, lying unbroken over 52 hectares. Cabernet Sauvignon is the major grape variety, endowing the wine with structure and concentration. Renowned for its roundness and suppleness, Merlot brings its silkiness to the final blending. Cabernet Franc lends its distinctive, rich bouquet of spicy notes. Later to mature, the Petit Verdot completes this range of aromas. Thus is born the Château du Tertre Grand Vin, reflecting the very soul of this exceptional terroir.

Vineyard Notes

The Margaux terroirs are there highest, with one of the most elevated gravel outcrops of the Médoc. The light and the sunshine wich bathe the vines protect them from the late spring frosts. A stream provides natural drainage, separating the two gravels outcrops, and cools the vines, thus giving them the cooler temperatures vital for thier development, protecting them both from excess water and drought.

Harvest Notes

Harvest: Hand-picked followed by hand sorting – Optical sorting

Winemaking

Tanks: Concrete, wood and stainless steel. Temperature management: Thermoregulation Pumping over: varies according to the lots. Temperature during the alcoholic fermentation: 25°C. Vatting time: 18 to 28 days Pressing: horizontal pneumatic Selection : plot by plot management according to the ages of the vines and the different terroirs.

Ageing

Type of barrels: 100 % French oak barrels(fine grain and medium toast) Age of barrels: 45% new oak , 55% oak of 1 wine. Ageing time: 15 to 17 months. Racking: Every 5 months with candle. Fining: Egg white albumen.

chateau-la-tour-blanche-2016.title: Chateau La Tour Blanche 2016
chateau-la-tour-blanche-2016.bodyHtml:
Château La Tour Blanche 2016 is a prestigious Premier Cru Classé Sauternes from Bordeaux, France. Crafted from botrytis-affected Sémillon, Sauvignon Blanc, and Muscadelle grapes, this luxurious dessert wine offers concentrated flavours of dried apricot, candied citrus, honey, and toasted nuts. Aged in new oak barrels, it combines luscious sweetness with vibrant acidity and an exceptionally elegant finish.

Food Pairing: Foie gras, Roquefort cheese, roasted poultry, lobster, spicy Asian cuisine, apricot tart, crème brûlée, and fruit-based desserts.

 

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Pale lemon-gold colored, the 2016 la Tour Blanche gives flamboyant tropical layers of mango, guava and passion fruit with hints of clover honey, beeswax, nutmeg, jasmine and preserved ginger. Big, rich, concentrated and seductively oily in the mouth, the palate is unashamedly decadent, and it finishes very long and spicy.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Barrel Sample. Structured and concentrated, this is a rich wine that is also fruity and packed with botrytis and acidity. Its texture and tangy edge are impressive and will certainly allow it to age.

93 Points - James Suckling

A slew of dried mangoes and candied citrus, a full, succulent body and a long, clean finish, give this Sauternes plenty of appeal.

91 Points - Wine Spectator

Soft and forward, with a mix of creamed peach, mango, apricot and orange cream flavors gliding through, backed by a honeyed finish.

chateau-la-tour-carnet-2016.title: Chateau La Tour Blanche 2016
chateau-la-tour-carnet-2016.bodyHtml:
Château La Tour Blanche 2016 is a prestigious Premier Cru Classé Sauternes from Bordeaux, France. chateau-villemaurine-2016.title: Chateau Villemaurine 2016 750ml
chateau-villemaurine-2016.bodyHtml:
"Not to be confused with the top-ranked Saint-Émilion Grand Cru Classé wines, Saint-Émilion Grand Cru is an overly employed status in the well-regareded Bordeaux region."
  
Saint-Émilion Grand Cru wines are produced under slightly tighter production restrictions than regular Saint-Émilion wines. As with other grand cru appellations, the intention behind this is to improve the quality, and to distinguish the area's finer wines from the more everyday wines.

This is not quite as straightforward in Saint-Émilion as it is elsewhere, however.

Characteristics

  • Earth
  • Bell Pepper
  • Tobacco
  • Cassis
  • Cedar
  • Structure

Cabernet Franc - Merlot Wine

The Merlot-Cabernet Franc duet is an established and important variant on the classic red Bordeaux blend, particularly on the Right Bank. It is used in the prestigious and Saint-Émilion and Pomerol appellations, and is behind some very high-profile wines.

Merlot is usually used in higher proportions in this blend, thanks (in part) to its broad appeal and higher profile than Cabernet Franc. It provides most of the fruit component, offering up flavors of mulberries, plum and dark berries.

Perhaps more fundamentally, Merlot is well suited to the clay of the Right Bank, and (pre-global warming, at least) a more reliable ripener.

Cabernet Franc adds more perfumed fragrances, usually with a distinctive herbal note. Used in higher proportions, it may also add some tobacco-leaf and green bell pepper characteristics.

Among Cabernet Franc-dominant blends, Château Cheval Blanc is by far the best known.

The combination has long been an institution on the Right Bank, but the wide spread of these two varieties has seen experimentation from several corners of the winegrowing world. In the US, some top wines are made from Merlot and Cabernet Franc (often with the addition of Cabernet Sauvignon) in California, Washington and New York. The blend is also made in Tuscany and Puglia in Italy.

In the southern hemisphere, Merlot - Cabernet Franc blends are popular in regions that have developed reputations for producing quality Bordeaux-style wines. Examples include South Africa's Stellenbosch region and Hawke's Bay in New Zealand.

Best food pairings for Merlot - Cabernet Franc wines include:

  • Braised lamb with truffles
  • Roasted wild boar
  • Steak with red wine sauce

couvent-des-jacobins-2016.title: Couvent des Jacobins Grand Cru Classe 2016 750ml
couvent-des-jacobins-2016.bodyHtml:
St-Émilion Wine
Bordeaux, France

Marked by its historic fortified village—perhaps the prettiest in all of Bordeaux, the St-Émilion appellation, along with its neighboring village of Pomerol, are leaders in quality on the Right Bank of Bordeaux. These Merlot-dominant red wines (complemented by various amounts of Cabernet Franc and/or Cabernet Sauvignon) remain some of the most admired and collected wines of the world.

St-Émilion has the longest history in wine production in Bordeaux—longer than the Left Bank—dating back to an 8th century monk named Saint Émilion who became a hermit in one of the many limestone caves scattered throughout the area.

Today St-Émilion is made up of hundreds of independent farmers dedicated to the same thing: growing Merlot and Cabernet Franc (and tiny amounts of Cabernet Sauvignon). While always roughly the same blend, the wines of St-Émilion vary considerably depending on the soil upon which they are grown—and the soils do vary considerably throughout the region.

The chateaux with the highest classification (Premier Grand Cru Classés) are on gravel-rich soils or steep, clay-limestone hillsides. There are only four given the highest rank, called Premier Grand Cru Classés A (Chateau Cheval Blanc, Ausone, Angélus, Pavie) and 14 are Premier Grand Cru Classés B. Much of the rest of the vineyards in the appellation are on flatter land where the soils are a mix of gravel, sand and alluvial matter.

Great wines from St-Émilion will be deep in color, and might have characteristics of blackberry liqueur, black raspberry, licorice, chocolate, grilled meat, earth or truffles. They will be bold, layered and lush.

Bordeaux Blends
One of the world’s most classic and popular styles of red wine, Bordeaux-inspired blends have spread from their homeland in France to nearly every corner of the New World. Typically based on either Cabernet Sauvignon or Merlot and supported by Cabernet Franc, Malbec and Petit Verdot, the best of these are densely hued, fragrant, full of fruit and boast a structure that begs for cellar time. Somm Secret—Blends from Bordeaux are generally earthier compared to those from the New World, which tend to be fruit-dominant.

Harvest Notes
Hand harvests in cagettes with double sorting; Merlots were harvested between 11 September and 18 September, Cabernets Francs on September 23 and the Petits-Verdots on September 23.

Winemaking
Parcel-specific vinification; pre-fermentation maceration of 2-5 days at 8°C-12°C; temperature-controlled macerations of 20 to 25 days; moderate extraction following regular tasting; vinification without added SO2.

Ageing
12 to 15 months ageing, with 45% new barrels, 55% barrels of 1 wine.

croix-de-beaucaillou-2016.title: La Croix Ducru-Beaucaillou 2016
croix-de-beaucaillou-2016.bodyHtml:
Deep garnet in colour, the 2016 La Croix Ducru Beaucaillou opens with a seductive bouquet of blackcurrant, crushed violets, and dark plum, interwoven with graphite, cedar, and subtle vanilla spice from new oak ageing. On the palate, it delivers richness and refinement in equal measure—full-bodied yet impeccably structured, with layers of ripe blackberry, cassis, and mocha supported by firm but polished tannins. The finish is long, savoury, and mineral-driven, showcasing Saint-Julien's hallmark finesse.

92 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Complex aromas of dark berries, sweet spices, licorice, cigar wrapper and loamy soil introduce the 2021 La Croix de Beaucaillou, a medium to full-bodied, seamless and layered wine that exhibits promising depth, concentration and structure in this challenging vintage. It's a blend of 64% Cabernet Sauvignon, 32% Merlot and 4% Petit Verdot—in other words, it contains at lot more Cabernet than usual.

les-pagodes-de-cos-2017.title: Chateau Cos d'Estournel Pagodes de Cos 2020
les-pagodes-de-cos-2017.bodyHtml:
Les Pagodes de Cos is the second wine of Chateau Cos d'Estournel, offering a refined and approachable expression of Saint-Estephe. It presents aromas of blackcurrant, plum, spice, and cedar, with a structured palate supported by firm tannins and fresh acidity. Elegant yet powerful, it reflects the character of the grand vin while being more accessible in its youth.

Food Pairing: Pairs well with grilled meats, lamb, duck, and aged cheeses.

 

94 Points - James Suckling

Refined and polished with silky tannins. Medium-bodied with savory notes of tobacco, berry and currant. Balanced and already showing approachability.

92 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Complex and structured while maintaining openness and early drinkability. Balanced with good aging potential and smooth development ahead.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

Shows anise and black tea nuances over lush berry fruit. Open-knit and approachable with a smooth, mid-term drinking profile.

aldegheri-amorone-della-valpolicella.title: Aldegheri Santambrogio Amarone della Valpolicella Classico 2018 750ml
aldegheri-amorone-della-valpolicella.bodyHtml:
Since 1956 this family business has been run by the same family. Seven family members are currently working in this special wine domain. They make a wide range of wines of which the Aldegheri Amarone della Valpolicella Classico ‘Santambroggio’ DOCG 2016 is one of the absolute toppers. With respect for old traditions, excellent balanced wines are produced in a modern way. Northwest of the beautiful city of Verona in the hills above Sant’Ambroggio in the heart of the Valpolicella Classico are the vineyards. The vineyards are on average 20 years old (running up to 35 years) and the vines are on a thin calcareous soil. This Italian powerful red wine is produced according to the traditional method. After the alcoholic fermentation, the young wine matures for about 24 months in large Slovenian oak barrels, followed by a barrel aging of 12 months on French oak barriques with a final bottle aging of 8 months.

Deep garnet red color with a robust, full, warm scent reminiscent of black cherries, licorice, leather and wood.

With its heady accent of cherries and a touch of licorice, this is the king of gamey foods cooked in sauces. Serve with venison, game meats or aged cheeses. 

91 Points - Falstaff

Dark, baroque ruby red. On the nose there are notes of dried fig, dark chocolate, overripe blood orange, milk chocolate, oak. On the palate it is fruit-driven, with some juiciness, nice drive, then minimally loosely knit on the finish, old school.

aldegheri-amarone-valpolicella-classico.title: Aldegheri Santambrogio Amarone della Valpolicella Classico 2018 750ml
aldegheri-amarone-valpolicella-classico.bodyHtml:
Since 1956 this family business has been run by the same family. Seven family members are currently working in this special wine domain. They make a wide range of wines of which the Aldegheri Amarone della Valpolicella Classico ‘Santambroggio’ DOCG 2016 is one of the absolute toppers. With respect for old traditions, excellent balanced wines are produced in a modern way. Northwest of the beautiful city of Verona in the hills above Sant’Ambroggio in the heart of the Valpolicella Classico are the vineyards. The vineyards are on average 20 years old (running up to 35 years) and the vines are on a thin calcareous soil. This Italian powerful red wine is produced according to the traditional method. After the alcoholic fermentation, the young wine matures for about 24 months in large Slovenian oak barrels, followed by a barrel aging of 12 months on French oak barriques with a final bottle aging of 8 months.

Deep garnet red color with a robust, full, warm scent reminiscent of black cherries, licorice, leather and wood.

With its heady accent of cherries and a touch of licorice, this is the king of gamey foods cooked in sauces. Serve with venison, game meats or aged cheeses. 

91 Points - Falstaff

Dark, baroque ruby red. On the nose there are notes of dried fig, dark chocolate, overripe blood orange, milk chocolate, oak. On the palate it is fruit-driven, with some juiciness, nice drive, then minimally loosely knit on the finish, old school.

beaune-1er-cru-boucherottes.title: Armand Heitz Beaune Premier Cru
beaune-1er-cru-boucherottes.bodyHtml: A refined and expressive Pinot Noir, combining freshness and complexity. A harmonious Beaune 1er Cru red, from Domaine Armand Heitz, ideal for fine dining and aging. The 2021 Beaune 1er Cru red from Domaine Armand Heitz is an elegant and balanced wine, combining intense fruit, freshness, and floral finesse. An approachable and refined Premier Cru, representative of the Côte de Beaune.

chateau-franc-maillet-pomerol.title: Chateau Franc-Maillet 2020
chateau-franc-maillet-pomerol.bodyHtml:
Château Franc-Maillet 2020 is an incredibly elegant, expressive, and classically styled right-bank Bordeaux red wine that beautifully captures the depth and concentration of an exceptional vintage. Sourced from carefully tended vineyards on the iron-rich clay and gravelly soils of the legendary Pomerol plateau, this blend is dominated by ancient Merlot vines with a small balance of Cabernet Franc. In the glass, it reveals a deep ruby core with purple flashes at the rim. The highly expressive nose opens with enticing aromas of ripe wild strawberries, fresh spearmint, and dark cherries, complexly layered with underlying hints of crushed violets, forest floor, and a kiss of sweet vanilla oak. On the palate, the wine is forward, supple, and medium-to-full-bodied, showing an engaging fluid coherence where its core of juicy black currant and red berry fruits is effortlessly framed by finely polished, silky tannins and a vibrant thread of natural acidity. It finishes beautifully with a smooth, lingering aftertaste highlighted by a touch of savory earthiness and subtle sweet spices.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with roasted duck breast, pan-seared beef wellington, rosemary-rubbed grilled lamb chops, or savory wild mushroom risotto.

kanonkop-cabernet-sauvignon.title: Kanonkop Cabernet Sauvignon 2019
kanonkop-cabernet-sauvignon.bodyHtml:
Kanonkop Cabernet Sauvignon 2019 pours a deep, concentrated ruby-red color with a subtle crimson rim in the glass. The nose opens with a complex and classic bouquet of ripe blackberries, cassis, and fresh blueberries, beautifully layered with nuances of cedarwood, sweet tobacco, baking spices, and a distinctive hint of wild fynbos. On the palate, this exceptional South African red wine displays a medium-to-full body supported by fine, firm, and well-integrated tannins that provide a beautifully powdery texture. A succulent, concentrated core of juicy black cherries and dark berries intermingles with a dusty mineral tension and toasted oak spice, carrying great vitality and poise into a remarkably long, focused finish driven by persistent pencil lead and savory spice notes.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with slow-roasted lamb shanks, grilled prime ribeye steaks, rosemary-infused venison stews, or matured hard artisanal cheeses.

93 Points - James Suckling

A textural and well-balanced red with red berry, earth, cedar and baking spice aromas. Medium to full body with fine, firm tannins. It has a powdery texture on the center-palate and juicy cherries and red berries intermingling with the spices, bringing much vitality and poise. Focused long finish. Drink or hold.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Starting with tart red fruits and a dusty mineral essence, the 2019 Cabernet Sauvignon offers notes of black cherry and spiced plum. Medium-bodied and with a ripe, fresh fruit condition, the palate expresses fine-grained tannins with a dusty mineral tension. It ends with a long, spicy finish with persistent pencil lead essences. It's a well-made, sturdy wine that produced 72,000 bottles from wine that rested in 50% new French oak barrels for two years.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

An impressive, ageworthy Cabernet Sauvignon, with ripe cherry and plum seamlessly integrated into notes of fennel seed, star anise and Darjeeling. Retains ample energy and firm tannic grip, keeping the long finish focused and composed. Drink now through 2031.

brancaia-christmas-tre.title: Brancaia Tre 2021
brancaia-christmas-tre.bodyHtml:
Brancaia Tre 2021 is a highly approachable, organic Tuscan red wine that beautifully blends Sangiovese with international Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon. Sourced from three of the estate's top-performing properties across Castellina, Radda in Chianti, and the coastal Maremma, this medium-bodied cuvée captures a vibrant and versatile regional character. The wine matures for 12 months, with two-thirds of the blend resting in French oak tonneaux and one-third in concrete vats to preserve pure fruit intensity. On the nose, it releases a remarkably fresh and inviting bouquet of ripe blackberries, wild cherries, and red plums, elegantly layered with nuances of dark chocolate, licorice, dried herbs, and a subtle touch of orange peel. The palate is juicy and balanced, highlighting a silky texture, fine-grained tannins, and a crisp line of mineral acidity that carries into a smooth, savory finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs beautifully with classic pasta dishes with meat sauces, roasted poultry, grilled white meats, or a selection of medium-aged cheeses.

93 Points - James Suckling

Aromas of ripe blackberries and mulberries with blue flowers and dried rosemary undertones. Some dry earth, too. Medium- to full-bodied with creamy tannins and chalky texture. Succulent and racy. From organically grown grapes.

90 Points - Wine Spectator

Pure, boasting cherry, raspberry, rose, mineral and light wild herb aromas and flavors. Smooth and elegant, with ample yet well-integrated grip on the finish. Sangiovese, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon. Drink now through 2033.

barbera-dalba-aldo-conterno.title: Aldo Conterno Barbera d'Alba Conca Tre Pile 2021
barbera-dalba-aldo-conterno.bodyHtml:
Produced from mature Barbera vines in the renowned Conca Tre Pile vineyard in Bussia, Monforte d'Alba, this elegant Piedmont red offers aromas of dark plum, blackberry, violet, licorice, and subtle spice. Rich yet vibrant, it combines concentrated fruit, bright acidity, and refined structure with a long, polished finish. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

Food Pairing: Braised beef, roast pork, mushroom pasta, pizza, game dishes, and aged cheeses.

 

89 Points - Wine Spectator

Defined by its acidity and sleek profile, this red is nonetheless saturated with plum, fruitcake, earth, sweet spice and tobacco flavors. Concentrated, turning compact on the finish. Drink now through 2029. 1,600 cases made, 350 cases imported.

martins-lane-fritzis-pinot-noir-2015.title: Martin's Lane Fritzi's Vineyard Pinot Noir 2015 750ml
martins-lane-fritzis-pinot-noir-2015.bodyHtml:
A single, complex block from our oldest Pinot Noir vines. Granite-based soils & a South-Eastern aspect yield a wild wine of complexity and tension.

Notes
A warm year. A very warm Spring flowed into a wonderful summer, tapering into a cool Fall. Concentrated, powerful wines with great structure. These will be long-lived wines.
Aromas: Powerful. Earthy. Wild.
Palate: Rich. Complex. Sinewy

gerard-bertrand-clos-du-temple-rose.title: Gerard Bertrand Cabrieres 'Clos du Temple' Rose 2021
gerard-bertrand-clos-du-temple-rose.bodyHtml:
Gérard Bertrand Cabrières 'Clos du Temple' Rosé 2021 is a monumental, ultra-premium, and multi-layered biodynamic rosé that sits at the absolute pinnacle of luxury winemaking in the South of France. Sourced from a unique patchwork of old vines planted on the schist and limestone terraces of a historic amphitheater vineyard in Cabrières, this exceptional cuvée is widely celebrated as a profound gastronomic wine with the texture and longevity of a fine white Burgundy. It pours a very pale, glittering salmon pink with subtle reflections of brass and gold. The bouquet is remarkably complex and highly aromatic, slowly unfurling in the glass to reveal enticing scents of yellow peach, apricot, and pomegranate, beautifully intertwined with floral hints of rose petals, jasmine, and wild garrigue herbs, balanced by an integrated background of toasted almonds, vanilla, and sweet spices from its six months of maturation in new oak. On the palate, it is medium-to full-bodied, dense, and fleshy, delivering a powerful yet beautifully harmonious core of raspberry sorbet, ripe stone fruits, and juicy tangerine pulp. Animated by a vibrant, seamless acidity and an exquisite, creamy texture, it culminates in a remarkably long, structured finish distinguished by an intense undercurrent of salty mineral concentration, a fine-grained peppery grip, and a subtle whisper of blond tobacco.

Food Pairing: Pairs elegantly with premium seafood crudo, pan-seared scallops with truffle butter, tuna tataki, sea bass cooked en papillote, or roasted guinea fowl.

95 Points - James Suckling

Pale salmon color with a copper tinge. A serious rosé with a discreet mineral whiff to the fresh vanilla, tangerines, peaches, thyme, spices and fresh flowers. Full-bodied for rose with a broad structure to it. I love the texture and the creamy, yet fresh mouthfeel, rendering a taut palate with fresh, medium acidity. Flavorful and long. From biodynamically grown grapes with Demeter certification. Drink now or hold.

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Inviting pomegranate and white lily aromas pop on the nose of this rosé. The palate is plush with rose petal, raspberry sorbet and vanilla flavors. Beautifully balanced with a generous finish.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

Elegant and pure, this brings together floral, wild strawberry and white peach with garrigue and fleur de sel on a seamless palate. Creamy and harmonious, with impressive concentration and good length. Reveals talc-fine mineral notes that bring a pleasing bitter edge. Grenache, Cinsault, Syrah, Viognier and Mourvèdre. Drink now through 2028.

90 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

A blend of Syrah, Grenache, Cinsault, Viognier and Mourvèdre, the 2021 Languedoc Cabrières Rosé Clos du Temple was matured for six months in French oak barrels. Evoking aromas of oak, smoke, jasmine, rose petal, gooseberry and spices, it’s tense and fleshy, medium-bodied to full-bodied, lively and rather muscular with a long, fresh finish dominated by oaky notes, which are a little prominent for me at the moment.

cast-dei-rampolla-chianti-classico.title: Castello Dei Rampolla Chianti Classico 2021
cast-dei-rampolla-chianti-classico.bodyHtml:
Castello Dei Rampolla Chianti Classico 2021 is an elegant, biodynamically farmed Italian red wine from the renowned Conca d'Oro area in Panzano in Chianti. Blending predominantly Sangiovese with touches of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, this vintage is meticulously aged in concrete vats and oak barrels without clarifying or filtering. In the glass, it displays a bright ruby red color. The inviting aromatic bouquet opens with rich notes of Morello cherries, wild berries, and crushed dried flowers, beautifully accented by subtle hints of tobacco, cinnamon, and leafy underbrush. On the palate, the wine is delicate and medium-bodied, offering a silky texture, fine-grained tannins, and a vivid natural acidity. The vibrant, highly focused core of juicy red fruit funnels gracefully through to a long, flavorful, and incredibly harmonious finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs beautifully with grilled red meats like Bistecca alla Fiorentina, braised beef cheeks, roasted pigeon, hearty tomato-based stews, and well-aged cheeses.

92 Points - James Suckling

A dense, velvety and delicious Chianti Classico showing aromas of Morello cherries, wild berries and dried flowers on the nose. Medium-bodied with fine tannins. Plenty of texture, with a core of berries funneling through.

91 Points - Wine Spectator

Maraschino cherry, pomegranate, smoked meat, earth and rosemary flavors highlight this sleek red, which is defined by vivid acidity and solid tannins, with a dry, sinewy finish. Sangiovese, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot. Best from 2026 through 2037.

chiara-boschis-barolo-mosconi.title: E. Pira & Figli Barolo Mosconi 2020
chiara-boschis-barolo-mosconi.bodyHtml:
Chiara is an artisan grower whose philosophy is to craft wines that combine the extraordinary power of Barolo with approachability, balance, intense aromatics, and elegance.
97 Points - James Suckling
Dried oyster savoriness and intriguing wet stones with a touch of nice peppercorn funk to the cherries, hibiscus and plums. Broad and compact on the palate with a full body and plump morello cherries in the middle. Quite expansive and long, but transparent. Even more powerful than her exciting Cannubi from this vintage. From organically grown grapes.
93 Points - Wine Spectator
Though clearly focused on its cherry, raspberry and plum fruit flavors, this red also boasts savory elements of eucalyptus and woodsy underbrush. Well-endowed, with dense, dusty tannins that shape the compact finish.

rippon-mature-vine-pinot-noir.title: Rippon Mature Vine Pinot Noir Central Otago 2020
rippon-mature-vine-pinot-noir.bodyHtml:
Rippon Mature Vine Pinot Noir 2020 is an elegant New Zealand red wine from the renowned Rippon vineyard in Wānaka, Central Otago. Produced by the Mills family, Rippon is celebrated for its biodynamic vineyard management, mature vines and dedication to producing expressive, terroir-driven wines that reflect the distinctive landscape surrounding Lake Wānaka. Crafted from Pinot Noir grown on established vines, the 2020 vintage offers an enticing combination of ripe red cherries, raspberries and dark plums, complemented by delicate floral aromas, savoury herbs, earthy undertones and subtle spice. The palate is beautifully balanced, featuring vibrant acidity, fine-grained tannins and a silky texture that leads to a persistent, elegant finish. Its complexity and refined structure make it an excellent choice for Pinot Noir enthusiasts and special occasions.

Food Pairing: Duck confit, roasted lamb, venison, grilled salmon, mushroom risotto, truffle pasta, pork tenderloin, roasted chicken, aged Comté, Brie and Gruyère.

 

97 Points - James Suckling

Extremely perfumed with a pretty ripeness and clarity, offering plums and al-dente strawberries. Some cantaloupe, too. It's medium- to full-bodied with juicy fruit that's lovely and open. You want to drink it now. And do. Crunchy yet velvety and caressing in the mouth-feel from the lovely, open tannins. From biodynamically grown grapes with Demeter certification. Best in a year or two, but right on.

93 Points - Wine Advocate

The 2020 Rippon Mature Vine Pinot Noir is restrained on the nose, with an earthy (i.e., of the earth, gray rocks, etc.) countenance that I find highly engaging. In the mouth, the fruit comes alive with cherry and cranberry, pomegranate pearls, graphite and pencil lead, layers of black tea, coal dust and brine. This is dark without being heavy or dense, and it’s very fine. The silty tannins linger through the finish and seem to settle on the palate, which is pleasurable. It's fresh, and it's restrained and composed. An exciting wine. 13.5% alcohol, sealed under Diam.

rippon-rippon-mature-vine-riesling.title: Rippon Mature Vine Riesling 2021
rippon-rippon-mature-vine-riesling.bodyHtml:
Rippon Mature Vine Riesling 2021 is an expressive, biodynamically farmed white wine from the shores of Lake Wānaka in New Zealand's Central Otago region. Sourced from mature, ungrafted vines rooted in ancient schist gravel soils, this elegant Riesling reveals vibrant citrus, orchard fruit, and delicate floral notes. Naturally fermented and matured on its lees, it offers refreshing acidity, subtle sweetness, and distinctive mineral complexity.

Food Pairing: Fresh oysters, grilled seafood, sushi, Thai cuisine, roasted chicken, citrus-marinated fish, and soft cheeses.

 

94 Points - James Suckling

A creamy and beautiful riesling with sliced spiced pears and green apple aromas and flavors. Medium body. Off dry. Slate and mineral undertones. Green melon, too. More like a dry wine. Drink now.

markham-cabernet-sauvignon.title: Robert Mondavi The Estates Oakville Cabernet Sauvignon 2021
markham-cabernet-sauvignon.bodyHtml:
Robert Mondavi The Estates Oakville Cabernet Sauvignon 2021 is a rich, powerful, and impeccably balanced Napa Valley red wine. Sourced primarily from the historic To Kalon Vineyard in Oakville, it captures the depth, tension, and signature valley floor character of this iconic AVA. In the glass, it displays a dark garnet color with vibrant aromas of ripe blackberries, black cherries, cassis, and fresh mint. On the palate, it is full-bodied, delivering complex layers of dark fruit preserves, cocoa, dried herbs, and graphite, structured by firm, fine-grained tannins and balanced acidity leading to a long finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs brilliantly with prime dry-aged ribeye steak, roasted rack of lamb, braised short ribs, venison tenderloin, and aged sharp cheeses.

94 Points - James Suckling

Intense blackberries and black cherries on the nose lead to vivid focused cherries, blueberries and minty, spicy accents on the palate. Firm in tannins and fresh with good acidity, this outstanding wine is well-balanced.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

Generous in feel, this offers up a big gush of boysenberry, plum and blackberry preserve flavors that fold in nicely, with licorice, apple wood and cocoa notes on the finish.

chateau-troplong-mondot-2016.title: Chateau Troplong Mondot 2016 750ml
chateau-troplong-mondot-2016.bodyHtml:
Critic tasting note: (2016 vintage) "The inky hue in the wine clearly matches up with the level of concentration in the ripe, dark berries. Add in liberal doses of black licorice, smoke, espresso, chocolate and boysenberry, and you have the core of the wine. Powerful, full, rich and with real depth of flavor, give this 10-12 years before popping a cork." - 97/100, Jeff Leve, The Wine Cellar Insider

Classification
Saint-Emilion Premier Grand Cru Classé B


Producer Notes
The power of the ‘terroir’ tempered by the glistening fruit. The aromatic richness enhanced with elegant precision. The perfect balance of elements that respond to one another. The revelation of a unique universe that opens itself up over time. A feeling of fullness.

Drinking Window 2021-2050

Blend

90% Merlot, 8% Cabernet Sauvignon, & 2% Cabernet Franc
Vineyard Notes
Troplong Mondot dominates the landscape. Located at the highest point of the appellation, its ‘terroir’ benefits from an exceptional 360° exposure and incomparable soil complexity. In this atypical panorama, the vineyard is part of a natural heritage whose biodiversity is a long-standing reality. As the outcome of this perfect balance, the wines reflect the estate’s riches and reveal an identity like no other.

albea-gran-maestoso-primitivo.title: Gran Maestoso Primitivo 2021 750ml
albea-gran-maestoso-primitivo.bodyHtml:
Primitivo from contract growers in 2 areas of Puglia: the southern end of Bari with more calcareous soil, and Taranto an area with deep, moisture-rich soil. Vinified in a temperature-controlled stainless tank and aged 6 months in French barrique.

Aromas of black cherry, raisin, blackberry with bitter chocolate, tea, liquorice spice on the nose. Rich and full on the palate with a juicy black fruit core, ripe tannin, good acidity, good length on the finish filled with spice and dark fruit.

barbaresco-montefico-vigna-bric-mentina.title: La Ca' Nova Montefico Barbaresco Vigna Bric Mentina 2022
barbaresco-montefico-vigna-bric-mentina.bodyHtml:
An expressive nose of fresh red fruit, cherries and strawberries, layered with rose petals and subtle earthiness. The palate is gracefully balanced, showcasing the vibrant acidity and refined tannins typical of the region, culminating in a silky, long finish with a touch of spice and toasted oak from careful aging.

93 Points - Vinous

The 2022 Barbaresco Montefico Vigna Bric Mentina is bright and focused, with fine balance, especially for the year. Sage, mint, chalk, white pepper and orange peel give the Montefico its characteristic upper register. Vineyard signatures are very much present, even if somewhat attenuated in this vintage. This small-scale Montefico is a delight, but probably best suited for medium-term drinking.

barbaresco-montestefano.title: La Ca' Nova Barbaresco Montestefano 2022
barbaresco-montestefano.bodyHtml:
Montestefano's south-facing vines yield a powerful wine, rich in black cherry and ripe raspberry notes, accented by violet, mint, and smoky minerals. The ample sun exposure ensures well-rounded tannins and a concentrated palate, infused with a symphony of spices and a well-integrated oak influence, leading to a profound and enduring finish.

94 Points - Vinous

The 2022 Barbaresco Montestefano is laced with macerated cherry, cinnamon, new leather and mocha. It possesses terrific mid-palate density and overall fleshiness, both signatures of this site. There's good textural presence to wrap it all together. I especially admire how the Montestefano opens in the glass. It's the finest wine I tasted during my most recent visit, and the most likely candidate to improve in bottle.

red-rooster-the-golden-egg.title: Red Rooster Rare Bird Series Meritage 750ml

culmina-saignee-rose.title: Culmina Saignee 2023
culmina-saignee-rose.bodyHtml:
This vintage of Saignée has a charming bouquet of red currant, watermelon, and nectarine. Upon tasting, the stone fruit flavors are enhanced by a lively acidity and a smooth, silky texture. The polished finish is creamy and rich leaving a lasting impression of elegance and finesse.

Pair with choice charcuterie cuts of prosciutto cotto and capicollo; Salty fresh cheeses such as Halloumi.

kanonkop-pinotage-2010.title: Kanonkop Pinotage 2014
kanonkop-pinotage-2010.bodyHtml:
Kanonkop Pinotage 2014 is a iconic, benchmark South African red wine crafted from old, dry-farmed bush vines ranging from 32 to 67 years of age grown in decomposed granite and Hutton soils on the slopes of the Simonsberg Mountain. Matured for 16 to 18 months in small French oak barrels (80% new), it exhibits a dark ruby hue with deep, evolving aromas of plum compote, black cherry, cassis, and black licorice complemented by nuanced earthy undertones of forest floor, smoked meat, and subtle mocha oak spice. On the palate, it is full-bodied, structured, and richly textured, offering concentrated flavors of ripe blackberries, blueberry, and anise framed by silky, well-resolved tannins and a long, savory finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with Colorado lamb chops, braised beef short ribs, venison stews, barbecue pork, wild game, and aged hard cheeses like Gouda.

92 Points - James Suckling

Bright and delicious aromas of blackberries, blackcurrants, fruit compote and hints of vanilla and sweet spices. The full-bodied palate has a really fresh blueberry tinge that runs all the way through it with silky tannins and a long finish. One of the best pinotages from South Africa.

92 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

This is a late-release vintage that is currently being sold to appease those who collect and drink older wines. The Kanonkop 2014 Simonsberg Stellenbosch Pinotage Estate Wine opens to a medium-rich color and a glossy texture. A library of back vintages is kept at the winery for educational purposes, and this is one of the few wineries that does this. The wine's evolution is fascinating, with an emphasis on black licorice and earthy tar, and the intensity of the bouquet has developed and increased over the years. It was aged from 16 to 18 months in small oak barrel with 80% new oak. The tannins are resolved and smooth, and there are tertiary hints of forest floor, button mushroom and beef jerky.

91 Points - Wine Spectator

A juicy, racy style, with deliciously pure plum and blackberry compote flavors enlivened by an anise note that lingers through the finish. Features dark fruit but remains bright and fresh in feel. Well done. Drink now through 2020.

adobe-road-sauvignon-blanc.title: Adobe Reserva Organic Sauvignon Blanc
adobe-road-sauvignon-blanc.bodyHtml:
Adobe Reserva Organic Sauvignon Blanc is a vibrant, crisp, and eco-friendly Chilean white wine produced from organically grown grapes in the Casablanca Valley. On the nose, it releases expressive aromas of lime, grapefruit, green apple, and fresh lawn grass, backed by delicate floral and mineral undertones. The palate is light to medium-bodied, delivering a juicy core of citrus and tropical fruit, bright mouth-watering acidity, and a clean, invigorating, dry finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with fresh oysters, goat cheese crostini, grilled sea bass, ceviche, green garden salads, or served chilled as an apéritif.

beaurenard-bolsrenard-chat-du-pape.title: Domaine de Beaurenard 'Le Boisrenard' Chateaneuf-du-Pape Rouge 2021
beaurenard-bolsrenard-chat-du-pape.bodyHtml:
Domaine de Beaurenard 'Le Boisrenard' Châteauneuf-du-Pape Rouge 2021 is an exceptional, biodynamically farmed Southern Rhône red blend crafted from ancient vines—some over a century old—growing together as a traditional field blend of all 13 permitted regional grape varieties. Sourced from a mosaic of limestone, clay, and round pebble terroirs, it undergoes whole-cluster and co-fermentation followed by aging in oak foudres and barrels. In the glass, it presents a deep garnet color with complex aromas of black raspberries, ripe cherries, dark plum, garrigue, crushed stone, and subtle baking spices. On the palate, it is full-bodied, structured, and elegant, showcasing a silky weave of fine-grained tannins, fresh acidity, and a long, savory finish layered with dark fruit and minerality.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with roasted rack of lamb, braised beef short ribs, venison stew, wild boar ragù, truffle pasta, and aged cheeses.

95 Points - James Suckling

A spectacular, focused and structured red from old-vine co-plantings of the 13 varietals accepted in the appellation. The nose shows notes of spices, cherries, dark plums, currants, wild herbs, baking spices, bark and some peppercorns. It’s full-bodied with fine tannins. There is class in this wine, with a delicate, silky texture at the center and a wise structure framing the palate. Freshness kicks in toward the end and lifts the long finish. 

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

An unusually complete offering given the challenges of the vintage, Beauregard's 2021 Chateauneuf du Pape Boisrenard delivers waves of black raspberries accented by black olives and hints of garrigue. Full-bodied, rich and supple, with a long, velvety finish.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

This red's flavors of strappy black cherry, damson plum and fruitcake spices are edged in graphite as violet perfume adds lift, with good energy and subtly chewy tannins. Showing good power and energy, this is built for the long haul. One for the cellar. Drink now through 2032.

cote-rotie-cote-brune.title: E. Guigal Cote Rotie Brune et Blonde 2018
cote-rotie-cote-brune.bodyHtml:
The 2018 E. Guigal "Brune et Blonde" is a classical and incredibly consistent expression of Côte-Rôtie, sourced from a mosaic of nearly 40 different vineyard parcels across both the Côte Brune (known for its iron-rich schist and power) and the Côte Blonde (famous for its limestone and elegance). The 2018 vintage is noted for its generosity and ripeness, offering a seductive bouquet of blackberry, dark cherry, and red currant, accented by characteristic notes of violet, white pepper, and smoky bacon fat. On the palate, the wine is medium-to-full-bodied and remarkably round, showcasing silky tannins and a savory mineral core. Aged for 36 months in second-fill French oak, it offers a refined balance of fruit and wood, leading to a long, spicy finish with hints of licorice and forest floor.

95 Points - James Suckling

All of the classic Cote-Rotie aromas (leather, smoked bacon, spices and black cherry) pour from the glass of this rich and fleshy wine. Very silky texture, in spite of the generous, fine tannins, which build beautifully at the long, complete finish.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

This pushes lots of alder, incense and singed tobacco notes to the fore, with commensurate cherry and red currant paste flavors following behind that, finishing with perfume and red tea accents. This is not shy with its oak treatment and very nicely done. Best from 2022.

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Approachable and gentle, this wine has a dense core of brambly black and red berries, oak spice, warm earth and a stone minerality. It is balanced with round tannins, making the wine enjoyable now but it has enough structure to be easily cellared well past 2030+.

91 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

While the 2018 Cote Rotie Brune et Blonde comes across as being slightly less complex than the 2017, it's also fruitier and more overtly charming. Cherries and berries abound in this supple, medium to full-bodied effort that finishes long and silky.

serafini-vidotto-rosso-dellabazia.title: Serafini and Vidotto Il Rosso dell'Abazia 2019
serafini-vidotto-rosso-dellabazia.bodyHtml:
Serafini & Vidotto Il Rosso dell'Abazia 2019 is a distinguished Bordeaux-style red blend from Veneto's Montello hills in northeastern Italy. Crafted from Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, and Merlot, this expressive wine offers ripe plum, dark berries, candied citrus, and elegant herbal notes. Extended oak maturation creates a rich, harmonious palate with polished tannins and a long, complex finish.

Food Pairing: Braised beef, roasted lamb, grilled steak, pheasant, wild mushroom risotto, aged mountain cheeses, and hearty Italian dishes.

 

 

91 Points - James Suckling

A cabernet-dominant Bordeaux blend. Classy, yet again in the sort of international mold that could come from many quality regions around the world. Piercing scents of creme de cassis that verge on Ribena. Spearmint and vanillin oak, an addendum rather than a bludgeon. Good drinking, if not a great deal of personality.

87 Points - Wine Enthusiast

From the rolling Colli Asolani comes this oak-kissed blend, where a medley of red, blue, and black fruits mingle under a generous veil of warm spice. The palate offers a straightforward celebration of berries dressed in vanilla and toasted notes, delivering its message without pretense.

alta-mora-guardiola.title: Cusumano Alta Mora Guardiola Etna Rosso 2020
alta-mora-guardiola.bodyHtml:
Cusumano Alta Mora Guardiola Etna Rosso 2020 is an elegant, highly aesthetic volcanic red wine crafted from 100% Nerello Mascalese.
