grand-select-zlatan-otok.bodyHtml: This big, inky wine offers heady black fruit on the nose, along with a mild and well-integrated sweet oak. Strong tannins and a full body support incredibly concentrated black cherry, plum, and blueberry fruit on the palate, along with earth and tobacco.

tua-rita-per-sempre-syrah.title: Tua Rita Per Sempre Syrah 2020
tua-rita-per-sempre-syrah.bodyHtml:
Tua Rita Per Sempre Syrah 2020 is a rare and powerful expression of Italian viticulture, widely considered one of the finest Syrahs produced outside of the Rhône Valley. The 2020 vintage in Suvereto was marked by a warm, dry summer, which resulted in grapes with exceptional phenolic ripeness and an intense aromatic profile. Sourced from the estate's most prestigious, low-yielding plots, this wine was matured for approximately 18 months in 100% new French oak barriques to polish its monumental structure.
On the nose, it delivers an explosive and multi-layered bouquet of blackberry liqueur, black pepper, and scorched earth, accented by sophisticated notes of dark chocolate, smoked meat, and wild rosemary. The palate is full-bodied and profoundly concentrated, showcasing a dense, velvety core of black fruit and espresso underpinned by the signature ferrous minerality of the Maremma coast. The finish is remarkably long and resonant, featuring firm, fine-grained tannins and a persistent balsamic lift.

99 Points - James Suckling

Seductive aromas of violets, blackberries, blueberries, flowers and sandalwood. Sophisticated. Full-bodied with super-fine tannins and good length. Classy and superb. Such balance. Hints of sweet tobacco and berries at the end. You can drink it now, but it will age for decades.

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

This new vintage is just terrific because it marries a sunny growing season with a grape like Syrah, which thrives in these conditions. The Tua Rita 2020 Syrah Per Sempre embraces juicy, full-bodied fruit with lots of blackberry, plum, sweet spice and campfire ash. Stefano Frascolla deliberately seeks to avoid any eucalyptus or camphor-like overtones. He looks for bold primary fruit instead. This is achieved through fruit ripeness, vineyard care and oak management. Syrah has a short harvest window, so timing is important. The vineyards are planted in marl soils with schistic material that is typical of the mineral-rich hills surrounding Suvereto. The wine goes from barrique to botte grande for an additional two or three months to stretch its legs. The 2019 vintage is gorgeous, but this expression from 2020 has more power and heft.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

The nose is an acrobatic oscillation among savory, sweet and floral aromas, as notes of smoke, spices and pepper brighten into dancing sugar plums, then soften into vanilla cream. The palate maintains the remarkable intersection of spice and perfume, but a deep earth element brings in a savory, sanguine contrast. Tannins are gorgeously sculpted but imposing, like classical statues, while acid is linear and directed, like the artist's chisel.
94 Points - Wine Spectator
A dense red, with expressive black cherry, blackberry and plum fruit, plus accents of mineral, tobacco and spices. Firmly structured and vibrant, this ends with a lingering aftertaste of oak spices. Syrah. Best from 2025 through 2042.

cotarella-montiano.title: Cotarella Montiano 2020 750ml
cotarella-montiano.bodyHtml:
Montiano is a deep ruby red color and exhibits a wide range of aromas from red berries to spices with hints of vanilla. On the palate it is supple, full-bodied,elegant, and remarkably enjoyable with a lingering finish.

This wine exhibits its best qualities when paired with meat dishes.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The Famiglia Cotarella 2018 Montiano Cotarella shows a profound and deep personality with generous richness and concentration. Despite that supple approach, I would say that this vintage does not reach the level of fruit sharpness that we see in the exceptional 2019 vintage also reviewed in this report. Thanks to 12 to 14 months in medium-toast barrique, the tannins are sweet and add lasting structure.

92 Points - James Suckling
A medium-to full-bodied red with aromas of spiced plums, cherries, anise, balsamic and sweet tobacco. Firm, creamy tannins frame a plush core of dark fruit with rich spice notes on the finish.

chateau-clos-fourtet-2017.title: Clos Fourtet Saint-emilion Grand Cru (Premier Grand Cru Classe) 2017 750ml
chateau-clos-fourtet-2017.bodyHtml: Clos Fourtet Saint-Emilion Grand Cru (Premier Grand Cru Classe) 2017 is a powerful and elegant wine from the renowned Saint-Emilion region in Bordeaux, France. It offers complex aromas of dark fruit, spice, and tobacco, with a hint of cedar. The palate is rich and concentrated, with velvety tannins and a long, satisfying finish.

chateau-figeac-2017.title: Chateau Figeac 2016 750ml
chateau-figeac-2017.bodyHtml:
Blend: 38% Cabernet Sauvignon, 36% Merlot, 26% Cabernet Franc

98 Points - Decanter

A testament to the work being undertaken at Figeac in recent years, this has depth and intensity while retaining the smile of the fruit. Richness combines with gorgeous length and intensity, every bit as impressive as it was during en primeur. Touches of violet and a silky texture precede hugely precise slate walls that pull the fruit into place through the palate. It takes its time in the glass to fully open, only slowly revealing the black olives, pungent white pepper and rosemary aromatics. Bottled in late July. 100% new oak.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Another brilliant wine from the genius of Frédéric Faye, the 2016 Château Figeac checks in as 38% Cabernet Sauvignon, 36% Merlot, and the rest Cabernet Franc that spent 19 months in new French oak. Roughly 75% of the production made it into the grand vin. This deeply colored beauty is a legendary wine in the making and offers ultra-pure aromas and flavors of crème de cassis, smoke tobacco, dried herbs, chocolate, truffle, and graphite. Showing more violets notes with time in the glass, it builds incrementally on the palate, with flawless balance as well as incredible elegance, no hard edges, and a finish that won't quit. Readers will have a blast comparing the 2016 and 2015 vintages over the coming 3-4 decades and this estate is firing on all cylinders. This will most likely merit a triple-digit rating in 7-8 years and keep for 4 decades or more.
Rating: 98+

97 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2016 Figeac is comprised of 38% Cabernet Sauvignon, 36% Merlot and 26% Cabernet Franc. Deep garnet-purple colored, the nose is a little broody and reticent at this very youthful stage, slowly unfolding to reveal profound plum preserves, crème de cassis, black raspberries and star anise with hints of moss-covered bark, truffles and tilled loam plus a waft of red currants and raspberry leaves sparks. Medium to full-bodied, the palate is practically quivering with energy, offering glimpses at tightly wound black fruit and mineral/ferrous layers, framed by very firm, ripe tannins and wonderful tension, finishing long with the spices coming through. This will need a good 7-8 years to come round and then should cellar for 40+ years. Very serious, beautifully poised and sophisticated personality this vintage.
Rating: 97+

96 Points - James Suckling

This is a very linear and driven Figeac with smooth and fine tannins. Full-bodied, yet compact and reserved. Blackberry, chocolate and hazelnut flavors. Direct and structured. A blend of 38 per cent cabernet sauvignon, 36 per cent merlot, and 26 per cent cabernet franc. Better after 2024.

96 Points - Wine Spectator
A gutsy, fully endowed wine, brimming with dark currant, warm fig and steeped blackberry notes, as well as waves of smoldering tobacco and warm gravel. Features a serious bass line, but everything works together, while flecks of savory and iron dart in and out.

chateau-gazin.title: Chateau Gazin Pomerol 2021 750ml
chateau-gazin.bodyHtml:
The Chateau Gazin vineyards cover 64.2 acres in a single lot, with 56.8 acres under vines, located on the renowned clay-gravel plateau of Pomerol. The estate can produce up to 100,000 bottles a year. A second AOC Pomerol wine "l’Hospitalet de Gazin", was created in 1986 in order to reserve the best of the harvest for Chateau Gazin.

The grapes are fermented in small cement vats. The wine is aged for 18 months in oak barrels (50% new) according to the Bordeaux tradition: malolactic fermentation in casks, rackings to separate the fine wine from the lees, fining with egg whites and, if necessary, light filtration

bread-and-butter-prosecco.title: Bread & Butter Prosecco
bread-and-butter-prosecco.bodyHtml:
Aromas of florals and citrus are followed by lively yet soft notes of ripe apple, pear and white peach. Balanced with refreshing acidity, the creamy mouthfeel and layers of soft bubbles persist through to the long, elegant finish.

This wine goes well with flavorful breads, mild cheeses, and plenty of laughs with friends and family.

85 Points - Wine Spectator

A juicy Prosecco, with a zesty bead and notes of yellow apple, peach skin and grated ginger. Glera, Chardonnay and Pinot Grigio.

jane-eyre-cotes-de-nuits-village.title: Jane Eyre Cote De Nuits Villages 2020 750ml
jane-eyre-cotes-de-nuits-village.bodyHtml:
This wine has intense aromas of ripe black and red cherry fruit, coupled with delicate notes of pepper and rose petal. On the palate, juicy red fruits dominate with an elegant floral and subtle spicy character. 

As with all of Jane's wines, the Cote de Nuits Villages is elegantly structured, with poised, delicate tannins, bright acidity and excellently defined fruit flavours. The finish is long and lifted.

valpolicella-superiore-ripasso-zeni-ma.title: Zenato Ripassa Valpolicella Ripasso Superiore 2021
valpolicella-superiore-ripasso-zeni-ma.bodyHtml:
Zenato Valpolicella Ripassa Superiore 2021 is a concentrated, deeply expressive, and harmonious Italian red wine often affectionately referred to as a "baby Amarone." Crafted using the traditional ripasso method, the young Valpolicella wine is re-fermented over the warm, grape-skin pomace leftover from the estate's Amarone production, infusing it with extra body, complexity, and soul. It pours a dense ruby-red and reveals an aromatic bouquet of wild blackberries, dried prunes, and dark cherry jam layered with sweet baking herbs, crushed black pepper, and fine leather. On the palate, it is silken and round, presenting a velvety texture with rich flavors of plum, mocha, and licorice. Balanced beautifully by an integrated, cooling acidity and fine-grained tannins, it glides into a long, savory, and layered finish.

Food Pairing: Gorgonzola risotto, slow-braised beef shanks, savory rabbit ragù, grilled lamb chops with rosemary, and mature, flavorful hard cheeses.

94 Points - James Suckling

Evolved, complex wine full of depth, with aromas of forest floor, prunes and blackberry jam, plus subtle spice and smoky wood. The overall elegance is confirmed on the palate with medium body, integrated, refreshing acidity and savory, long, layered finish. One of the best Ripassos tasted this year. Drink now.

amarone-classico-zeni-della-valpolicel.title: Zeni Amarone della Valpolicella Classico 2019
amarone-classico-zeni-della-valpolicel.bodyHtml:
Zeni Amarone della Valpolicella Classico 2019 is a rich, full-bodied Italian red wine from Veneto's historic Valpolicella Classica region. Made using the traditional appassimento method, partially dried grapes develop concentrated flavours of ripe plum, dark cherries, cocoa, and warm spices. Extended oak maturation creates a velvety texture, offering an elegant balance of richness, structure, and a lingering finish.

Food Pairing: Braised beef, roasted lamb, venison, mushroom risotto, aged Parmesan, blue cheese, and hearty Italian stews.

 

90 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Sugared plums, candied violets, freshly ground coffee and cocoa all work together in the glass of this classically styled Amarone. The palate is soft and driven by the cocoa notes, with black-hued fruits right behind. The wine finishes with savory herbal and earthy accents.

manoir-de-mercey-rully-cuvee-louis-white.title: Domaine Berger-Rive Manoir De Mercey Rully Cuvee Louise 2022 750mlo
manoir-de-mercey-rully-cuvee-louis-white.bodyHtml: The Berger Rive Manoir De Mercey Rully 2020 is a refined white Burgundy from the Rully appellation, showcasing the elegance and complexity of Chardonnay. This wine offers aromas of green apple, citrus zest, and subtle white flowers, complemented by flavors of pear, lemon, and a touch of almond. Aged partially in oak, it delivers a balanced minerality with a refreshing finish and delicate hints of vanilla.

berger-rive-manoir-de-mercey-rully-en-ro.title: Berger-Rive Manoir De Mercey Rully En Rosey 2020 750ml
berger-rive-manoir-de-mercey-rully-en-ro.bodyHtml: The Berger Rive Manoir De Mercey Rully En Rosey 2020 is an elegant white wine from the Rully appellation in the Côte Chalonnaise subregion of Burgundy, France. This Chardonnay showcases a harmonious blend of crisp citrus, green apple, and white floral notes, with a subtle minerality and delicate oak influence. The wine's balanced acidity and creamy texture make it an excellent representation of Burgundy’s classic white wines.

manoir-de-mercey-mercurey-chateaubea-red.title: Dmaine Berger-Rive Manoir De Mercey Mercurey Chateaubeau 2020 750ml
manoir-de-mercey-mercurey-chateaubea-red.bodyHtml: The Berger Rive Manoir De Mercey Chateaubeau Mercurey 2019 is an elegant and expressive red wine from Burgundy, France, specifically the prestigious Mercurey appellation in the Côte Chalonnaise. This Pinot Noir offers a sophisticated palate with notes of ripe red cherries, wild berries, subtle oak, and earthy undertones. Medium-bodied with refined tannins, it delivers balance, complexity, and a lingering finish. Aged partially in oak barrels, this wine highlights the region's classic terroir-driven profile and is suitable for both immediate enjoyment and short-term cellaring.

chateau-dyquem-1.title: Y de Chateau d'Yquem 2023
chateau-dyquem-1.bodyHtml:
Y de Chateau d'Yquem 2023 is a sophisticated dry Bordeaux white showing grapefruit, lemon, white peach, fresh herbs, acacia, and subtle mineral notes. Vibrant and precise, the palate combines Sauvignon Blanc freshness with Semillon richness, delivering refined texture, impressive concentration, and a long, elegant finish.

Food Pairing: Pair with lobster, seared scallops, grilled turbot, roast chicken, creamy seafood dishes, or goat cheese for an elegant Bordeaux Blanc pairing.

rose-cuvee-cru-classe-tibouren-tradition.title: Clos Cibonne Tibouren Tradition Rose 2021 750ml
rose-cuvee-cru-classe-tibouren-tradition.bodyHtml: The Clos Cibonne Tibouren Tradition Rosé 2021 is a refined and elegant rosé from the prestigious Clos Cibonne estate in the Côtes de Provence region of France. Made from the Tibouren grape, an indigenous variety to the region, this rosé showcases a delicate balance of fresh red berries, citrus zest, and subtle floral aromas, with a hint of minerality from the estate’s terroir. The 2021 vintage offers crisp acidity, smooth texture, and a long, refreshing finish. Perfect for warm-weather occasions, seafood, or Mediterranean cuisine.

dario-princic-cabernet-sauvignon.title: Dario Princic Cabernet Sauvignon 2006 750ml
dario-princic-cabernet-sauvignon.bodyHtml: Dario Princic Cabernet Sauvignon 2006 is a full-bodied red wine from Friuli Venezia Giulia, Italy. The wine is crafted with exceptional attention to detail, offering complex aromas of dark fruits, herbs, and earthy undertones. Aged to perfection, it has a robust structure with smooth tannins and a long finish, making it ideal for pairing with rich meats and aged cheeses.

foreau-vouvray-moelleux-reserve-2009.title: Philippe Foreau Reserve Vouvray Moelleux 2009 750ml
foreau-vouvray-moelleux-reserve-2009.bodyHtml: Philippe Foreau Reserve Vouvray Moelleux 2009 is a beautifully crafted white wine from the Vouvray appellation in the Loire Valley, France. This demi-sec wine is made from Chenin Blanc, offering rich aromas of honey, ripe fruit, and a touch of floral notes. On the palate, it is elegant with a fine balance between sweetness and acidity, providing a smooth, round finish. It is perfect for pairing with foie gras, blue cheese, or fruit-based desserts.

chateau-montrose-saint-estephe.title: Chateau Montrose 2018 750ml
chateau-montrose-saint-estephe.bodyHtml: Château Montrose 2018 is a prestigious Bordeaux red wine from the Saint-Estèphe appellation, located in the Médoc region of France. This exceptional wine is a blend of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, offering deep, rich aromas of blackberries, cassis, and hints of tobacco and spice. On the palate, it is structured with powerful tannins, balanced acidity, and a long, elegant finish. It is a wine with great aging potential, ideal for collectors and connoisseurs, and perfect for pairing with grilled meats, game, and aged cheeses.

riesling-grand-cru-mandelberg.title: Gustave Lorentz Riesling Grand Cru Altenberg de Bergheim
riesling-grand-cru-mandelberg.bodyHtml:
Gustave Lorentz Riesling Grand Cru Altenberg de Bergheim is an exceptional Alsace white wine crafted from 100% Riesling. This Grand Cru showcases aromas of grapefruit, bergamot, lemon oil, cardamom, and flint, with a concentrated palate featuring vibrant acidity, pronounced minerality, remarkable depth, elegant structure, and a long finish.

Food Pairing:Fine fish dishes, lobster, scallops, roasted poultry with delicate sauces, and refined seafood cuisine.

chateau-des-annereaux-ldpomerol-2018-bio.title: Chateau des Annereaux Lalande-de-Pomerol 2018
chateau-des-annereaux-ldpomerol-2018-bio.bodyHtml:
Château des Annereaux Lalande-de-Pomerol 2018 is an elegant Bordeaux red blend from the renowned Lalande-de-Pomerol appellation on France's Right Bank. Produced from organically cultivated vineyards, this Merlot-dominant wine showcases concentrated blackberries, ripe plums, delicate spice, and subtle chocolate notes. Twelve months of oak maturation contribute depth and complexity without overpowering its vibrant fruit character. Silky tannins, balanced acidity, and a persistent finish make this an excellent expression of traditional Right Bank Bordeaux winemaking.

Food Pairing: Roasted lamb, grilled ribeye steak, braised beef, duck breast, mushroom risotto, venison, aged cheeses, and herb-roasted pork.

taylor-fladgate-vintage-port-2018.title: Taylor Fladgate Late Bottled Vintage Port 2019
taylor-fladgate-vintage-port-2018.bodyHtml:
Deep ruby red with vivid purple highlights on the rim. The first impression is of intense woodland fruit with crisp blackcurrant and blackberry aromas. The nose has a youthful freshness and vigor with bursts of powerful, black berry fruit slowly revealing undertones of raspberry and cherry, scents of wild herbs and discreet warmer notes of licorice and coffee. This elegant and polished LBV displays the characteristic Taylor definition and restraint. The palate is supported by taut, sinewy but perfectly integrated tannins and delivers a surge of powerful woodland berry flavors from the outset which are sustained into the long finish. The character of the 2019 harvest, with its freshness and pure, bright fruit, shines through on this wine. As usual, this LBV shares the precision and elegance of the great Taylor Vintage Ports in a more approachable and early drinking style.

A perfect finish to any meal. Excellent with fully flavored cheeses such as blue cheeses and Stilton or Roquefort. Also pairs well with chocolate or berry desserts.

93 Points - James Suckling
This is complex and powerful, offering notes of ripe but vivid black and blue fruit, crushed violets, coffee liqueur, wet stones and earth. Full-bodied and concentrated with firm tannins and walnuty character. Its not overly sweet and very lively on the palate, showing delicious fruit within the darker spectrum. Long and mineral. Drink now or hold.

st-joseph.title: Domaine Louis Cheze St. Joseph Blanc
st-joseph.bodyHtml:
A white Rhône from the northern appellation of Saint-Joseph, this wine typically displays aromas of white peach, apricot, and honeysuckle with a streak of minerality. On the palate it is medium-bodied, fresh, and textured, with bright acidity, gentle floral lift, and a clean, lingering finish driven by the Marsanne grape.

Food Pairing: Grilled river trout, roasted chicken with herbs, mild goat cheese, and dishes featuring cream sauces or fresh vegetables

vilain.title: Lucy M - Le Vilain Gris Petillant

lail-georgia-sauvignon-blanc.title: Grgich Hills Estate Sauvignon Blanc 2021
lail-georgia-sauvignon-blanc.bodyHtml:
This bright, zesty Sauvignon Blanc delivers great aromatic complexity by opening with aromas of fresh lime, lemon verbena and gooseberry. On the palate are flavors of lime, tangy star fruit and a hint of green mango. The long chiseled finish exhibits a wonderful slate minerality followed by juicy fresh citrus notes. 

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Vibrant and generous aromatics lead to a flavorful palate and lingering finish. This wine offers a tantalizing combination of flinty aromas, pithy citrus flavors and an energizing, palate-refreshing presence.

91 Points - James Suckling

Aromas of wet stone, sliced peach and fresh flowers. Medium- to full-bodied with citrus acidity and fresh stone fruit. A little phenolic tension here, too, with refreshing tannins at the finish.

mark-herold-uproar-cabernet.title: Freemark Abbey Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2019
mark-herold-uproar-cabernet.bodyHtml:
Freemark Abbey Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2019 is a classic, classic-styled Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon crafted from premium vineyard sources across the valley floor and mountain slopes. In the glass, it displays a deep garnet-purple color with intense clarity. The bouquet opens with inviting aromas of blackberry jam, dark plum, and cassis, seamlessly integrated with notes of milk chocolate, baking spices, cedar, dried tobacco, and subtle forest floor. On the palate, it is full-bodied, rich, and supple, offering a dense core of black fruit flavor underpinned by fine-grained, firm tannins and a balanced, lively acidity that leads to a long, polished finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with grilled ribeye steak, braised short ribs, roasted rack of lamb, savory venison stews, and aged hard cheeses.

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This bold, ripe but nicely polished wine wraps black cherries, black currants and mint in moderate, fine-grained tannins that will help carry it for several years. Subtle cinnamon, clove and cedar accents keep it interesting on the finish. Best through 2030.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

A fresh, polished style, with a relatively open-knit core of boysenberry and black cherry compote backed by friendly singed vanilla and licorice notes. A crowd-pleaser. Drink now through 2031.

conterno-fantino-barolo-ginesta-v-gris.title: Conterno Fantino Barolo Vigna del Gris 2011 750ml
conterno-fantino-barolo-ginesta-v-gris.bodyHtml:
A rich bouquet of ripe red fruits with prevalence of red cherries. A superb but elegant and grand structure with just the right amount of acidity.

A wonderful accompaniment to meat, pasta and aged cheese. A nice surprise with chicken cacciatore.

93 Points - Wine Spectator

An alluring mélange of sweet cherry, raspberry, licorice, menthol and spice aromas and flavors highlights this elegant red. Firm, yet stays balanced and long through the spice-filled finish. Best from 2018 through 2032.

93 Points - James Suckling

A firm and silky red with dark fruits, mineral and light walnut character. Medium to full body, very silky and a pretty finish. Such elegance and finesse. Better than 2010. Drink or hold.

93 Points - Wine & Spirits
From a plot in the Ginestra cru with a high percentage of sand, this is an autumnal wine with some delicacy to its structure. Dark berry flavors meld with savory notes of soy and hoisin, the flavors buoyed by brisk acidity and fine tannins.

conterno-fantino-barolo-mosconi.title: Conterno Fantino Barolo Mosconi 2012 750ml
conterno-fantino-barolo-mosconi.bodyHtml:
Deep garnet in color, the Barolo Mosconi has a fruity bouquet recalling brushwood, berry fruit, and brier rose. This wine has gorgeous structure, ripe, rich tannins, and complexity. Pairs well with meat dishes and seasoned cheese

93 Points - James Suckling

Aromas of dried meat, plum and sage leaf follow through to a full body, yet it's tight and tannic. Firm, chewy and polished tannins. Closed. Needs three years to open. Try in 2019.

90 Points - Wine Spectator
This is pretty, showing menthol, eucalyptus, cherry and tobacco flavors. Fresh and balanced overall, with a long finish. Needs a year or so to integrate. Best from 2018 through 2029.

conterno-fantino-barolo-mosconi-1.title: Conterno Fantino Barolo Mosconi 2011 750ml
conterno-fantino-barolo-mosconi-1.bodyHtml:
Deep garnet in color, the Barolo Mosconi has a fruity bouquet recalling brushwood, berry fruit, and brier rose. This wine has gorgeous structure, ripe, rich tannins, and complexity. Pairs well with meat dishes and seasoned cheese.

94 Points - James Suckling

A juicy red with a full body, spice and dried fruit character. Full and balanced with delicious fruit and a fresh finish. So hard not to drink now but better in 2018. Like it slightly better than 2010.

94 Points - Wine Spectator
The lovely, complex nose of sweet cherry, eucalyptus, menthol, licorice and tar shows the promise of this red. Beefy, well-integrated tannins add support as this lingers on the aftertaste. Displays fine intensity and harmony. Best from 2019 through 2035.

conterno-fantino-barolo-mosconi-2.title: Conterno Fantino Barolo Mosconi Vigna Ped 2005 750ml
conterno-fantino-barolo-mosconi-2.bodyHtml: Deep garnet in color, the Barolo Mosconi has a fruity bouquet recalling brushwood, berry fruit, and brier rose. This wine has gorgeous structure, ripe, rich tannins, and complexity. Pairs well with meat dishes and seasoned cheese.

conterno-fantino-barolo-sori-ginestra.title: Conterno Fantino Barolo Sori Ginestra 2014 750ml
conterno-fantino-barolo-sori-ginestra.bodyHtml:
Sori` Ginestra is Conterno Fantino’s flagship wine. The vineyard is located in the Ginestra district on one of the most important hills in Monforte, if not Barolo itself. It is the thoroughbred of Barolos, and fully reflects its terroir. Located 340 meters (1,115 feet) above sea level, it absolutely benefits from southern exposure, which affords the vines warm sunlight from morning to night. The soil is not sandy, but a bit more compact. The wines from this vineyard are bigger, with much more body, structure, and tannins. The older part of this vineyard was planted in 1971, giving the wine its unique elegance and complexity.

95 Points - James Suckling

Impressive complexity and fruit presence on the nose with ripe, spiced red plums, cherries and fresh cedary oak, leading to a palate with some handy weight. Good flow of fruit and tannins that carry the finish long. Try from 2022.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Enticing flavors of sweet cherry and strawberry are accented by leather, licorice and tar details in this solidly built yet supple red. Notes of wild herb, menthol, mineral and underbrush add interest as this plays out on the finish.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2014 Barolo Ginestra Vigna Sorì Ginestra is an amped up expression of Nebbiolo with excellent structure and lasting intensity. I am told that this vineyard site performs best in the cool vintages such as 2014. The wine plays its best cards in the mouth, thanks to the structure and the grounded firmness on offer here. Fabio Fantino tells me: "You can drive a car in the sunshine, in the rain and in the fog." I just love this quote because it so perfectly sums up the difficult 2014 vintage. As long as the driver knows where he or she is headed, the outside conditions can be navigated nevertheless.

94 Points - Wine & Spirits
Fruit for Sorì Ginestra comes from some of Conterno Fantino’s oldest vines, some up to 40 years of age, and those vines performed beautifully in the cool, wet 2014 vintage. The wine leads off with scents of green cardamom, mint and anise that follow through into cool herbal flavors. Notes of dark berries and sweet plums unfold as the wine opens, the fruit held taut by zippy acidity and vigorous tannins that need time to soften.

conterno-fantino-barolo-sori-ginestra-1.title: Conterno Fantino Barolo Sori Ginestra 2012 750ml
conterno-fantino-barolo-sori-ginestra-1.bodyHtml:
Deep garnet red with ruby highlights, with a rich, fruity and persistent bouquet of rose petals, brushwood and blackberries and a full-bodied, luscious, and austere palate.

A wonderful pairing with meat, pasta and aged cheese.

95 Points - James Suckling

Impressive complexity and fruit presence on the nose with ripe, spiced red plums, cherries and fresh cedary oak, leading to a palate with some handy weight. Good flow of fruit and tannins that carry the finish long. Try from 2022.

94 Points - Wine Spectator
Enticing flavors of sweet cherry and strawberry are accented by leather, licorice and tar details in this solidly built yet supple red. Notes of wild herb, menthol, mineral and underbrush add interest as this plays out on the finish.
94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate
The 2014 Barolo Ginestra Vigna Sorì Ginestra is an amped up expression of Nebbiolo with excellent structure and lasting intensity. I am told that this vineyard site performs best in the cool vintages such as 2014. The wine plays its best cards in the mouth, thanks to the structure and the grounded firmness on offer here. Fabio Fantino tells me: "You can drive a car in the sunshine, in the rain and in the fog." I just love this quote because it so perfectly sums up the difficult 2014 vintage. As long as the driver knows where he or she is headed, the outside conditions can be navigated nevertheless.

antoniolo-gattinara-riserva.title: Antoniolo Gattinara Riserva 2017 750ml
antoniolo-gattinara-riserva.bodyHtml:
96 Points - Decanter
Lorella Zoppis Antoniolo is an energetic producer of Gattinara. Her Riserva is released in a quantity of around 20,000 bottles. The grapes are fermented with their own natural yeasts in concrete, with a maceration of approximately 20 days and spontaneous malolactic fermentation. The wine ages in large 30hL oak casks for 36 months. There's a stunning complexity on the nose of savoury liquorice, smoky woodland, wild strawberry, violet and tar. The attack is relaxing and refined, with firm, dusty, velvety tannins and crisp acidity. It's austere and powerful enough to cellar but with the grace to drink now due to an amazing balance between the supple fruit and the structure. A very classic profile with graphite and earthy depth leading to a great finish.

crystal-head-vodka-pride.title: Crystal Head Vodka Limited Edition Pride 1.75L
crystal-head-vodka-pride.bodyHtml:
Art is empowerment, inspiring social change and fostering community. It is an influential tool empowering LGBTQ+ creators with a means of positive visibility and proud, authentic self-representation. Crystal Head Vodka is bringing the creative spirit to life with this limited edition Pride bottle, made with a one-of-a-kind decoration process unique to the brand. It shines proudly and brightly to celebrate diversity and equality and to inspire freedom of expression and creative thought.

The bottle contains our multi-award-winning original vodka distilled four times from the highest quality, locally sourced Canadian corn and blended with pristine Newfoundland water. The vodka is filtered seven times, of which three are through Herkimer diamonds. Crystal Head contains no sugar, additives, or gluten. This pure spirit is made with pride.

st-ambroise-apricot-can-4-pack.title: St Ambroise Apricot Can 4 Pack 4 Tall Cans
st-ambroise-apricot-can-4-pack.bodyHtml: St Ambroise Apricot Can 4 Pack 4 Tall Cans

pierre-gimonnet-special-club-chardonnay.title: Pierre Gimonnet Rose De Blancs Brut
pierre-gimonnet-special-club-chardonnay.bodyHtml:
Pierre Gimonnet et Fils Rose de Blancs Premier Cru Brut is a Rose Champagne based predominantly on Chardonnay, complemented by red Pinot Noir. Produced in the Cote des Blancs, it combines fresh red-fruit character with citrus notes, fine bubbles, mineral freshness and the precise structure associated with the house.

Food Pairing: Pairs best with seared salmon, duck breast, tuna tartare, and strawberry-glazed quail.

gimonnet-special-club-oger-cru-brut.title: Pierre Gimonnet & Fils Special Club Brut Champagne Grand Cru 'Oger' 2015 750ml
gimonnet-special-club-oger-cru-brut.bodyHtml: Pierre Gimonnet & Fils Special Club Brut Champagne Grand Cru 'Oger' 2015 is a luxurious and refined Champagne made from 100% Chardonnay, sourced from the prestigious Grand Cru village of Oger in the Côte des Blancs. This exceptional wine offers a bouquet of white flowers, citrus zest, and hints of minerality, alongside delicate notes of toasted brioche and almonds. On the palate, it is well-balanced with a fine, persistent mousse and a long, crisp finish. With its elegance and complexity, it showcases the quality and terroir of Oger, making it a perfect pairing for seafood, shellfish, and gourmet appetizers.

cota-45-carrascal.title: Cota 45 UBE De Uberrima Carrascal 2017 750ml
cota-45-carrascal.bodyHtml:
Ramiro Ibáñez Espinar is a talented winemaker who, with experience in Bordeaux and Australia as well as his native Sanlúcar, runs a winemakeing consultancy under the name GL Cero used by various bodegas in the Marco de Jerez. He is hugely enthusiastic about the potential of albariza soil and the recovery of traditional local grape varieties, many of which are all but lost, and which are no longer permitted in the Consejo regulations. He makes interesting wines to demonstrate the terroir and personality of each vineyard and grape variety without letting too much flor obscure it.

Aromas and flavours of citrus and mountain herbs, surprising acidity and a chalky tingle on the gums and tongue. Then the flavours grow in intensity and are herbal and savoury. The citrus flavours persist and turn slightly bitter like gooseberries.

charles-heidsieck-blanc-de-blancs.title: Charles Heidsieck Blanc De Blancs 750ml
charles-heidsieck-blanc-de-blancs.bodyHtml:
Charles Heidsieck was one of the very first Champagne Houses to demonstrate its passion for Chardonnay by producing a Blanc de Blancs in its 1949 vintage. There is also evidence that the Maison had produced some mono-crus from the Côte des Blancs as early as1906...  Through this cuvée, relaunched in 2018, two of the House’s areas of expertise come together: the production of great white wines and the art of blending a large selection of wines from different years and terroirs. The considerable challenge is to make opposites coexist: the tautness and the freshness of young chardonnays on the one hand, and the silky “Charles” character on the other.

The Blanc de Blancs is the result of a very selective blend of 100% Chardonnay from the Côte des Blancs and, in particular, the cuvée base 2016 is composed of 10 crus of Chardonnay, the most sought-after grapes in the region. 

For this cuvée, only the juice from the first press are used and, the wines benefit from a slow and long maturation of 3 to 4 years, far beyond the norms of the region.

ch-pavie.title: Chateau Pavie 2020 750ml
ch-pavie.bodyHtml:
100 Points - James Suckling

The aromas are already exceptional, showing crushed-stone, limestone and salt character to the dark fruit and bark. It’s full-bodied, yet agile. Floats on the palate, then kicks in with loads of ultra fine tannins. The intensity and verve of this wine promises true greatness. Barrel Sample: 99-100

99 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Composed of 50% Merlot, 34% Cabernet Franc and 16% Cabernet Sauvignon, the 2020 Pavie weighs in with an alcohol of 14.82% and a pH of 3.61. It is aging in French oak barriques, 75% new. Opaque purple-black colored, notes of plum pudding, blueberry pie and dark chocolate-covered cherries charge out of the gate, followed closely by hints of eucalyptus, star anise, unsmoked cigars and fertile loam with a hint of cedar chest. The full-bodied palate is built like a brick house, offering very firm yet wonderfully ripe, velvety tannins and seamless freshness to support the densely laden, muscular black and blue fruits, finishing very long and with loads of mineral-laced layers. As hedonic as it is cerebral this year, it is a beautiful paradox.
Barrel Sample: 97-99

99 Points - Vinous

The 2020 Pavie is very clearly one of the wines of the year. Rich, inky and wonderfully vibrant, it pulses with energy from start to finish. All the elements are well balanced. Soaring Cabernet Franc aromatics lead into a core of finely knit yet deep fruit in a wine that feels endless. Harvest for the reds started on September 17, paused briefly during some rain on the 25th and 26th, and then wrapped up by the end of the month. The blend is 50% Merlot, 34% Cabernet Franc and 15% Cabernet Sauvignon, so more Cabernets than in the past, the result of a large replanting program that began in the early 2000s. A real head-turner. Magnificent! –Antonio Galloni
Barrel Sample: 97-99

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

A wine that’s going to flirt with perfection, the 2020 Château Pavie is another magical wine from the genius of Gerard Perse and is 50% Merlot, 34% Cabernet Franc, and 16% Cabernet Sauvignon, brought up in 75% new French oak. The style here has unquestionably shifted from the blockbuster style of the 2000, 2005, 2009, and 2010 to a more elegant, refined style today that still brings plenty of fruit yet certainly stays more focused and precise. Is the new style better? I’m not sure, and there are certainly times I miss the opulence and decadence of the old style. Nevertheless, the wines today are magical Saint-Emilion that still show a rare mix of power and elegance. The 2020 is full-bodied and beautifully concentrated on the palate, offering a mouthful of cassis, black cherry, and mulberry fruits as well as a liqueur of rocks-like minerality, leafy herbs, and truffly earth. It doesn’t lack structure and has silky, polished tannins and flawless balance. Give bottles at least 7-8 years in the cellar and enjoy over the following 3+ decades.
Barrel Sample: 96-98

97 Points - Decanter

The Cabernets dominate the blend on the aromatics, and you can really see they are moving the needle on the architecture and sculpting of this wine. A ton of concentration on the nose and upfront, but it is well balanced by damson and blackberry, and has a sense of energy, uplift and clear minerality. This shows the limestone terroir in a way that, with the best will in the world, the more concentrated style of Pavie just didn't do. There is density and glamour, with layers of black chocolate, graphite and licorice. It is pretty disarming overall, and will age extremely well.
Barrel Sample: 97

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Big, bold and rich with solid black fruits and dense tannins that are definitely not shy. This solid wine is packed with structure. The fruit and freshness of the year are almost overwhelmed by the wine's richness. The wine is redeemed by the perfumed, balanced finish. Barrel Sample: 94–96

ch-pichon-lalande-comtesse.title: Chateau Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande 2022
ch-pichon-lalande-comtesse.bodyHtml:
Château Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande is the Grand Vin of the estate in the Pauillac appellation of Bordeaux. Crafted from estate-grown fruit, it is renowned for its elegance, complexity, refined structure, and exceptional ageing potential, expressing the distinctive gravel terroir of Pauillac.

Food Pairing: Pairs best with roasted lamb, beef tenderloin, duck, venison, braised short ribs, wild mushroom dishes, and aged hard cheeses.

 

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2022 Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande has turned out even better in bottle than I anticipated, bursting from the glass with aromas of cassis and blackberries mingled with scents of licorice, violets and pencil shavings. Full-bodied, layered and enveloping, it's suave, seamless and complete, with faultless precision, pristine integration of tannin, controlled sweetness and a long, expansive finish. The 2022 manages to unite the sensuality that's the estate's calling card and the ripeness of the vintage on the one hand, with a sense of Pauillac classicism on the other, threading the needle to deliver one of the finest wines of the vintage and a benchmark Pichon Comtesse. It's a blend of 78% Cabernet Sauvignon, 17% Merlot and 5% Cabernet Franc.

99 Points - James Suckling

What perfect aromas of blackcurrants, lead pencil, violets, blood oranges and blood. Some iron. Medium- to full-bodied, this has incredible tannins that are completely loaded and integrated, melting into the wine with such a glorious mouthfeel. The finish goes on and on, lightly austere in the most sophisticated way. Racy and rigorously focused. 78% cabernet sauvignon, 17% merlot and 5% cabernet franc.

98 Points - Decanter

One of my favourite wines from 2022, utterly seductive from the first sip, this is a stunning effort that shows the power of Pauillac in 2022 delivered with elegance and class. Heavily scented on the nose, full of dark fruits, savoury notes of salty chocolate and floral scents. Smooth and so appealing in the mouth, the texture stands out, deep and rich but soft and chalky, tannins have a subtle powderiness that spreads the mouth, cooling and refreshing giving the minerality while the cool black and blue fruits linger in layers expanding vertically. This is so refined and polished - it's serious no doubt, not super fun, but it doesn’t need to be, it’s rich and sumptuous with sweet blue fruits balanced by high acidity that keeps the focus and energy. Bright, bold, well worked, clean, crystalline and pure. Somehow delicate and punchy at the same time. A mind-blowing wine that you just have to marvel at with intensity, brightness and vibrancy, building as it goes. A long, clean finish leaves you wanting more, salivating for that next sip.

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Looking at the flagship 2022 Château Pichon Longueville Comtesse De Lalande, it's based on 78% Cabernet Sauvignon, 16% Merlot, and the balance Cabernet Franc that spent 19 months in two-thirds new oak and one-third in once-used barrels. Its similarly deep purple hue is followed by a magical, heavenly 2022 that has a layered, full-bodied profile that brings an incredibly floral character as well as a huge core of darker currant fruits, ripe, polished, velvety tennis, no hard edges, and a thrilling finish. It’s a quintessential Comtesse that brings the forward, supple elegance of the château while still offering plenty of classic Pauillac depth, structure, and character.

98 Points - Wine Spectator

This brims with notes of dark currant, blackberry and black cherry preserves that sparkle subtly with reserved energy, while sweet tobacco, licorice snap, chestnut, violet and ink notes work harmoniously through the long, crumpled velvet finish. A late humus echo provides a beautiful counterpoint, which just makes you want to go right back and start the experience all over with another sip. A total stunner. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Cabernet Franc.

piteira-talha-doc-tinto.title: Piteira Vinho De Talha Tinto 2017
piteira-talha-doc-tinto.bodyHtml:
Piteira Vinho De Talha Tinto 2017 is a traditional, deeply authentic Portuguese red wine produced using centuries-old Roman winemaking techniques in the Alentejo subregion of Granja-Amareleja. Crafted exclusively from 100% Moreto grapes harvested from old vines, the wine undergoes natural fermentation and skin contact in large 2,000-liter clay amphorae (talhas). In the glass, it displays a deep ruby hue with rustic undertones. The nose presents wild red berries, stewed plums, clay dust minerality, dried herbs, and subtle spice notes. On the palate, it is full-bodied and textured, featuring bright, natural acidity, firm rustic tannins, and a long, savory finish driven by earthy red fruit depth.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with braised lamb shanks, roasted pork shoulder, wild game stews, grilled chorizo, cured Portuguese sausages, and aged hard cheeses.

tesselaarsdal-wines-pinot-noir.title: Tesselaarsdal Pinot Noir 2022 750ml
tesselaarsdal-wines-pinot-noir.bodyHtml:
South African Wine
With an important wine renaissance in full swing, impressive red and white bargains abound in South Africa. The country has a particularly long and rich history with winemaking, especially considering its status as part of the “New World.” In the mid-17th century, the lusciously sweet dessert wines of Constantia were highly prized by the European aristocracy. Since then, the South African wine industry has experienced some setbacks due to the phylloxera infestation of the late 1800s and political difficulties throughout the following century.

Today, however, South Africa is increasingly responsible for high-demand, high-quality wines—a blessing to put the country back on the international wine map. Wine production is mainly situated around Cape Town, where the climate is generally warm to hot. But the Benguela Current from Antarctica provides brisk ocean breezes necessary for steady ripening of grapes. Similarly, cooler, high-elevation vineyard sites throughout South Africa offer similar, favorable growing conditions.

South Africa’s wine zones are divided into region, then smaller districts and finally wards, but the country’s wine styles are differentiated more by grape variety than by region. Pinotage, a cross between Pinot Noir and Cinsault, is the country’s “signature” grape, responsible for red-fruit-driven, spicy, earthy reds. When Pinotage is blended with other red varieties, like Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah or Pinot Noir (all commonly vinified alone as well), it is often labeled as a “Cape Blend.” Chenin Blanc (locally known as “Steen”) dominates white wine production, with Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc following close behind.
Pinot Noir
Thin-skinned, finicky and temperamental, Pinot Noir is also one of the most rewarding grapes to grow and remains a labor of love for some of the greatest vignerons in Burgundy. Fairly adaptable but highly reflective of the environment in which it is grown, Pinot Noir prefers a cool climate and requires low yields to achieve high quality. Outside of France, outstanding examples come from in Oregon, California and throughout specific locations in wine-producing world. Somm Secret—André Tchelistcheff, California’s most influential post-Prohibition winemaker decidedly stayed away from the grape, claiming “God made Cabernet. The Devil made Pinot Noir.”

chianti-gratius-il-molino-di-grace.title: Il Molino Di Grace Toscana Gratius 2012 750ml
chianti-gratius-il-molino-di-grace.bodyHtml: Pure Sangiovese aromatics, wild cherry and sweet plum nose, united with classic balance on the palate, straightforward yet yielding, soft yet concentrated and finishing with a real sense of place. The 2012 Il Molino di Grace "Gratius" is a powerhouse, not an exploding fruit laden blockbuster, this wine is focused yet supple on the palate, chocolaty, toasted almonds, ripe and potent with a long lasting finish. 93 Points Wine Spectator

ch-peby-faugeres.title: Chateau Peby Faugeres 2018
ch-peby-faugeres.bodyHtml:
Château Péby Faugères is the flagship cuvée of the Faugères estate in Saint-Émilion Grand Cru, crafted primarily from Merlot. Rich and concentrated, it reveals layers of black cherry, blackberry, plum, dark chocolate, licorice, and graphite with velvety tannins and remarkable aging potential.

Food Pairing: Pair with beef tenderloin, roast lamb, venison, duck breast, braised short ribs, truffle dishes, or aged hard cheeses.

 

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2018 Château Péby Faugères is another brilliant wine from this talented team. Based on 100% Merlot from vines in the eastern side of the appellation, it was brought up in 65% new French oak, which has been the norm for the past couple of years. (The 2015 saw 90% new oak.) Deep purple-hued, with a glorious bouquet of crème de cassis, toasted spices, violets, vanilla, and a touch of chalky minerality, this full-bodied, super-rich, incredibly sexy Saint-Émilion builds with time in the glass and has a great mid-palate and flawless balance. It has a modern style, yet I still find plenty of classic Saint-Émilion minerality. It's already beautiful, but smart money will give bottles 3-5 years and it should keep for two decades.

98 Points - Wine Spectator

Offers layers of dark fig, boysenberry and cassis fruit, with alluring black tea and anise notes. The long, smoldering finish is carried by a graphite edge. Dense, but with serious cut and detail. A classic in the making.

97 Points - James Suckling

Very attractive aromas of currants, blackberries, bark and dried mushroom follow through to a full body with firm, fine tannins that are round and creamy-textured. Pretty finish. Drink after 2024.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Made of 100% Merlot, the 2018 Péby Faugères has a deep garnet-purple color and bombastic scents of plum preserves, baked black cherries, cedar chest and blueberry pie with an undercurrent of menthol, black olives, charcuterie and Indian spice, plus a waft of oolong tea. The seductively rich, full-bodied palate (15.5% alcohol) delivers mouth-coating black fruit preserves with a velvety texture and just enough freshness, finishing long and spicy yet with a touch of oak poking through. It will need a good 5 years in cellar for the oak to settle in, then drink it over the next 20 years or more. Rating: 95+

91 Points - Decanter

Inky damson in colour, this is a wine where you can feel the influence of the cooler terroir in terms of the bulkier tannins. They are not rustic but are certainly present, crawling across the palate. It's good quality - as are all the Denz wines in 2018, but there's no escaping the slightly distracting concentration, with a little too much marzipan oak on the finish. Drinking Window 2026 - 2040.

ch-smith-haut-lafitte-rouge.title: Chateau Smith Haut Lafitte 2023
ch-smith-haut-lafitte-rouge.bodyHtml:
A distinguished Pessac-Leognan red with aromas of blackcurrant, blackberry, plum, graphite, cedar, and subtle tobacco. Concentrated fruit, polished tannins, and mineral freshness create a powerful yet elegant palate with impressive complexity, balance, and a persistent finish.

Food Pairing: Pair with beef tenderloin, roast lamb, duck breast, venison, grilled ribeye, truffle dishes, aged Comte, or wild mushrooms.
98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2023 Château Smith Haut Lafitte offers black currants, smoky tobacco, graphite and subtle espresso. Composed of 70% Cabernet Sauvignon, 23% Merlot, 6% Cabernet Franc and 1% Petit Verdot, it is medium- to full-bodied with impressive concentration and focus. Ripe tannins provide structure, while chalky minerality and freshness define the finish. Beautifully balanced and exceptionally pure.

98 Points - James Suckling

Currant, tobacco and hazelnut aromas lead into a medium-bodied palate with vibrant, crunchy fruit and attractive open-grained, velvety tannins. Graceful, fresh and beautifully composed, it combines immediate appeal with excellent underlying structure. From biodynamically grown grapes, the blend is 70% Cabernet Sauvignon, 23% Merlot, 6% Cabernet Franc and 1% Petit Verdot. Best from 2028 onward.

97 Points - Decanter

Dark and intensely fragrant, with roses and floral notes introducing a cool, fresh profile. The substantial palate combines powdery tannins with juicy fruit, mint, graphite, wet stone, herbs, cocoa and licorice. More muscular and streamlined than typically suave expressions of Smith Haut Lafitte, it nevertheless retains finesse, freshness and tension. Chewy strawberry and cranberry notes add further complexity to this structured, age-worthy wine. 

96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2023 Smith Haut Lafitte offers aromas of licorice, spices, dark berries, rose petals and clove. Medium- to full-bodied, dense and precisely structured, it possesses a fleshy, concentrated core surrounded by abundant yet seamlessly integrated tannins. A long, mineral and penetrating finish reinforces its impressive potential for extended cellaring.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Bold and generously styled, with mocha and bittersweet cocoa leading into plum reduction, blackberry preserves and melted black licorice. Roasted vanilla, chestnut and sweet tobacco enrich the finish, while an earthy, loamy element provides balance and structure. A powerful blend of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot.

luigi-righetti-amarone-classico.title: Luigi Righetti Corvina Campo Tordi 2019 750ml
luigi-righetti-amarone-classico.bodyHtml: Comprised of 100% Corvina, the primary varietal in wines such as Valpolicella Classico and Amarone della Valpolicella. Unlike these traditional wines, however, Campo Tordi is fermented in temperature controlled, stainless steel tanks as opposed to neutral Slavonian oak barrels. The result is a fresher more fruit driven expression of the Corvina grape. Look for notes of bright, red cherry fruit with a subtle bitter almond on the finish. Light tannins, balanced acidity.

castelvecchi-chianti-classico.title: Castelvecchi Capotondo Chianti Classico 2022
castelvecchi-chianti-classico.bodyHtml:
This Chianti Classico is a blend of 88% Sangiovese and 12% Canaiolo grapes, grown in the heart of the Chianti Classico region. The wine is aged for 14 months in a combination of large barrels and barriques, resulting in a well-balanced wine with a smooth, complex flavour profile. Deep ruby red with violet reflections. Fresh and inviting, with aromas of red fruits like cherry and plum, complemented by delicate floral notes of rose and violet. Hints of spice add complexity. Harmonious and well-balanced, with a velvety texture and a lingering finish. Flavours of ripe red fruit are supported by subtle spice and oak notes.   

90 Points - James Suckling

A textured, fruity and juicy Chianti Classico delivering aromas of cherries, currants and dried herbs on the nose, following through to a medium body with fine tannins. Silky and balanced, with a polished character and a juicy, peppery finish. Drink now.

castelvecchi-chianti-classico-riserva.title: Castelvecchi Lodolaio Chianti Classico Riserva 2019
castelvecchi-chianti-classico-riserva.bodyHtml:
Castelvecchi Lodolaio Chianti Classico Riserva 2019 is an elegant Tuscan red wine crafted from 100% Sangiovese grown in the hills of Radda in Chianti. Aged in French oak, this expressive Riserva reveals ripe cherries, blackberries, aromatic spices, and subtle earthy notes. Its structured tannins, vibrant acidity, and refined finish showcase the character of Chianti Classico.

Food Pairing: Florentine steak, braised beef, roasted lamb, wild boar, mushroom risotto, and aged Pecorino cheese.

 

93 Points - James Suckling

A nicely judged blend of juicy plum and berry fruit and lightly spicy oak on the nose. Medium-bodied with good balance, the weighty, spicy fruit dominating through to the end. The firm tannins show themselves late and feel a little apart. Needs another couple of years for greater integration, but shows promise. Try from 2026.

91 Points - Wine Enthusiast

A primarily sanguine, umami nose offers aromas of soil, coffee, cured meat, balsamic and herbs, then tart black cherries and blackberries. The fruit bounces off the palate, but undertones of spice and bitterness, along with polished yet chewy tannins, provide structure. Satisfying and energetic.

eberle-estate-cabernet-sauvignon.title: Beaulieu Vineyard Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2019
eberle-estate-cabernet-sauvignon.bodyHtml:
Beaulieu Vineyard Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2020 is a rich, elegant, and full-bodied red wine from California's renowned Napa Valley. Crafted with carefully selected Cabernet Sauvignon grapes, this wine showcases the region's exceptional winemaking heritage and Beaulieu Vineyard's commitment to quality. It offers concentrated dark fruit flavours, refined tannins, and subtle oak influences, creating a beautifully balanced and sophisticated drinking experience. With its smooth texture, layered complexity, and lingering finish, this Cabernet Sauvignon is an excellent choice for special occasions, fine dining, or enjoying with a hearty meal.

Food Pairing: Perfect with grilled ribeye steak, roasted lamb, beef tenderloin, braised short ribs, barbecue, hearty pasta dishes, mushroom risotto, and aged cheeses such as cheddar and Gouda.

 

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast 

Focused and brilliant flavors of red and black cherries and black currants drive this sleek and powerful wine, as minty, toasty, and tobacco-like accents stay subtly in the background until the finish. A full body, medium to full tannins and good fruit acidity lend tangy freshness. Best from 2026.

91 Points - James Suckling 

A juicy and delicious wine with a round and polished texture with hints of chocolate and walnuts. Some iron shavings, too. Medium body. Savory at the end. Lovely dark fruit in the finish. Juicy. Drink now.

91 Points - Wine Spectator

Shows a light mesquite edge that mingles with gently mulled plum and blackberry fruit flavors, while lightly singed vanilla and tobacco fill in through the finish. Reveals a solid graphite spine, too. Drink now through 2033. Tasted twice, with consistent notes

eberle-syrah.title: E. Guigal Crozes Hermitage 2019
eberle-syrah.bodyHtml:
The 2019 E. Guigal Crozes-Hermitage is a robust and deeply expressive Syrah from a vintage defined by exceptional solar intensity and concentration. Sourced primarily from the villages of Beaumont-Monteux and Mercurol, this wine reflects the stony, alluvial terroirs of the region. It presents a dark, brilliant ruby colour and an intense bouquet of blackberries, red currants, and plums, interwoven with signature notes of black pepper, smoked meat, and violet. On the palate, the wine is full-bodied and fleshy, featuring a rich texture and fine-grained tannins that provide a solid structural framework. Aged for 24 months in second-fill French oak, it balances its powerful dark fruit core with a refined savory complexity and a long, persistent finish.

91 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The only one of the 2019 reds to have been bottled at the time of my visit, the 2019 Crozes Hermitage is a super effort, and it should represent a terrific value. Hints of violets accent blueberries and cassis on the nose in this full-bodied, concentrated offering. Rich, velvety and a bit tannic, it's an impressive négoce bottling.

90 Points - Wine Spectator

A perfumed style, with silky-edged red currant and Damson notes flecked with sandalwood, white pepper and sanguine hints that then linger prettily on the dusty finish. Drink now through 2025.

eberle-viognier.title: Eberle Mill Road Vineyard Viognier 2019 750ml
eberle-viognier.bodyHtml:
Vibrant flavors of ripe pears, peaches, almonds and spice add to the lush mid-palate of this exceptional wine. The clean and refreshing citrus finish makes a perfect partner for a variety of foods or a spectacular treat just by itself.

90 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Tight apple-blossom, candied jasmine and tart apple-slice aromas show on the nose of this bottling from the Mill Road and Four Lanterns vineyards. There's a pleasant ashy tone on the palate, where peach, melon and bubblegum flavors converge. Matt Kettmann

mate-brunello-di-montalcino-riserva.title: Le Potazzine Brunello Di Montalcino Riserva 2015 750ml
mate-brunello-di-montalcino-riserva.bodyHtml: The 2015 Le Potazzine Brunello di Montalcino Riserva is a highly-regarded Brunello, known for its elegant, full-bodied profile with notes of cherry, spice, and cedar. It's a wine that benefits from aging, with critics recommending drinking it after 2023.

chateau-jean-faux-les-sources-bordeaux.title: Chateau Grand Jean Bordeaux Superieur Reserve Rouge 2022
chateau-jean-faux-les-sources-bordeaux.bodyHtml:
The 2022 Château Grand Jean Bordeaux Supérieur Réserve Rouge is a rich, oak-aged blend with aromas of ripe blackberry, blackcurrant, cedar, toasted oak, and subtle undergrowth. Firm yet polished tannins, refreshing acidity, and concentrated dark fruit create a full-bodied, structured palate with excellent aging potential. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

Food Pairing: Pair with grilled ribeye, roast lamb, beef bourguignon, venison, aged cheddar, mushroom dishes, or hard alpine cheeses.

 

90 Points - James Suckling

A spicy, full-bodied red, showing notes of blackcurrants, roasted plums and spice box, framed by medium-firm tannins. Attractively toasty. Drink from 2026.

89 Points - Wine Enthusiast

A smoky young wine, showing its wood aging. It has attractive black currant fruits and a structure from the Cabernet Sauvignon in the blend. Drink from 2026.

89 Points - Wine Spectator

Fresh and inviting, with a sleek edge to its mix of blackberry and black cherry preserves. Subtle hot stone and tobacco notes permeate the finish. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Malbec. Drink now through 2027. 25,000 cases made, 2,000 cases imported.

castellin-villa-santacroce-1997.title: Castell'in Villa Santacroce 2004
castellin-villa-santacroce-1997.bodyHtml:
Castell’in Villa Santacroce 2004 is a deeply complex, beautifully matured, and historically significant Super Tuscan that exemplifies the estate’s mastery of blending native Sangiovese with international varietals. Pouring a beautiful dark garnet hue with brick-red reflections, it opens with an intensely expressive bouquet of dried black cherries, cassis, and wild plum, gracefully intertwined with savory tertiary notes of worn leather, sweet pipe tobacco, damp earth, and toasted cedar from its 18 months of maturation in French oak barriques. On the palate, it is medium to full-bodied, firmly structured, and remarkably elegant. This seamless 50/50 blend of Cabernet Sauvignon and Sangiovese offers a generous core of dark fruit, beautifully balanced by finely integrated tannins and a refreshing, vibrant acidity that keeps the wine incredibly lively. It culminates in a long, savory, and multi-layered finish that beautifully showcases its outstanding age-worthiness and complex evolution.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with premium grilled ribeye steaks, slow-roasted wild boar, a rich duck ragù, and well-aged pecorino cheese.

93 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2004 Santacroce is silky, layered and impeccably balanced. Sweet red roses, red berries and spices are all woven together beautifully in this refined, expressive wine. This is a lovely showing. The 2004 captures the essence of the 2004 vintage in a relatively soft, supple style built for near and mid-term enjoyment. Anticipated maturity: 2012-2020.

emilia-romagna-la-stoppa-macchiona-2010.title: La Stoppa Macchiona 2016
emilia-romagna-la-stoppa-macchiona-2010.bodyHtml: It’s a red wine with a deep ruby red colour, and on the nose, it presents aromas of red berry fruit, followed by spicy and earthy notes. The palate is described as structured, fresh, and pulpy, offering a long finish. This wine represents the Colli Piacentini region, with a taste profile that reflects its terroir.

lion-dragon-cuvee-rose.title: Chateau Roubine Lion & Dragon Rose (Cru Classe) 2020 750ml
lion-dragon-cuvee-rose.bodyHtml:
The Lion & Dragon Rosé from Château Roubine in Provence reveals a bright, light red color in the swirled glass. When swirling the wine glass, one can perceive a first-class balance in this rosé wine, as it does not stand out on the walls of the glass, neither watery nor syrupy or liqueur-like. To the nose, this Château Roubine rosé wine shows all sorts of lemons, strawberries and pears. As if that weren't already impressive, the aging in large wooden barrels adds other aromas like toasted wood.

The Château Roubine Lion & Dragon Rosé presents itself to the wine lover wonderfully dry. This rosé wine is never coarse or meager, as one might expect from a top wine. Balanced and multifaceted, this light rosé wine presents itself on the palate. In the finish, this youthful rosé wine from the wine-growing region of Provence finally inspires with considerable length. There are again hints of strawberry and lemon.

Food recommendation for the Lion & Dragon Rosé from Château Roubine
Drink this rosé wine from France ideally moderately chilled at 11 - 13°C as an accompanying wine to asparagus salad with quinoa, stir-fried vegetables with fish or coconut-lime fish curr

Andreas Larsson: 93Pts; Jancis Robinson: 92Pts; Wine Enthusiast: 90Pts
Certified Organic & Biodynamic

valdemar-la-gargantilla-garnacha.title: Bodegas Borsao Tres Picos Garnacha 2020 750ml
valdemar-la-gargantilla-garnacha.bodyHtml: Critic tasting note: (2019 vintage) "This wine offers a nose of dark plum and raspberry with a hint of forest floor. It is soft in the mouth, with delicate tannins and flavors of black cherry, fennel pollen and coffee bean. There is a note of orange zest that lingers on the finish. Mike DeSimone" - 88/100, Wine Enthusiast

social-lite-vodka-soda-24-pack.title: Nude Vodka Soda 24 Mix Pack Sleek

podere-le-boncie-le-trame-igt.title: Podere Le Boncie Le Trame 1.5L Magnum
podere-le-boncie-le-trame-igt.bodyHtml:
Le Trame is the flagship wine of Podere Le Boncie, crafted from organically farmed vineyards in the hills of Tuscany. Elegant and expressive, it reveals aromas of red cherry, wild berries, dried flowers, spice, and earthy undertones. The palate is vibrant and refined with bright acidity, fine tannins, and remarkable balance, leading to a long and complex finish.

Food Pairing: Bistecca alla Fiorentina, roast lamb, wild boar ragù, mushroom dishes, and aged Pecorino cheese.

el-coto-875m-finca-carbonera-tempranillo.title: El Coto 875m Vinedos De Altura Tempranillo 2019 750ml
el-coto-875m-finca-carbonera-tempranillo.bodyHtml: The nose displays delicate aromas of cherries and red fruit alongside notes of coffee and cacao. The palate is fresh and intense with a good backbone of acidity, red fruit flavours and a long finish.

chateau-lalande-saint-julien.title: Chateau Lalande 2019
chateau-lalande-saint-julien.bodyHtml:
Château Lalande 2019 is an elegant, well-structured Left Bank red wine crafted by owner and winemaker Pierre Meffre in the Saint-Julien appellation of Bordeaux. Sourced from deep gravel soils adjacent to renowned Classified Growths, this blend of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot undergoes traditional fermentation followed by aging in French oak barrels. In the glass, it displays a deep ruby-purple color. The expressive nose features vibrant aromas of ripe cassis, black cherries, plum, cedar, graphite, and subtle baking spices. On the palate, it is medium- to full-bodied with a supple texture, delivering concentrated dark berry fruit underpinned by balanced natural acidity and fine-grained, structured tannins that extend into a long, harmonious finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with grilled ribeye steak, roasted rack of lamb, braised beef short ribs, duck breast, and aged hard cheeses.

93 Points - James Suckling

A delicious red with blackcurrant, walnut, mushroom and forest-floor character. Full-bodied, layered and chewy. Yet, it’s very attractive. Try after 2024.

93 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This estate, one of the relatively few in Saint-Julien that is not classified (and therefore good value), has produced a young and structured wine that is very much in the understated style of Saint-Julien. Its fruits and ripe tannins promise great things. Smoky and rich, the wine will be ready from 2026.

91 Points - Wine Spectator

Very expressive, with a forward display of warmed cassis, plum reduction and blackberry compote flavors, which are underscored by licorice root and menthol. Features a ganache coating on the finish, giving it a broad feel. Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot.

90 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Lalande is performing nicely in bottle, offering up aromas of cassis, dark berry fruit, loamy soil and cigar wrapper. Medium to full-bodied, layered and velvety, with lively acids and ripe tannins, it's a nicely balanced, characterful Saint-Julien that's already drinking well. Best After 2021.

la-pelle-ceniza-vineyard-cabernet.title: Peller Family Vineyards Cabernet Sauvignon 200mL
la-pelle-ceniza-vineyard-cabernet.bodyHtml:
Smooth and approachable, with blackberry, black currant, plum, dark cherry, and subtle spice. The palate is medium-bodied and fruit-forward, offering ripe dark fruit, soft tannins, balanced acidity, and a clean finish.

Food Pairing: Pair with grilled beef, burgers, barbecue, roast meats, hearty pasta, pizza, charcuterie, or semi-aged cheeses.

stolpman-so-fresh-love-you-bunches.title: Stolpman Vineyards Love You Bunches Sangiovese 2023 750ml
stolpman-so-fresh-love-you-bunches.bodyHtml: If you love carbonic maceration and you love Sangiovese, look no further than this seriously fruity expression of the grape. Just pull the cork and pour into the punch bowl. Red cherries, pomegranate, watermelon and juicy acidity.  The winery seems to have their feet firmly planted in both the past and the future with a line of both traditional wines and crushable reds.

r-stuart-co-big-fire-pinot-noir.title: R. Stuart & Co Big Fire Pinot Noir 2020 750ml
r-stuart-co-big-fire-pinot-noir.bodyHtml:
R. Stuart & Co Big Fire Pinot Noir 2020 750ml

AROMAS: cherry, sage, cranberry, red plum, wild strawberry, thyme, pine shavings, palo santo
FLAVORS: cranberry, plum, nutmeg, fresh fig, blood orange, raspberry, graphite, vanilla

roederer-estate-lermitage-2013.title: Roederer Estate L'Ermitage Brut 2013 750ml
roederer-estate-lermitage-2013.bodyHtml: Fine bubbles and creamy finish are the usual footprints of the L’Ermitage wine. Aromatics of hazelnut, brioche and flint create a mysterious and layered first contact. Mouthfeel is inviting quince jelly aromas and bright acidity with layered texture. Dosage is balanced with the acid and structure brought by the reserve wines from cask.

st-hallett-old-block-shiraz.title: Jacob'S Creek Heritage St. Hugo Shiraz 2020 750ml
st-hallett-old-block-shiraz.bodyHtml: Award tasting note: (2014 vintage) "Neatly and precisely structured, crunchy blackberry and black currant fruit, hint of sweet spice and liquorice and a hint of leafy freshness" - Silver, International Wine Challenge

chateau-lynch-bages-2018.title: Chateau Lynch-Bages 2018
chateau-lynch-bages-2018.bodyHtml:
Daring, innovative and with a reputation for often being the last to harvest, Jean-Charles Cazes defined the style of Lynch-Bages in the 1930's. The wine's distinctive character has earned it a place amongst Pauillac's greatest. It combines structure, finesse and elegance, offering generous aromas in its youth and developing deeper complexities with bottle age. The estate’s reputation as a top quality wine producer took off in 1945 after a series of exceptional vintages. Since then, Lynch-Bages has continued to produce excellent wines, even during years considered difficult in the Bordeaux region. The wine’s deep color and tannic backbone have become part of its signature style. Jean-Michel Cazes, grandson of Jean-Charles, has worked hard to develop and refine the wine’s supple and smooth structure over the years. Vintage after vintage, the estate’s precise and excellent winemaking techniques have served to firmly establish Lynch-Bages reputation for consistent quality.

97 Points - Wine Spectator

Vibrant, with a violet and cassis lead-in that then expands to include steeped black cherry and plum fruit as well as extra savory, iron and licorice root notes. Nice latent grip too, with a mouthwatering tug of earth at the very end. The fruit is so vibrant, it's a tease now, but there's structure here for the long haul, so be patient. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot. Best from 2025 through 2040.


97 Points -James Suckling

Aromas of blackberries, cloves, licorice, dried leaves, graphite and black olives. It’s full-bodied with firm, tight tannins. Structured and tannic with beautiful austerity and a long, mineral and layered finish. The tannins grow on the palate. Try from 2026.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast
The Lynch-Bages style is un mistakeable in this wine’s richness and the density of its structure and tannins. In addition it conveys a great sense of style, restrained power and opulence. Drink this wine from 2027.

96 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Composed of 72% Cabernet Sauvignon, 19% Merlot, 6% Cabernet Franc and 3% Petit Verdot, the 2018 Lynch-Bages was aged in 75% new barriques. Deep garnet-purple in color, it soars out of the glass with a magnificently expressive nose of blueberry compote, black cherry preserves and blackcurrant pastilles, plus suggestions of dark chocolate, licorice, tar and violets with a waft of hoisin. The medium to full-bodied palate is just as impactful as the nose, coating the mouth with juicy black berry and spicy layers, supported by firm, grainy tannin's and seamless freshness, finishing long with a refreshing earthiness coming through at the end.

chateau-haut-brion-2018.title: Chateau La Mission Haut Brion 2014
chateau-haut-brion-2018.bodyHtml:
Chateau La Mission Haut Brion is one of Bordeaux's greatest wines, revered for its extraordinary power, elegance, and longevity. Aromas of blackcurrant, blackberry, graphite, cedar, cigar box, violet, and exotic spice unfold into a concentrated palate with velvety tannins, exceptional depth, and a remarkably persistent finish.

Food Pairing: Pair with beef Wellington, roast lamb, venison, duck breast, truffle dishes, or aged Comte for an unforgettable Bordeaux experience.

 

96 Points - James Suckling

The typicity of La Mission is really here. Aromas of iodine, oyster shell, currants and orange peel are evident. Full-bodied, tight and tannic with a muscular and toned texture that holds the wine down at the moment, but it’s waiting to release its joy and true nature. Fine-grained. Give it until 2023.

95 Points - Decanter

Medium-bodied, fresh attack, dominated by late summer fruits, suggesting perfectly but not overly ripe fruit with great integrity. A floating, gossamer quality to the structure, the tannins are deceptively fine, yet they hold the wine together very tightly. You feel it on the finish, where blackberry and raspberry fruits are kept firmly in check. A lovely wine with medium- to long-term potential and great capacity to provide pleasure.

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2014 Château La Mission Haut-Brion is slightly more elegant and pretty compared to the richer, slightly more masculine Haut-Brion. A blend of 54% Merlot, 45% Cabernet Sauvignon and a splash of Cabernet Franc, it shows a kiss of red fruits in its core of darker currants, smoked tobacco, scorched earth, vanilla bean and spice-driven aromas and flavors. With medium- to full-bodied richness, impeccable balance, fine tannins and a great finish, it’s a downright classy La Mission that will benefit from 4–5 years of bottle age and keep for 20+ years.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2014 Château La Mission Haut-Brion is a blend of 54% Merlot, 1% Cabernet Franc and 45% Cabernet Sauvignon, picked between September 15 and October 8 and raised in 55% new oak. It has retained that engagingly fresh and vibrant bouquet, the bashful nature that it showed in barrel replaced by a more outgoing personality. This is an exquisite bouquet with pure black fruit, cold stone, a touch of black olive and later a suggestion of boysenberry preserve. The palate is still structured and, considering that a majority is Merlot, quite masculine. There remains some new oak to be fully assimilated, although there is clearly the fruit to soak that up. It comes more alive on the second half with a lovely spiciness and impressive persistence. It will have more to give down the line, and the strictness implies that this La Mission Haut-Brion should be afforded a decade in the cellar before it will show what it can do.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Richly endowed, the wine is beautifully concentrated. Still young, it has considerable potential with its rich fruits and firm tannins. There is a strongly juicy aftertaste that brings in the freshness of the year. The wine will age well and should not be drunk before 2026.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Fleshy and very compact, with layers of dark fig, black currant paste and blackberry reduction still sorting themselves out. Sports a serious spine of tar while a well-roasted apple wood element forms the backdrop on the dense finish. The range and density set this apart. Should be rather long-lived for the vintage. Best from 2020 through 2030.

shibumi-knoll-chardonnay.title: Beringer Luminus Oak Knoll Chardonnay 2022
shibumi-knoll-chardonnay.bodyHtml:
Beringer Luminus Oak Knoll Chardonnay 2022 is an exceptionally crisp, vibrant, and focused white wine sourced exclusively from the cool-climate Oak Knoll District in southern Napa Valley. Crafted by Beringer Vineyards, it presents aromas of citrus blossom, white peach, mandarin orange, and subtle baking spice with a touch of saline minerality. On the palate, it delivers a medium body, lively acidity, and layers of lemon curd, green apple, and almond notes, framed by a delicate touch of toasted oak and a smooth, lingering finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with pan-seared halibut, roasted chicken, crab cakes, butter-poached lobster, mushroom risotto, or creamy goat cheese dishes.

93 Points - James Suckling

Mandarin orange, quince and apple blossom with cheese rind, almonds, baking spices and a touch of saline minerality. Medium-bodied with very bright, crisp acidity. Beautiful harmony and freshness to it. Aged for eight months in 10% new French oak barrels. Drink now.

90 Points - Wine Spectator

Fragrant, sleek and juicy, showing pomelo, lime and pear flavors. Offers accents of fleur de sel and lemongrass, with a hint of orange blossoms. Drink now.

90 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Mouthwatering and flavorful, enlivening acidity in this wine wash the mouth with flavors of tropical fruit and lime pith. A chalky texture adds allure through a long finish.

shibumi-knoll-pinot-noir.title: Meiomi Pinot Noir 2022/2023
shibumi-knoll-pinot-noir.bodyHtml:
Meiomi Pinot Noir 2022 is a richly textured, opulent, and fruit-forward California red wine crafted from grapes sourced across premier coastal winegrowing regions, including Monterey, Sonoma, and Santa Barbara counties. Fermented using both punch-downs and pump-overs to ensure balanced extraction of color and flavor, the wine is aged for six months in 100% French oak barrels prior to final blending and bottling. In the glass, it displays a deep, luminous ruby-garnet hue. The aromatic bouquet opens with lifted notes of bright strawberry, dark cherry, and ripe raspberry layered with toasted vanilla, mocha, cedar, and warm baking spices. On the palate, it delivers a plush, medium-to-full-bodied mouthfeel marked by jammy red and dark berry flavors, gentle tannins, and subtle oak spice, culminating in a smooth, lingering, and off-dry finish.

Food Pairing: Grilled cedar-plank salmon, herb-roasted duck breast, wild mushroom risotto, roasted pork tenderloin, or soft triple-cream Brie and Camembert cheeses.
