Palate : Intense and warming with bold flavors of brown sugar, butterscotch, black pepper, clove, toasted almonds, and sweet oak char.

Finish : Long, robust, and lingering with notes of baking spice, sweet caramel, and drying oak tannins.

Serve : Serve neat in a Glencairn glass, allowing it to rest in the glass for a few minutes, or add a few drops of water to temper the proof and open up the complex aromatics.

omc-blair-athol-sherry.title: Omc Blair Athol - Sherry
omc-blair-athol-sherry.bodyHtml:
Hunter Laing Old Malt Cask Blair Athol 11 Year Old 2011 is a single cask Highland single malt Scotch whisky. It was distilled at Blair Athol in June 2011, matured in a single sherry butt and bottled in August 2022 by Hunter Laing & Co. of Glasgow for its Old Malt Cask series, yielding just 729 bottles. Each month Hunter Laing's tasting panel reviews the company's stocks and selects only the casks it judges to be at their best, and every Old Malt Cask release is bottled without chill filtration or added colouring so the character of the cask comes through. The blender's notes describe vanilla custard, apricot and honey on the nose, caramel over ginger sponge cake on the palate and a long toffee and brown sugar finish. Bottled at 50% ABV, 700ml, in the series' green tube.

Tasting Notes: Vanilla custard, apricot, honey, caramel, ginger, toffee.

Nose: Vanilla custard, apricot, honey.

Palate: Caramel over ginger sponge cake.

Finish: Long, with toffee and brown sugar.

Serve: Neat, then with a few drops of water.

omc-dailuaine-sherry.title: Douglas Laing & Co. Old Particular Midnight Series Dailuaine 2009 12 Year Old Sherry Butt Finish 57.3% ABV
omc-dailuaine-sherry.bodyHtml:
Douglas Laing Old Particular Midnight Series Dailuaine 2009 12 Year Old #DL15400 was distilled in 2009 and independently bottled by Douglas Laing as part of its Old Particular Midnight Series. Finished in a Sherry butt, it offers a rich, full-bodied profile of dark berries, dried fruit, chocolate and warming spices, complemented by the distillery's distinctive malty character. Bottled at 57.3% ABV without chill filtration or added colouring, this single-cask release is limited to just 270 bottles.

Food Pairing: Dark chocolate truffles, sticky toffee pudding, roasted pecans, aged Gouda, spiced fruitcake or slow-roasted beef.

Tasting Notes: Rich dark fruits, Sherry sweetness, warming spices, chocolate and malty depth, balanced by delicate oak and vanilla.

Nose: Blackberries, ripe plums, tobacco, freshly baked cake and aromatic baking spices.

Palate: Full-bodied and expressive, with raisins, currants, ginger, sweet barley, mocha, vanilla cream and dark berry compote.

Finish: Long and warming, with lingering dried fruits, chocolate, oak spice and gentle malt sweetness.

Serve: Enjoy neat in a Glencairn glass to appreciate its concentrated aromas. Add a few drops of water if desired.

omc-glen-moray.title: Omc Glen Moray
omc-glen-moray.bodyHtml:
Hunter Laing Old Malt Cask Glen Moray is a single malt Scotch whisky from Glen Moray Distillery in Speyside, bottled by Glasgow's Hunter Laing & Co. for its Old Malt Cask series. Old Malt Cask is one of the longest-standing names in single cask Scotch: every month the Hunter Laing tasting panel works through the company's stocks and picks out only the casks it judges to be ready. This release is bottled at 50% ABV and, like every new Old Malt Cask expression, is not chill filtered, so the individual character of the cask is preserved. It comes in a 700ml bottle.

Serve: Neat, or with a few drops of water.

cu-bocan-creation-3.title: Cù Bòcan Creation #3 Cabernet Sauvignon and Rye Casks
cu-bocan-creation-3.bodyHtml:
Cù Bòcan Creation #3 is a limited edition from Cù Bòcan, the lightly peated single malt produced at Tomatin Distillery in the Scottish Highlands. Cù Bòcan spirit is distilled every winter in small batches from lightly peated Scottish barley, and the Creation series exists to explore unusual cask combinations. For this third edition the whisky was matured in Moroccan Cabernet Sauvignon casks, which bring rose water, strawberry and black fig, and in North American rye casks, which push exotic spice, citrus and tropical fruit to the front. Launched in January 2022 together with Creation #4, it was limited to 4,200 bottles worldwide. Like the rest of the range it carries no age statement and is bottled at 46% ABV without chill filtration or added colour, in a 700ml bottle presented in its own box.

Food Pairing: Chef Tony Singh created a Punjabi-spiced salmon with warm herbed rice to match it.

Tasting Notes: Light smoke with strawberries in balsamic vinegar, exotic spice and citrus.

Serve: Neat, or with a few drops of water to open up the smoke and fruit.

cu-bocan-creation-4.title: Cù Bòcan Creation #4 Tawny Port and Cognac Casks
cu-bocan-creation-4.bodyHtml:
Cù Bòcan Creation #4 is a limited edition from Cù Bòcan, the lightly peated single malt produced at Tomatin Distillery in the Scottish Highlands. Each winter the distillery makes Cù Bòcan in small batches from lightly peated Scottish barley, and the Creation series is where it experiments with unusual casks. This fourth edition is a nod to the Antrim Cocktail, bringing together two of Europe's great drinks by maturing the whisky in tawny Port and Cognac casks. The result is a jammy, gently smoky dram with plum jam, grilled peach, stewed forest fruit, cinnamon and sweet campfire smoke. Released in January 2022 and limited to 4,200 bottles worldwide, it won Gold at the 2022 San Francisco World Spirits Competition. It carries no age statement and is bottled at 46% ABV, non-chill filtered and natural in colour, in a boxed 700ml bottle.

Food Pairing: Chef Tony Singh paired it with a damson jam and pistachio tart served with vanilla ice cream and cinnamon custard.

Tasting Notes: Plum jam, grilled peach, stewed forest fruit, cinnamon and sweet campfire smoke.

Serve: Neat, or with a splash of water.

opus-one-2017-magnum.title: Opus One 2017 1.5L Magnum
opus-one-2017-magnum.bodyHtml:
The Opus One 2017 offers a harmonious aromatic balance of rich dark fruit, stems of roses, and earthy forest floor. The juicy entry offers a round, silky mouthfeel with just enough acidity to complement the satin texture. This seductive wine shows flavors of black cassis, black cherry and a hint of cocoa powder. The fine-grained, plush tannins evolve into a long, supple finish.

96 Points - Decanter

A fist of late summer cherries, raspberry and bilberry fruits set out their stall, all with the juicy character that confirms, even in a hot vintage like 2017, Opus can deliver balance and sculpted elegance. Beautiful grip, creamy texture with a strikingly powerful tannic frame. As the wine stays in the glass the floral aromatics begin to bloom up. A brilliant Opus. 20 days maceration - around half what it would have been a decade ago. 54% native yeast, as part of their native yeast project. 5% Merlot and 1% Malbec complete the blend. Harvest spread out over September 5 to October 8, just before the fires, by which time they had less than 10% of the fruit still out on the vines.

95 Points - James Suckling

Lots of currant and floral notes on the nose. Hints of mint and spice. Medium-to full-bodied, round and savory with creamy, juicy tannins. Hints of citrus underneath. Bright, fresh and delicious. Drink or hold.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Opus One had picked 91% of their fruit before the fires started in 2017, and only two lots were eliminated from consideration. The 2017 Opus One, bottled in July 2019, is a blend of 81% Cabernet Sauvignon, 8.5% Petit Verdot, 5% Cabernet Franc, 4.5% Merlot and 1% Malbec. Medium to deep garnet-purple colored, it slowly grows on the nose, revealing compelling notes of baked black cherries, mulberries, black raspberries, warm cassis and blackberry pie with nuances of spice cake, yeast extract, tapenade, licorice and dusty soil with a waft of wild sage. Medium-bodied, the palate has a lively skip in its step, featuring bags of juicy raspberry and cassis-laced fruit and a refreshing line, supported by ripe, plush tannins, finishing long and graceful.


93 Points - Wine Spectator

This features currant and plum fruit, with tobacco, loam and singed savory notes, maintaining range and driving through the finish. The structure is fine-grained, delivering a lingering hint of acidity. A more subtle expression of Cabernet. Cabernet Sauvignon, Petit Verdot, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Malbec. Best from 2022 through 2036.

ch-citran.title: Chateau Citran 2010
ch-citran.bodyHtml:
A beautifully mature Haut-Médoc with aromas of cassis, blackberry, dried plum, cedar, tobacco, graphite, and earthy spice. Silky tannins, vibrant freshness, and refined complexity create an elegant Left Bank Bordeaux with a long, graceful finish.

Food Pairing: Pair with roast lamb, grilled ribeye, beef tenderloin, duck breast, aged Comté, Gruyère, or wild mushroom dishes.

 

90 Points - James Suckling

Aromas and flavors of orange peel, dried strawberries and subtle coffee notes define this expressive wine. Full-bodied with a chewy texture and well-integrated tannins, it finishes with elegance and balance. Already drinking beautifully, though it was recommended to enjoy from 2015 onward.

89 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Bright red fruit flavors lead the way in this elegant, approachable wine. Attractive tannins and a gentle, ripe character provide structure without excessive weight or power. Balanced and refined rather than overtly fruity, it benefits from 4–5 years of cellaring to reach its full potential.

ch-latour.title: Chateau Latour Les Forts de Latour 2019
ch-latour.bodyHtml:
The 2019 Les Forts de Latour is a powerhouse and a "jewel of a wine" that marks a significant milestone as the estate's first release fully certified organic and biodynamic. Produced with the same meticulous care as the Grand Vin, it originates from dedicated parcels outside the famed "Enclos". This vintage offers a complex bouquet of blackberries, cassis, and iris, interwoven with sophisticated notes of cedar, cigar box, and graphite. On the palate, it is full-bodied and velvety, featuring powerful yet ultrafine linear tannins and a mineral core of crushed stone. Aged in approximately 70% new French oak, it displays an extraordinary balance of tension and sapid freshness with a resonant, long-lasting finish.

97 Points - James Suckling

Exquisite aromas of lavender, cigar ash and Spanish cedar with dried citrus follow through to a medium body and a solid palate with powerful, ultrafine and linear tannins. The muscle and long finish are so beautiful. Give it two or three years but already a solid wine. Drink after 2028.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2019 Les Forts de Latour appears to have tightened up a little since I last tasted it a few years ago. Unwinding in the glass with aromas of sweet cassis fruit mingled with hints of cedar, iris, orange zest and new oak, it's medium to full-bodied, lively and nicely concentrated, with a ripe core of fruit underpinned by chalky structuring tannins. While it's approachable after a decant, it certainly merits additional patience. As readers will remember, this bottling mostly derives from dedicated parcels located further inland from Latour's famous "Enclos," next to Château Haut-Batailley.

y-yquem-blanc.title: Y de Chateau d'Yquem 2023
y-yquem-blanc.bodyHtml:
Y de Chateau d'Yquem 2023 is a sophisticated dry Bordeaux white showing grapefruit, lemon, white peach, fresh herbs, acacia, and subtle mineral notes. Vibrant and precise, the palate combines Sauvignon Blanc freshness with Semillon richness, delivering refined texture, impressive concentration, and a long, elegant finish.

Food Pairing: Pair with lobster, seared scallops, grilled turbot, roast chicken, creamy seafood dishes, or goat cheese for an elegant Bordeaux Blanc pairing.

pavillon-blanc-du-ch-margaux.title: Chateau Margaux Pavillon Rouge Du Chateau Margaux 2016 750ml
pavillon-blanc-du-ch-margaux.bodyHtml: Pavillon Rouge du Château Margaux 2016 is the second wine of Château Margaux, made since the 17th century and the oldest second wine in the Médoc; it has carried this name since the 1906 vintage. In 2016 only 26% of the harvest was selected for it, partly from plots that had been producing Château Margaux a few years earlier. The blend is 84% Cabernet Sauvignon, 13% Merlot and 3% Petit Verdot. A wet winter and spring were followed by a very dry summer, with only 8 mm of rain in July and August, and the red harvest, the most staggered in the estate's history, ran from 23 September to 18 October. The estate describes a dense, silky, vibrant and long tannic structure and advises a little more patience before opening. 750ml, 13.5% alcohol.

montes-wings-carmenere.title: Montes Wings Carmenere 2021 750ml
montes-wings-carmenere.bodyHtml:
The wine shows a deep red colour, with the purple undertones very characteristic of Carmenère. The intense nose reveals aromas of black fruit, such as blackberry and blueberry, accompanied by pleasing spice notes of bell pepper and black pepper, joined by sweet notes from the French oak barrels, delivering a very complex wine. The rounded palate of the wine shows extreme smoothness and potency, with a very long, pleasant finish.

91 Points - Wine Enthusiast 

Carménère grapes used in this blend grow over granite soils in the Apalta Valley. The resulting wine shows energy and tension on the palate. A bouquet of oak spices introduces pronounced red and black fruit, green bell pepper and toasted oak flavors. It has lively acidity and a long savory finish.

opus-one-2019a.title: Opus One Overture 2022
opus-one-2019a.bodyHtml: Overture 2022 captivates you from the start. Its aromatic profile weaves a complex tapestry of bright cherry, fresh forest berries, and cut rose stems interwoven with delicate scents of violets, toasted almond, and anise. Blackberry, blueberry, and wild cherry take the lead on the palate with a lively acidity that adds a vibrant edge. The finish is long and rounded, with a touch of mocha and black tea that showcase the wine’s depth. This expression of selected parcels from our estate vineyards will age gracefully for years to come.

j-p-wisers-collectors-series-hickory.title: J.P. Wiser's Collector's Series Smoked Oak & Maple
j-p-wisers-collectors-series-hickory.bodyHtml:
J.P. Wiser’s Collector’s Series Smoked Oak & Maple is a Canadian whisky expression built around rich oak character and maple-inspired sweetness. It combines classic Canadian whisky flavours with smoky wood, caramel, toffee and warming spice, creating a fuller and more robust profile than a traditional easy-drinking Canadian blend.

Food Pairing: Pairs well with smoked brisket, barbecue ribs, grilled steak, maple-glazed pork, aged cheddar, roasted nuts and dark chocolate.

Tasting Notes: Rich and warming with caramel, maple sweetness, toasted and smoky oak, dried fruit, toffee and rye spice.

Nose: Caramel, honeyed bread and orange blossom with toasted oak and subtle smoky notes.

Palate: Rich toffee and dried fruit with maple-like sweetness, oak and warming rye spice.

Finish: Warm and lingering with sweet oak, caramel and gentle spice.

Serve: Enjoy neat, over ice or in an Old Fashioned.

kaiyo-whiskey-the-single-7-year-old.title: Kaiyo 7 Year Old Mizunara Oak Japanese Whisky
kaiyo-whiskey-the-single-7-year-old.bodyHtml: This beautiful malt is made in Japan, double matured in aged bourbon barrels, and finished for 6 months on a rocking ship in Mizunara oak. The ship's motion extracts every bit of extra flavour from the extremely expensive Ariake Mizunara oak barrels. Made on a Coffey still, this malt drinks somewhere between Suntory's Toki and Nikka's Coffey Malt with the added complexity, fruitiness, and herbal notes of Mizunara oak.

old-forester-ps-barrel-strength.title: Old Forester Personal Selection Barrel Strength
old-forester-ps-barrel-strength.bodyHtml:
Consistency, balance, and above all, quality. That’s what drove our founder, George Garvin Brown, to seal Bourbon in a glass bottle – and sign his name to it as a personal guarantee – for the very first time way back in 1870.

Today, Old Forester remains the distinguished choice for those who appreciate authenticity in their Bourbon. Individuals who wish to share a special place in this legacy have an exclusive opportunity to select a single barrel of Old Forester for purchase and personalization through our unique Single Barrel program.

siempre-rebel-cask-northern-gold.title: Siempre Rebel Cask Reposado Tequila
siempre-rebel-cask-northern-gold.bodyHtml:
Siempre Rebel Cask Reposado Tequila is a limited-release, additive-free reposado tequila produced using wild-fermented 100% Blue Weber agave filled into casks at still strength. Aged for 5 to 11 months in unique, hand-selected barrels—such as ex-bourbon, Bordeaux Sauternes, and maple syrup casks—it delivers a rebellious, micro-batch profile that balances agave intensity with complex wood character.

Food Pairing: Roasted pork carnitas, grilled ribeye, smoked gouda, glazed figs, or dark chocolate desserts.

Tasting Notes : Golden amber to pale straw gold in appearance with a rich, complex, and full-bodied mouthfeel.

Nose : Earthy cooked agave and caramelized pears accompanied by warm baking spices, vanilla, oak, and subtle floral fruitiness.

Palate : Rich cooked agave, dried fruits, wet earth, baked bread, cinnamon, vanilla, and hints of toasted oak spice.

Finish : Long and lingering with a subtle fruit acidity, golden raisins, honey, and warm spicy oak.

Serve : Serve neat in a tulip glass or over a single large ice sphere.

g-m-discovery-glen-grant-11-year-old.title: Gordon & MacPhail Discovery Glen Grant 11 Year Old
g-m-discovery-glen-grant-11-year-old.bodyHtml:
Glen Grant Distillery is in the heart of the Speyside region of Scotland and is known for rich & fruity apple flavors. It is owned by the Italian company Campari so they serve great espresso at the distillery as well.

Discovery Series Bottling – Bourbon Matured

Brand Tasting Notes: Sweet and tropical fresh lemons and lime with coconut and mango. The palate is elderflower, grapefruit, and lightly charred oak with a gentle oak finish.

g-m-connoisseurs-choice-caol-ila-2008-c.title: Gordon & MacPhail Connoisseurs Choice Caol Ila 14 Year Old 2008 First Fill Sherry Butt Cask 312051 55.6% ABV
g-m-connoisseurs-choice-caol-ila-2008-c.bodyHtml:
Caol Ila 14 Year Old 2008 First Fill Sherry Butt Cask 312051 is a single cask Islay single malt from the Gordon & MacPhail Connoisseurs Choice range. Distilled on 18 June 2008, it spent its whole maturation in one first fill sherry butt before being bottled on 5 August 2022 at a natural cask strength of 55.6% ABV. The label records an outturn of 637 bottles, filled into 750 ml bottles without chill filtration and with no added colour. The first fill butt wraps the smoky Islay spirit in sherried dried fruit, nuts and spice.

Tasting Notes: Cured meat, stewed plum, Medjool date, toasted hazelnut, smoke.

Nose: Cured meat leading into stewed plum and festive spices.

Palate: Sweet Medjool date with toasted hazelnuts and demerara sugar.

Finish: Full and spicy, closing on bonfire embers.

Serve: Neat, then with a few drops of water to open it up at cask strength.

g-m-connoisseurs-choice-glen-grant-1998.title: Gordon & MacPhail Connoisseurs Choice Glen Grant 23 Year Old 1998 Refill Sherry Hogshead Cask 18605101 53.6% ABV
g-m-connoisseurs-choice-glen-grant-1998.bodyHtml:
NOSE

SHERRY aromas complement SULTANAS and DARK CHOCOLATE. FRUITCAKE aromas develop alongside Seville ORANGE PEEL and roasted COFFEE BEANS.

TASTE

Smooth flavours of stewed RED BERRIES and BAKED APPLE lead to subtle MINT LEAVES. CITRUS FRUIT comes to the fore accompanied by TREACLE TOFFEE.

FINISH

A medium-bodied and long finish with lingering toasted ALMONDS.

g-m-connoisseurs-highland-park-1995.title: Gordon & MacPhail Connoisseurs Choice Highland Park 27 Year Old 1995 Refill Sherry Butt Cask 1323 59% ABV
g-m-connoisseurs-highland-park-1995.bodyHtml: Stewed fruit combines with subtle ginger and cinnamon spice, with a hint of beeswax polish. Bitter orange and hazelnut lead to notes of chocolate raisins. Smooth, ripe plum notes infuse with festive spices balanced by cracked black pepper. Dried cherry comes to the fore alongside mature oak. Full and spicy with lingering citrus fruit and toffee.

g-m-connoisseurs-tomatin-2003.title: Gordon & MacPhail Connoisseurs Choice Tomatin 17 Year Old 2003 First Fill Bourbon Barrel 58.4% ABV
g-m-connoisseurs-tomatin-2003.bodyHtml: Created in 1968 by whisky visionary, George Urquhart, over the years this range has featured single malts from almost 100 Scottish distilleries. Comprising more than 2,000 individual bottlings, each Connoisseurs Choice tells its life story through its label: cask type, bottling date, strength, vintage and tasting note.

g-m-connoisseurs-choice-glenburgie-1990.title: Gordon & MacPhail Connoisseurs Choice Glenburgie 31 Year Old 1990 First Fill Sherry Butt Cask 12524 52.9% ABV
g-m-connoisseurs-choice-glenburgie-1990.bodyHtml: Stewed PLUM and Morello CHERRY give way to toasted HAZELNUT. CINNAMON spice aromas develop alongside soft DARK CHOCOLATE with a hint of POLISH. BLACK PEPPER flavours give way to Seville ORANGE and dried BANANA. TREACLE TOFFEE and BRAZIL NUT develop.

g-m-connoisseurs-choice-glentauchers-19.title: Dewar's Double Double 32 Year Old 375ml
g-m-connoisseurs-choice-glentauchers-19.bodyHtml:
Dewar's 32 Year Old Double Double is an exquisite, ultra-premium blended Scotch whisky crafted by Master Blender Stephanie Macleod using the brand's meticulous four-stage "Double Double" aging process. First, single malts and single grain whiskies are aged separately for at least 32 years. Next, the malts are blended together and rested, while the grains are blended and rested. In the third stage, the malt and grain blends are married together and rested once more. Finally, this expertly crafted blend undergoes a finishing period in exceptional Pedro Ximénez (PX) sherry casks. This incredibly demanding process results in a rich, deeply complex, and silky-smooth whisky characterized by intense notes of dark treacle, rich fruitcake, and decadent chocolate.

Food Pairing: Rich fruitcake, dark chocolate truffles, sticky toffee pudding, mature blue cheeses like Stilton or Roquefort, or roasted duck with a dark berry or plum reduction.

Tasting Notes : Deep, dark mahogany in appearance with an exceptionally viscous, rich, and velvety mouthfeel.

Nose : Intensely rich and decadent, bursting with aromas of dark treacle toffee, ripe peaches, dark chocolate, and heavy dried fruits like raisins and figs.

Palate : Luscious, sweet, and full-bodied, delivering complex layers of dark molasses, dense fruitcake, roasted nuts, vanilla, and the distinct, syrupy sweetness characteristic of Pedro Ximénez sherry casks.

Finish : Exceptionally long, sweet, and silky, leaving a lingering, warming impression of dark chocolate, dried dark fruits, and gentle oak spice.

Serve : Serve neat in a Glencairn glass or snifter to fully appreciate its depth and the luxurious texture created by the four-stage aging process.

g-m-connoisseurs-choice-miltonduff-1990.title: Gordon & MacPhail Connoisseurs Choice Miltonduff 31 Year Old 1990 First Fill Sherry Butt Cask 19440 54.6% ABV
g-m-connoisseurs-choice-miltonduff-1990.bodyHtml: Dark Toffee intertwines with orange oil and roasted coffee beans. Dark Chocolate comes to the fore accompanied by subtle marzipan and a hint of aged leather. Orange marmalade gives way to cinnamon and ginger spice. Raspberry licorice combines with stewed red fruit and spiced plums.

g-m-private-collection-highland-1984.title: Gordon & MacPhail Private Collection Highland Park 1984 46.3% ABV
g-m-private-collection-highland-1984.bodyHtml: Fragrant lemon aromas intertwine with honeydew melon and sweet Demerara sugar. Red apple notes develop accompanied by grapefruit zest and walnut. Citrus fruit flavours give way to guava and subtle cured meats. Dried mango comes to the fore alongside toasted almonds and spicy pepper.

g-m-connoisseurs-choice-balblair-1997.title: Gordon & MacPhail Connoisseurs Choice Balblair 24 Year Old 1997 Refill Sherry Hogshead Cask 1870 58.3% ABV
g-m-connoisseurs-choice-balblair-1997.bodyHtml:
Balblair 1997 24 Year Old is a single-cask Highland single malt from Gordon & MacPhail's Connoisseurs Choice range. Distilled at Balblair, one of Scotland's oldest distilleries, in 1997, it spent 24 years in refill sherry hogshead cask 1870 before being bottled at 58.3% ABV. This is a rich, fruity, old-school sherried style: fruitcake, ginger and clove on the nose with dried cherry, citrus zest and cocoa, then smooth stewed berries, apple, roasted coffee and toasted hazelnut with sweet clementine on the palate. The finish is full and long-lasting with mature oak and spice. 700ml.

Tasting Notes: Fruitcake, dried cherry, berries, coffee and oak spice.

Nose: Rich fruitcake with ginger and clove; dried cherry, citrus zest and a hint of cocoa.

Palate: Smooth stewed berries, apple and roasted coffee beans, with toasted hazelnut and sweet clementine.

Finish: Full and long, with mature oak and spice.

Serve: Neat, or with a few drops of water.

g-m-connoisseurs-choice-glen-scotia-200.title: Gordon & MacPhail Connoisseurs Choice Glen Scotia 22 Year Old 2000 Refill American Oak Hogshead Cask 325 56.9% ABV
g-m-connoisseurs-choice-glen-scotia-200.bodyHtml:
Glen Scotia 22 Year Old 2000 Refill American Oak Hogshead Cask 325 is a single cask Campbeltown single malt from the Gordon & MacPhail Connoisseurs Choice range. Distilled at Glen Scotia in 2000, it spent 22 years in a single refill American oak hogshead before being bottled at 56.9% ABV in a 700 ml bottle. The gentle refill cask leaves the spirit in charge: bright citrus and tropical fruit with honey and an oily texture.

Tasting Notes: Lemon zest, green apple, mango, pineapple, honeydew, coconut, lime.

Nose: Bright lemon zest, ripe green apple and tropical fruit, with light honey and a little milk chocolate.

Palate: Sweet pineapple and mango against cracked black pepper, then honeydew melon, desiccated coconut and mature oak.

Finish: Full, sweet and creamy, with fresh lime.

Serve: Neat or with a splash of water.

g-m-connoisseurs-choice-linkwood-2001.title: Gordon & MacPhail Connoisseur's Choice Linkwood 2001 54.7% ABV

benromach-single-cask-2012-bbarrel.title: Benromach Single Cask 2012 Bourbon Barrel
benromach-single-cask-2012-bbarrel.bodyHtml:
Benromach Single Cask 2012 Bourbon Barrel is a single-cask Speyside single malt from the Benromach distillery, a Gordon & MacPhail property since 1993. Distilled in 2012 and matured in a single bourbon barrel, it was bottled at 59.3% ABV in a 700ml bottle.

Serve: Neat, with a few drops of water to soften the strength.

jadot-hospices-1er-dames-hospitalieres-1.title: Hospices de Beaune  Premier Cru Cuvée Dames Hospitalieres 2017 3L Double Magnum
jadot-hospices-1er-dames-hospitalieres-1.bodyHtml: This is a Burgundy red wine, typically Beaune 1er Cru, known for its floral nose, fruity palate with subtle tannins, and ability to pair well with cured meat, red meat, and game. This particular cuvée is a tribute to the nuns who cared for the sick at the Hospices de Beaune, and it's often the first cuvée auctioned during the annual wine auction. It's known for its balance of suppleness and robustness, and its inclusion of vineyards like Bressandes, Teurons, and the Clos de la Mignotte, which contribute to its unique character.

jadot-hospices-1er-cru-nicolas-rolin.title: Hospices de Beaune Nicolas Rolin Premier Cru 2022 3L Double Magnum
jadot-hospices-1er-cru-nicolas-rolin.bodyHtml: The robustness of Climat des Cent Vignes is a fitting tribute to the Hospices co-founder's Nicolas Rolin's memory. This deep terroir anchors the cuvée in the register of power and generosity. Its structure is completed by the Teurons and their rocky marls, which lighten it with their minerality. Together, in a lesser proportion, the Grèves, Genêts and Bressandes build a refined attack and finesse on the finish.

glenallachie-21-yo-batch-3.title: The GlenAllachie 21 Year Old Batch 2
glenallachie-21-yo-batch-3.bodyHtml:
Pedro Ximenéz barrels were selected from The GlenAllachie Distillery's premium collection, which contains 50,000 barrels. After maturing, the whiskey was filled into bottles with 51.1 % alcohol content. No added dye and cold filtration. We recommend serving at room temperature to enhance the excellent aroma and amazing taste.

This is a limited special edition, which means that only 1,600 bottleshave been produced! Whisky comes in an exclusive blue-gold gift boxwith a book-style opening.

a-d-rattray-cask-orkney-15-yo.title: A.D. Rattray Cask Orkney 15 Year Old
a-d-rattray-cask-orkney-15-yo.bodyHtml:
Cask Orkney 15 Year Old single malt scotch whisky matured in ex-bourbon casks. Created to celebrate the Neolithic folklore of Orkney, it captures the island spirit with a deeply engaging and perfectly balanced malt.

Tasting Notes

Colour: Butterscotch gold.
Nose: Clover honey, Parma violet, ripe peach and wild heather embers.
Palate: Grilled plum, old-fashioned barley sugar, noble hop and caraway.
Finish: A prolonged peppery smoke lifted by tart citrus and foraged pine.

Subtle smoke, stone fruit and spice.

ole-smoky-salty-caramel-whiskey.title: Ole Smoky Salty Caramel Whiskey
ole-smoky-salty-caramel-whiskey.bodyHtml: Might be the best thing to happen to whiskey since, well, whiskey. Savor every sip of this blend of rich, sweet 60 proof whiskey that tastes like liquid caramel with a hint of salt at the end of it. Whiskey never tasted so decadent.

two-stacks-blenders-cut-batch-2.title: Two Stacks Blenders Cut Batch 2 Irish Whiskey
two-stacks-blenders-cut-batch-2.bodyHtml:
Two Stacks The Blender's Cut Batch 2 is the cask strength version of the Two Stacks complex blend, marrying grain, malt and pot still Irish whiskey. First released in 2020, The Blender's Cut set out to show that a blended Irish whiskey at full cask strength can offer the depth usually associated with single cask bottlings. This batch is bottled at 64% ABV in a 700ml bottle and works neat, over ice or in a stirred cocktail.

Tasting Notes: Caramel, dark fruit, honey, dark chocolate and pepper.

Nose: Rich caramel, dark fruit, spice and oak.

Palate: Intense and full-bodied, with honey, dark chocolate and peppery spice.

Finish: Long, warming and complex.

Serve: Neat with a splash of water, or over ice.

bombay-sapphire-gift-box.title: Bombay Sapphire London Dry Gin 1.14L
bombay-sapphire-gift-box.bodyHtml:
Bombay Sapphire London Dry Gin is an iconic, world-renowned gin crafted using a proprietary vapor-infusion process. First created in 1987 based on an 1761 recipe, ten sustainably sourced botanicals are held separately from the spirit in perforated copper baskets and infused with hot spirit vapor, yielding a delicate, bright, and perfectly balanced botanical profile.

Food Pairing: Fresh oysters, smoked salmon, seafood tapas, goat cheese crostini, lemon tarts, or sushi.

Tasting Notes : Crystal clear and luminous in appearance with a smooth, light, and crisp mouthfeel.

Nose : Fresh juniper, bright citrus, floral notes, subtle pine, and warm earthy spices.

Palate : Clean, balanced, and round with vibrant juniper berries, zesty lemon, peppery coriander, subtle liquorice, and almond sweetness.

Finish : Medium, crisp, and refreshing with lingering hints of citrus zest and gentle spice.

Serve : Serve as the foundational spirit in a classic Gin & Tonic with fresh lime, in a Dry Martini, or over ice with tonic water.

moet-chandon-brut-i-love-you.title: Moet & Chandon Imperial Brut
moet-chandon-brut-i-love-you.bodyHtml:
Moët & Chandon Impérial Brut is the iconic flagship non-vintage Champagne of the historic Épernay house, first created in 1869. Crafted from an assemblage of more than 100 individual wines—including 20% to 30% specially selected reserve wines—it draws fruit from nearly 280 crus across Champagne to ensure consistent complexity, maturity, and balance. Composed of 30% to 40% Pinot Noir for body, 30% to 40% Meunier for suppleness, and 20% to 30% Chardonnay for finesse, it is aged on the lees and finished with a dosage of 7 g/L. In the glass, it displays a luminous golden straw-yellow color with green highlights and a fine, persistent mousse. The aromatic bouquet opens with vibrant notes of green apple and citrus layered with white flowers, mineral nuances, and warm brioche, cereal, and fresh nuts. On the palate, it combines sumptuous white-fleshed fruits—pear, peach, and apple—with lively citrus acidity and subtle hints of gooseberry, leading to a crisp, harmonious finish.   Food Pairing: Fresh oysters, seared scallops, sushi and sashimi, herb-roasted chicken, lobster with drawn butter, or soft triple-cream Brie cheese.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

An elegant version, fine and creamy in texture and backed by lively, orange peel acidity. A streak of smoke-tinged minerality underscores flavors of almond madeleine, poached pear, anise and preserved lemon. Pinot Noir, Pinot Meunier and Chardonnay.

90 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This Champagne gets better and better. It has a fine dryness with a crisp apple and citrus character. That goes with the touches of maturity that give the wine fine balance.

90 Points - James Suckling

Nicely complex aromas here, from dried apples, peaches and pears to candied citrus and brioche. It’s fruity, soft and rounded on the palate. Medium-bodied, lightly honeyed and balanced. Blend of pinot noir, pinot meunier and chardonnay.

moet-chandon-rose-i-love-you.title: Moet & Chandon Nectar Imperial Rose 750ml
moet-chandon-rose-i-love-you.bodyHtml: Nectar Impérial Rosé brings its savvy and vibrant style to create a unique night experience. Moët & Chandon decided to come up with a new cuvée, intense and fruity, perfect for nightlife.

cognac-lot-75-gc-le-chef.title: Malternative #16 'Le Roi de l'Automne' Laurichesse Lot 75 1975 Grande Champagne Cognac

cognac-lot-48-gc.title: Vallein Tercinier Lot 96 1996 Grande Champagne Cognac
cognac-lot-48-gc.bodyHtml: Vallein Tercinier Lot 96 1996 Grande Champagne Cognac is an exceptional, highly sought-after "Brut de Fût" (cask strength) expression from the fiercely traditional, independent Vallein Tercinier family estate. Distilled in 1996 exclusively from Ugni-Blanc grapes grown in the premier Grande Champagne cru, this single cask cognac (Cask #218) was patiently matured in French oak for over two and a half decades before being bottled in 2023 at a natural, unreduced 49.7% ABV. Yielding just 614 bottles worldwide and presented completely free of chill-filtration or added caramel coloring, it beautifully showcases the house's signature purity and elegant precision. The nose is wonderfully expressive, bursting with bright melon, fresh peaches, sweet lime blossom, and rich waves of honey drops and old Sauternes wine. On the palate, it delivers a masterclass in balance, offering a vibrant, fruit-forward profile packed with flambéed bananas, mirabelle plums, and muscovado sugar, beautifully accented by a touch of soft violet and delicate liquorice. The finish is remarkably long and chiseled, leaving lingering traces of golden syrup, bruised apples, sultanas, and gentle French oak.

chicken-cock-kentucky-straight-bourbon.title: Chicken Cock Chanticleer Cognac Barrel Finish Bourbon
chicken-cock-kentucky-straight-bourbon.bodyHtml:
Chanticleer celebrates the long time French-American friendship dating back to the 1700’s and to Paris, Kentucky where Chicken Cock was founded in 1856. Sealed in a prohibition era collectible tin, this Kentucky Straight Bourbon finished in fine French Cognac casks has vibrant notes of ripened peaches with tannic bursts of vanilla and cherry.

 

NOSE

Vibrant notes of ripened peaches, delicate sweet cream, and succulent honey.

PALATE

Tannic bursts of vanilla and cherry complimented by softened plums, candied dates, and banana flambe.

FINISH

Hot caramelized sugar, melted butter, and fresh citrus zest.

chicken-cock-cotton-club-rye.title: Chicken Cock 20 Year Old Cotton Club Rye
chicken-cock-cotton-club-rye.bodyHtml: Originally established in Paris, Kentucky in 1856, Chicken Cock was forced to move production up to Canada during Prohibition. The Canadian Rye whiskey produced during that period was then smuggled back into the U.S. in tin cans, earning the brand the nickname, “The whiskey in a tin can.

chicken-cock-island-rooster-rye.title: Chicken Cock Island Rooster Rum Barrel Rye
chicken-cock-island-rooster-rye.bodyHtml: Island Rooster is a limited edition Kentucky Straight Rye finished in rum barrels. Inspired by a trip to the Caribbean, where roosters announce the coming day, we decided to finish 25 barrels of our Signature Kentucky Straight Rye Whiskey in Caribbean rum casks. The result is a relaxing blend of spicy notes from the rye with candied molasses notes from the rum barrels. Sun and sand meets the Bluegrass state.

komos-reposado-rosa-tequila.title: Komos Reposado Rosa Tequila
komos-reposado-rosa-tequila.bodyHtml: Komos Reposado Rosa starts with the special blanco base, then rests for 65 days in French oak red wine barrels to age and soften it as it evolves delicate flavors. The rich, unique rosé color is naturally derived from grape skins, reminiscent of a French rosé.

komos-anejo-cristalino-tequila.title: Komos Añejo Cristalino Tequila
komos-anejo-cristalino-tequila.bodyHtml: Komos Anejo Cristalino expression begins with the blanco base which is aged in French oak white wine barrels for 12 months, rather than traditional American bourbon barrels. The now-anejo tequila is refined gently with charcoal filtration, removing impurities while maintaining rich barrel notes, creating a perfectly smooth Anejo Cristalino.

komos-extra-anejo-tequila.title: Komos Extra Anejo Tequila
komos-extra-anejo-tequila.bodyHtml: <meta charset="UTF-8">Komos Extra Anejo is aged for a minimum of three years in a combination of French oak white wine barrels and American oak whiskey barrels. The richness of American oak is masterfully blended with the refinement of French oak, creating an opulent, beautifully complex Extra Anejo.

star-of-bombay.title: Star of Bombay London Dry Gin
star-of-bombay.bodyHtml:
Star of Bombay London Dry Gin is a super-premium, small-batch expression from Bombay Sapphire, produced entirely at the Bombay Sapphire Distillery at Laverstoke Mill in Hampshire, England, and bottled at 47.5% ABV in a 750ml bottle. Master Distiller Nik Fordham created it as a fresh interpretation of the Bombay house style, inspired by the then-new distillery and its Thomas Heatherwick-designed glasshouses. The gin is slowly distilled, and alongside the ten Bombay Sapphire botanicals it uses two more: bergamot orange peel from Calabria in southern Italy and ambrette seed from Ecuador. It was presented in a modern, finely detailed bottle and has since been discontinued, so remaining bottles are of interest to collectors as well as drinkers.

Serve: In a gin and tonic garnished with a thin strip of orange peel.

the-kraken-gold-spiced-rum-1.title: The Kraken Gold Spiced Rum 1.14L
the-kraken-gold-spiced-rum-1.bodyHtml: The Kraken's deep and watery keep is said to be filled with the only thing it loves more than darkness - gold. Oh, and rum. Obviously. Kraken Gold Spiced Rum, a Caribbean spiced rum from the Dominican Republic, aged for two years with hints of vanilla and cinnamon, rich beyond words and perhaps the only bit of lightness the beast loves with as much passion as its storied black ink.

inglenook-cabernet-2015.title: Inglenook 1882 Cabernet Sauvignon 2018
inglenook-cabernet-2015.bodyHtml:
Inglenook 1882 Cabernet Sauvignon 2018 is a classic, expressive, and historic Napa Valley red wine crafted to honor Gustave Niebaum’s inaugural vintage at Inglenook. Sourced from organically farmed estate vineyard blocks—including Chateau, Cohn, and Red Barn—rooted in the deep, gravelly loam soils of the Rutherford Bench, it displays a deep garnet-red hue in the glass. The aromatic profile is inviting and nuanced, revealing aromas of ripe black cherries, macerated plums, and fresh cassis layered over undertones of dark cocoa powder, cedar, sweet pipe tobacco, and subtle baking spices derived from 18 months of aging in French oak. On the palate, it is full-bodied, vibrant, and supple, delivering a solid core of juicy dark fruits framed by refined, fine-grained "Rutherford dust" tannins and balanced natural acidity, concluding in a structured, long, and lightly spiced finish.

Food Pairing: Grilled prime ribeye steak, roasted rack of lamb, braised beef short ribs, rosemary venison medallions, and aged white cheddar or gouda cheese.

94 Points - James Suckling

A solid cabernet with lots of blackberry, chocolate and walnut character. It's full-bodied with plenty of fruit and a flavourful finish. Juicy and intense. Needs time to soften and mellow.

inglenook-rubicon-2013.title: Inglenook Rubicon 2013 750ml
inglenook-rubicon-2013.bodyHtml: The 2013 Inglenook Rubicon is a Napa Valley Bordeaux blend, primarily Cabernet Sauvignon, known for its expressive character and quality. It offers aromas of cherries, black currants, and dark chocolate, with notes of oak, toast, and floral hints. The palate features dark berries, cassis, and smoky wood, with evolving nuances of tobacco and spices. This vintage is described as having fine tannins and a balanced acidity, resulting in a long, fresh finish, with the potential for further development.

malibu-coconut-flavoured-liquor.title: Malibu Coconut Rum Liqueur 1.75L
malibu-coconut-flavoured-liquor.bodyHtml:
Malibu Coconut Rum Liqueur is a globally renowned, exceptionally smooth, and sweetness-forward white rum-based liqueur that stands as the world's definitive tropical spirit. Originally conceived in 1978 to simplify the process of making Piña Coladas for bartenders, this iconic expression blends high-quality Caribbean white rum with natural coconut extracts and pure sugar. The base rum is expertly distilled from sugarcane molasses, traditionally utilizing continuous multi-column stills to capture a clean, light, and highly mixable profile. With its signature low proof and creamy, sun-kissed coconut flavor, Malibu functions as an effortless, sweet-tempered modifier that instantly infuses any beverage with a vibrant, laid-back summer identity.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with spicy jerk chicken, crispy coconut shrimp, fresh mango and pineapple skewers, key lime pie, or a rich bittersweet dark chocolate bark.

TASTING NOTES - A crystal-clear appearance with a light, silky, and syrupy body that coats the palate smoothly with no perceptible alcohol burn.

NOSE - Sweet and highly aromatic, bursting with dominant notes of creamy coconut milk, whipped cream, and vanilla bean, underpinned by a faint hint of warm sugarcane.

PALATE - Soft, unctuous, and approachable on the arrival, delivering an immediate wave of natural coconut sweetness and rich vanilla fudge, supported by a gentle, clean white rum warmth.

FINISH - Relatively short, clean, and refreshing, resolving smoothly with a lingering fade of sweet shredded coconut, light brown sugar, and a mild, soothing tropical heat.

SERVE - Exceptionally versatile; best served chilled or over crushed ice as a premium modifier in iconic tropical cocktails like the Piña Colada, Malibu Sunrise, or simply mixed with fresh pineapple juice or ginger ale.

koval-bourbon.title: Koval Single Barrel Bourbon 200ml
koval-bourbon.bodyHtml:
A fantastic 200ml tasting size of Koval's award-winning signature bourbon! Unlike traditional bourbons that use rye or wheat as the secondary grain, Koval uses an entirely organic mash bill of 51% corn and 49% millet (an ancient, gluten-free grain). Aged in heavily charred new oak and bottled at 94 proof, this single barrel release delivers a highly approachable, naturally sweet, and incredibly unique flavor profile that sets it distinctly apart from Kentucky bourbons.

 

NOSE

Bright and sweet with aromas of mango chutney, creamy vanilla, and a hint of toasted apricot.

PALATE

Soft and mellow, featuring rich flavors of caramel, vanilla custard, peppery spice, and sweet candied fruit.

FINISH

Clean, smooth, and sweet with a lingering gentle warmth and a touch of tobacco.

chateau-la-mission-haut-brion-rouge.title: Chateau La Mission Haut Brion 2014
chateau-la-mission-haut-brion-rouge.bodyHtml:
Chateau La Mission Haut Brion is one of Bordeaux's greatest wines, revered for its extraordinary power, elegance, and longevity. Aromas of blackcurrant, blackberry, graphite, cedar, cigar box, violet, and exotic spice unfold into a concentrated palate with velvety tannins, exceptional depth, and a remarkably persistent finish.

Food Pairing: Pair with beef Wellington, roast lamb, venison, duck breast, truffle dishes, or aged Comte for an unforgettable Bordeaux experience.

 

96 Points - James Suckling

The typicity of La Mission is really here. Aromas of iodine, oyster shell, currants and orange peel are evident. Full-bodied, tight and tannic with a muscular and toned texture that holds the wine down at the moment, but it’s waiting to release its joy and true nature. Fine-grained. Give it until 2023.

95 Points - Decanter

Medium-bodied, fresh attack, dominated by late summer fruits, suggesting perfectly but not overly ripe fruit with great integrity. A floating, gossamer quality to the structure, the tannins are deceptively fine, yet they hold the wine together very tightly. You feel it on the finish, where blackberry and raspberry fruits are kept firmly in check. A lovely wine with medium- to long-term potential and great capacity to provide pleasure.

95 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2014 Château La Mission Haut-Brion is slightly more elegant and pretty compared to the richer, slightly more masculine Haut-Brion. A blend of 54% Merlot, 45% Cabernet Sauvignon and a splash of Cabernet Franc, it shows a kiss of red fruits in its core of darker currants, smoked tobacco, scorched earth, vanilla bean and spice-driven aromas and flavors. With medium- to full-bodied richness, impeccable balance, fine tannins and a great finish, it’s a downright classy La Mission that will benefit from 4–5 years of bottle age and keep for 20+ years.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2014 Château La Mission Haut-Brion is a blend of 54% Merlot, 1% Cabernet Franc and 45% Cabernet Sauvignon, picked between September 15 and October 8 and raised in 55% new oak. It has retained that engagingly fresh and vibrant bouquet, the bashful nature that it showed in barrel replaced by a more outgoing personality. This is an exquisite bouquet with pure black fruit, cold stone, a touch of black olive and later a suggestion of boysenberry preserve. The palate is still structured and, considering that a majority is Merlot, quite masculine. There remains some new oak to be fully assimilated, although there is clearly the fruit to soak that up. It comes more alive on the second half with a lovely spiciness and impressive persistence. It will have more to give down the line, and the strictness implies that this La Mission Haut-Brion should be afforded a decade in the cellar before it will show what it can do.

95 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Richly endowed, the wine is beautifully concentrated. Still young, it has considerable potential with its rich fruits and firm tannins. There is a strongly juicy aftertaste that brings in the freshness of the year. The wine will age well and should not be drunk before 2026.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Fleshy and very compact, with layers of dark fig, black currant paste and blackberry reduction still sorting themselves out. Sports a serious spine of tar while a well-roasted apple wood element forms the backdrop on the dense finish. The range and density set this apart. Should be rather long-lived for the vintage. Best from 2020 through 2030.

chateau-cheval-blanc.title: Chateau Cheval Blanc 2016
chateau-cheval-blanc.bodyHtml:
Chateau Cheval Blanc is a Saint-Emilion Grand Cru red centered on Cabernet Franc and Merlot. Its distinctive gravel and clay terroir contributes freshness, elegance, power, and finesse, while precise parcel-by-parcel vinification creates a complex, balanced expression combining aromatic refinement, structured depth, and exceptional aging potential.

Food Pairing: Pairs best with roasted lamb loin, beef tenderloin, duck breast, or braised short ribs.

100 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

Deep garnet-purple in color, with intense red currant, black cherry, wild blueberry, violet, star anise, cinnamon, cigar box, and smoky notes. The palate shows exceptional elegance and depth, layered red and black fruit, mineral character, firm grainy texture, and an extraordinarily persistent, perfumed finish.

99 Points - James Suckling

Wet earth, fresh mushroom, menthol, blackberry, and blueberry aromas lead into a full-bodied, dense, structured palate. Powerful tannins are remarkably integrated, with detailed definition, a cashmere-like texture, and a long, polished finish.

97 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Rich and smoky, with powerful fruit and an impressive perfumed character. Spice and blackberry notes combine with substantial tannins, providing firmness, structure, and excellent aging potential.

97 Points - Wine Spectator

A highly structured and refined expression with concentrated fruit, firm tannins, freshness, and considerable length, showing the depth and balance expected from the 2016 vintage.

lobos-1707-mezcal.title: Lobos 1707 Mezcal Artesanal
lobos-1707-mezcal.bodyHtml: In a league of its own, Lobos 1707 Mezcal Artesanal is gradual, smoky and sultry. Each sip conjures its epic past: created from 100% Espadín agave, roasted in an open, conical Oaxacan fire pit, then ground in an Egyptian stone mill, resulting in a stealthily smooth liquid whose flavor experience is deep, affecting, and will leave its mark with the subtle warmth of spice. For Mezcal lovers and rookies alike.

deau-cognac-vs.title: Deau VS Cognac
deau-cognac-vs.bodyHtml:
Deau VS Cognac is the Very Special expression of the Deau range from La Distillerie des Moisans. It is made from eaux-de-vie distilled by the traditional Charentais pot-still method, drawn from good crus of the Cognac region and aged slowly in the house cellars for about two years; it is made from Ugni Blanc grapes. The cellar master blends it for freshness, roundness and liveliness, and the producer presents it as soft and harmonious, with intense aromatic freshness. Deau reports that its VS Collection won a silver medal at French Spirits for Asia in 2013. It is bottled at 40% ABV in a 700ml bottle and is meant above all for long drinks.

Tasting Notes: Fresh and aromatic, floral and fruity.

Nose: Vine flower, peach and citrus with white-wood freshness.

Palate: A soft, fresh attack on elegant oak, moving to orchard fruit.

Finish: Supple and soft.

Serve: As a long drink with tonic or ginger ale, or in cocktails.

cazadores-extra-anejo-1.title: Cazadores Extra Anejo Tequila
cazadores-extra-anejo-1.bodyHtml:
Cazadores Extra Añejo Tequila is an ultra-premium, 100% blue agave tequila produced in the Highlands of Jalisco, Mexico. Double-fermented and double-distilled, it is aged for at least three years in virgin American white oak barrels, creating a deeply rich profile filled with notes of sweet agave, vanilla, dried fruit, and toasted wood.

Food Pairing: Grilled ribeye steak, dark chocolate, slow-roasted pork carnitas, aged cheeses, or churros.

Tasting Notes : Deep reddish-gold with amber highlights, featuring a full-bodied, smooth, and velvety mouthfeel.

Nose : Roasted agave, sweet vanilla, dark caramel, dried fruit, cinnamon, and rich oak.

Palate : Complex and smooth with notes of toasted oak, sweet vanilla, roasted agave, dark chocolate, and subtle nutmeg.

Finish : Warm, long, and smooth with lingering notes of sweet wood, caramel, and baking spices.

Serve : Serve neat or over a large ice cube in a tasting glass or snifter.

domaine-henri-magnien-cazetiers-magnum.title: Caymus Special Selection Cabernet Sauvignon 2019 3L Double Magnum
domaine-henri-magnien-cazetiers-magnum.bodyHtml:
The Caymus 'Special Selection' Cabernet Sauvignon is an exceptional wine made from this storied Napa Valley estate. Following some time to open, this incredible Cabernet begins to yield profound aromatics of black cherry compote, blueberry pie and boysenberry along with creosote, black tar, milk chocolate and licorice all soaring from the glass. The mouthfeel is rich, voluptuous and intense, as this wine offers exceedingly dense, concentrated flavors of black cherry reduction, blueberry pie, raspberry liquor and boysenberry, alongside milk chocolate shavings and tar, all cascading on to the long mouth coating finish.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

Lush and polished, with waves of cassis and blackberry compote pouring through, underscored by chocolate, espresso crema and roasted vanilla bean. Maintains a lush, velvety feel through the lengthy finish, where flashes of sweet tobacco and warm earth peek through. For the power Cabernet crowd. Best from 2024 through 2038.

 

92 Points - CellarTracker

vodkow-orange-cream.title: Bartenders Trading Co Awesome Orange Cream Cocktail
vodkow-orange-cream.bodyHtml: Awesome Orange is a zesty blast of sweet orange flavor, with a silky layer of real dairy cream, and the intensely smooth finish of premium vodka.

drouhin-saint-veran.title: Joseph Drouhin Saint-Veran 2022
drouhin-saint-veran.bodyHtml:
A wine that smiles and makes you smile. It is stylistically close to Pouilly-Fuissé, with its golden hue, its greenish reflection and its refreshing taste. The aromas are reminiscent of the ripe Chardonnay grape, with subtle notes of musk. A pleasant roundness coats the palate.

91 Points - Wine Spectator

Peach and melon fruit is offset by a bitter citrus note in this tense, well-structured white. An intense version, with hints of wild herbs and a stony feel on the finish.

glencadam-american-oak-res-bourbon.title: Glencadam American Oak Reserve
glencadam-american-oak-res-bourbon.bodyHtml:
Glencadam American Oak Reserve is matured exclusively in hand-selected premium quality American oak ex-bourbon barrels sourced by our Master Distiller from Kentucky, USA.

Scoring an impressive 98 points out of 100 at the 2022 International Wine & Spirits Competition, Glencadam American Oak Reserve is the perfect introduction to the Glencadam range of premium single malt Scotch whiskies highlighting the delicate yet complex, smooth, sweet, tropical and orchard fruit style of Glencadam Single Malt.

tomintoul-speyside-single-malt-10-yr.title: Tomintoul 10 Year Old
tomintoul-speyside-single-malt-10-yr.bodyHtml:
Matured exclusively in hand selected American oak ex-bourbon barrels. Tomintoul 10 Years Old is a delicate well-balanced single malt with honey and citrus combing to create a sweet, fruity and vanilla flavour profile.

A fan favourite in the Tomintoul range, our 10 Years Old has been awarded gold medals for its taste by  some of the most prestigious spirits competitions in the world.

tomintoul-speyside-white-port-finish.title: Tomintoul White Port Cask Finish
tomintoul-speyside-white-port-finish.bodyHtml:
Master Distiller, Robert Fleming, created this small batch bottling by specially selecting Tomintoul aged in exceptional ex-bourbon American oak barrels, which are then married & finished in hand selected White Port barriques from Portugal.

The process of ‘finishing’ creates a beautifully rich, complex & full flavoured single malt scotch whisky.

tomintoul-17-yo-pedro-ximenez-sherry-cas.title: Tomintoul 17 Year Old 2005 Pedro Ximénez Sherry Cask Finish
tomintoul-17-yo-pedro-ximenez-sherry-cas.bodyHtml:
Tomintoul which has been given fantastically sherried finish. Distilled in 2005, this Speyside single malt matured for 17 years and was finished in PX sherry butts selected from renowned producers, Fernando de Castilla. Non-chill filtered, 9,870 bottles were produced of this limited edition whisky.

Tasting Note 

Nose: Fruity and spicy, with cinnamon, candied citrus peel, and raisins.

Palate:Rich fruitcake, with warm spices, gentle sweetness, and a touch of toasted hazelnuts.

Finish:Winter spices, with some dryness.

tomintoul-1977-cognac.title: Tomintoul Cognac Cask Finish
tomintoul-1977-cognac.bodyHtml:
Tomintoul Cognac Cask Finish is a small-batch Speyside single malt Scotch whisky crafted by Master Distiller Robert Fleming. Matured initially in American oak ex-bourbon barrels, selected whiskies are married together before being finished in hand-selected Cognac casks sourced from France. Bottled at 40% ABV, the Cognac finish adds rich sweetness, fruit and nutty complexity while complementing Tomintoul's characteristically smooth and approachable malt profile. 

Food Pairing: Pair with almond pastries, crème brûlée, roasted chestnuts, white chocolate, buttery shortbread, fruit tarts or mild creamy cheeses.

Tasting Notes: Smooth and richly layered, combining honeyed sweetness, citrus and nuts with creamy pastry, butterscotch, dried fruit and warming spice.

Nose: Light and lifted with chestnut, lemon rind, blossom honey and amaretti biscuits alongside hints of chamomile and fennel.

Palate: Sweet choux pastry and Chantilly cream mingle with sugared almonds, butterscotch, golden raisins and subtle rolling tobacco.

Finish: Warming and lingering with white chocolate, panettone and nutmeg fading into ginger spice.

glencadam-1982-white-port.title: Glencadam 38 Year Old 1982 White Port Barrel
glencadam-1982-white-port.bodyHtml:
Nose: Tangy and complex with aromas of honey pomelo, apple skin, lychoe and boiled sweets highlighted with an elderflower and chamomile

Palate: Sweet black cherry and raspberry yoghurt mingled with chocolate coated brazil nuts mocha spices and cacao nibs.

Finish: Morello cherry jam and apple strudel fading into warming sweet spices.

Maturation/Cask: White Port Cask

glenfarclas-family-cask-1956-sp15.bodyHtml:
Glenfarclas 'The Family Casks' 1956 Cask 1767 is a single cask Speyside single malt Scotch whisky from the family-owned Glenfarclas distillery at Ballindalloch. Distilled in 1956 and drawn from cask #1767, it was bottled for the Family Casks Release SP15 at 43.8% ABV and presented in a 700ml bottle. The Family Casks collection was born from the Grant family's foresight in keeping casks from every decade, so that each bottling captures the character of a single year. A rare, long-matured whisky and a remarkable gift for anyone with a connection to 1956.

Serve: Neat, at room temperature, in a nosing glass; take time over it and add water only sparingly, if at all.

Distilled in 1963 at Glenfarclas in Speyside, it matured in a sherry hogshead, cask 178, before being bottled on 10 July 2014 at 45.1% ABV; just 168 bottles of 700ml were filled. The Family Casks exist thanks to George S. Grant, who chose to lay down mature stock for the distillery's own bottlings instead of relying on blenders, so Glenfarclas now holds casks from eight decades. Owned by the Grant family since 1865 and still independent, the distillery sits at the foot of Ben Rinnes and distils twice in direct-fired stills. Each bottle is presented in the series' wooden case.

Serve: Neat, at room temperature, in a tulip glass; let it rest a few minutes before nosing and add a few drops of water only if wanted.

chateau-batailley-magnum-2015.title: Chateau Batailley 2015 1.5L Magnum
chateau-batailley-magnum-2015.bodyHtml:
The Château Batailley 2015 is a highly regarded vintage from this historic 5th Growth Pauillac estate, marking a return to a more generous and opulent style after a series of cooler years. The 2015 growing season in the Médoc was characterized by a superb, dry summer followed by a successful harvest, resulting in a wine with exceptional aromatic intensity and silkier tannins than the structured 2014. Critics have praised this vintage for its "hedonistic" appeal and classical Pauillac pedigree, earning scores such as 94 points from Wine Enthusiast and 93-95 points from Wine Advocate. It is a beautifully balanced, full-bodied red featuring a signature core of crème de cassis, cedar, and graphite, with the structural depth to age gracefully for 20–30 years.

95 Points - James Suckling

Impressive depth to the wine from the outset with a gently smoky edge to the ripe blackberries, blueberries and red plums. Some attractive spicy oak here, too. The mid-weight palate has a very composed and linear shape with a long, succulent and regal finish. Great polish and balance here; the structure is superb. Try from 2022.

92 Points - Wine Spectator

A showy mint note leads off, followed by a flash of ganache before giving way to a core of steeped black currant and fig fruit. A strong charcoal edge through the finish gives this texture and length, while a bay leaf note adds freshness. There's lots to like in this old-school version. Best from 2022 through 2033.

glenfarclas-family-cask-1983-w18-1.title: Glenfarclas The Family Casks 1983 35 Year Old Refill Hogshead Cask 28 Winter 2018 Release
glenfarclas-family-cask-1983-w18-1.bodyHtml:
Glenfarclas The Family Casks 1983 is a single cask Highland single malt from the Winter 2018 release of the Grant family's celebrated vintage series. Distilled in 1983 at Glenfarclas in Speyside, it matured in a refill hogshead, cask 28, for 35 years, before being bottled on 6 December 2018 at 48.8% ABV; just 272 bottles of 700ml were filled. The Family Casks exist thanks to George S. Grant, who chose to lay down mature stock for the distillery's own bottlings instead of relying on blenders, so Glenfarclas now holds casks from eight decades. Owned by the Grant family since 1865 and still independent, the distillery sits at the foot of Ben Rinnes and distils twice in direct-fired stills. Each bottle is presented in the series' wooden case.

Serve: Neat, at room temperature, in a tulip glass; let it rest a few minutes before nosing and add a few drops of water only if wanted.

cht-ht-brion-double-magnum.title: Chateau Haut-Brion Double Magnum 3L
cht-ht-brion-double-magnum.bodyHtml: Château Haut-Brion, when bottled as a Double Magnum (3 liters), presents a wine with enhanced complexity and aging potential. It is known for its intense, layered aromas, rich, balanced palate, and long, lingering finish. The Double Magnum format offers a larger volume, allowing the wine to age more gracefully and develop more nuanced flavors over time.

cht-ht-brion-imperial.title: Cht Ht Brion Imperial 6L
cht-ht-brion-imperial.bodyHtml: Château Haut-Brion is a prestigious First Growth Bordeaux wine from the Graves region. A 6L Imperial bottle (often referred to as an "Imperial") contains the equivalent of eight standard 750ml bottles. According to Manila Wine and Rollers Wine & Spirits, the wine is known for its rich, concentrated flavors, often with notes of red and black fruit, and its long, complex finish. The specific tasting notes can vary depending on the vintage.

plantation-white-rum.title: Plantation Planteray 3 Stars Artisanal White Rum
plantation-white-rum.bodyHtml:
Planteray 3 Stars is a white rum from Planteray Rum, the house formerly known as Plantation, bottled at 41.2% ABV in a 750ml bottle. The name refers to the three Caribbean origins that go into the blend: Barbados, Jamaica and Trinidad. According to the producer, Barbados brings richness and balance, Trinidad adds finesse and Jamaica gives structure. The blend combines aged and unaged rums made with a range of fermentation and distillation techniques, and the bottle is labelled as a product of Barbados. Planteray positions 3 Stars as a cocktail rum, suggesting it for drinks such as the Mojito and the Daiquiri.

Tasting Notes: Light and fresh, with coconut, guava, vanilla, sugar cane honey and soft spice.

Nose: Dried coconut and guava with a little honey and soft spice.

Palate: A spicy entry, then creamy vanilla custard, sugar cane honey and a hint of agave.

Finish: Floral, with zingy spice.

Serve: In a Mojito or Daiquiri, or over ice.

hope-single-malt-whisky.title: Bushmills 16 Year Old Single Malt Irish Whiskey
hope-single-malt-whisky.bodyHtml: Our Bushmills 16 Year Old is a marriage of single malts matured for at least 16 years in hand-selected Oloroso sherry butts and bourbon barrels, then finished in port pipes for up to a year. This triple casking transforms the colour to a beautiful ruby red and adds layers of juicy sun-ripened dark fruit and berries, complex almond nuttiness and a treacly vanilla spice.

glenfarclas-family-cask-1995-s22.title: Glenfarclas 25 Year Old
glenfarclas-family-cask-1995-s22.bodyHtml: From a long-time family-owned distillery, this 25-year-old single malt from Glenfarclas spent its days in 100% Oloroso sherry casks. It’s complex and delicately sherried, a whisky that’s sure not to disappoint. The price for a similar 25-year-old whisky is typically double or triple what this bottle costs making this an extraordinary value.

glenfarclas-family-cask-1995-s22-1.title: Glenfarclas 1995 26 Year Old S22 Cask 6651 Sherry Butt 50.2% ABV
glenfarclas-family-cask-1995-s22-1.bodyHtml:
Glenfarclas 26 Year Old 1995 The Family Casks Cask 6651 is a single cask Speyside single malt Scotch whisky from the Summer 2022 release of The Family Casks, the Grant family's series of single-vintage bottlings from their family-owned distillery at Ballindalloch. Distilled in 1995, the spirit spent 26 years in a sherry butt, cask number 6651, before being bottled on 28 July 2022 at natural cask strength of 50.2% ABV. The cask yielded just 568 bottles. Maturation in a sherry butt places it squarely in the rich, sherried house style for which Glenfarclas is best known. The collection was made possible by the foresight of George S Grant, and the distillery now holds casks from eight decades, so each bottling captures the character of one year. Presented in a 700ml bottle with the wooden Family Casks box, it is a fine gift for a 1995 birth year or anniversary.

Serve: Neat in a nosing glass; at cask strength, a few drops of water will help open the aromas.

2017-chateau-lascombes.title: Chateau Lascombes 2017 750ml
2017-chateau-lascombes.bodyHtml:
92-95 Points - Lisa Perrotti-Brown MW, Wine Advocate
The medium to deep garnet-purple colored 2017 Lascombes gives up lovely scents of roses and lavender over a core of kirsch, crushed black plums and black raspberries with a waft of cinnamon stick. Medium-bodied with a rock-solid frame of firm, ripe, grainy tannins, it has a great core of muscular fruit and lingering spicy notes on the finish.

2014-domaine-de-chevalier.title: Domaine de Chevalier 2021 750ml
2014-domaine-de-chevalier.bodyHtml:
Shiny dark garnet color, black in the middle. Pure, typical and fresh nose of ripe Cabernet Sauvignon in gravelly soil where wild fruits, plants and spices mingle: blackcurrant, blackberry, blueberry, sour cherry, peppermint, cedar, heather On the palate: great unctuous and fresh structure, dense with silky, fine and elegant tannins. The Merlot brings a delicate and fruity flesh. The Cabernet Franc ensures refinement and elegance and the Petit Verdot releases its fruity and spicy energy. A classy finish where the flavors of graphite and licorice appear. The 80% of Cabernet Sauvignon are in balance in this blend and ensure a great wine for laying down, full of freshness.

96 Points - Vinous

The 2021 Domaine de Chevalier was terrific both times I tasted it. Potent and driving, the 2021 dazzles with Cabernet Sauvignon intensity in its aromas, flavors and overall structure. Graphite, spice, menthol, spice, rose petals, mocha and flowers run through a core of red/purplish fruit. The Blanc gets most of the attention at Domaine de Chevalier, but these days I find the red more complete and more interesting. –Antonio Galloni Barrel Sample: 94-96

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This estate, owned by the Bernard family, has produced a ripe, elegant wine. It shows great black fruits and some solid tannins that will stand the wine in good stead as it ages. An impressive wine for the vintage.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2021 Domaine de Chevalier reveals a deep, complex bouquet with aromas of blackberries and blueberries mingled with spices, cigar wrapper and coniferous forest floor, followed by a medium to full-bodied, sweet and concentrated palate animated by bright acids and framed by fine, powdery tannins. It's an impressive effort that will reward a bit of bottle age. It's a blend of 60% Cabernet Sauvignon, 25% Merlot, 10% Petit Verdot and 5% Cabernet Franc. Rating: 94+

94 Points - Decanter

Aromatic nose, perfumed black fruits, bramble tones and a touch of sweet spice. Round and mouthfilling, this has good density and depth for the vintage, tannins are on the juicy plump side with a dry grippy texture though satisfying not austere with the fruit powering through giving cherry and blackcurrant flavours. This has good persistency and doesn't let up - it's not a showstopper at this point but I love the quality of the fruit and the tannins and the lifted acidity as well as the darker more savoury elements of liquorice, black chocolate, graphite and smoked cedar that come in towards the end. Lots going on here with good potential. You get the impression nothing is hiding and I love that. Really the grapes and the terroir on show. A good success and will be interesting to taste in bottle. 2% Cabernet Franc completes the blend. Barrel Sample: 94

93 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

Looking at the Grand Vin, the 2021 Domaine De Chevalier is based on 80% Cabernet Sauvignon, 10% Merlot, and the balance Petit Verdot and Cabernet Franc, with harvest not wrapping up until October 15. It's a terrific wine in the vintage offering ripe currant and darker berry fruits as well as classy oak, graphite, and scorched earth nuances. This medium-bodied, concentrated, balanced 2021 has ripe tannins, integrated acidity, and a great finish. It actually reminds me slightly of the estate’s 2014, albeit in a slightly fresher package.

2016-domaine-de-chevalier.title: Domaine de Chevalier Rouge 2016
2016-domaine-de-chevalier.bodyHtml:
Domaine de Chevalier Rouge 2016 is a profoundly elegant, sophisticated, and deeply structured Grand Cru Classé red wine from the Pessac-Léognan appellation. Crafted from a classic Graves blend of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Petit Verdot, and Cabernet Franc, it presents an intense dark ruby color in the glass. The complex nose bursts with expressive aromas of blackcurrants, dark plums, blueberry compote, tobacco, wood smoke, cedar, and crushed gravel minerality. On the palate, it is medium-to-full-bodied and incredibly racy, delivering concentrated layers of sappy dark berry fruit framed by fine, velvety tannins, vibrant acidity, and an extraordinarily long, earthy, saline finish.

Food Pairing: Pairs wonderfully with roasted rack of lamb, pan-seared duck breast, prime ribeye steak, venison, wild mushroom risotto, and aged hard cheeses.

98 Points - James Suckling

Tobacco, dark fruit and earth on the nose. The palate shows exceptional balance, with incisive acidity and precise dark fruit that are deeply appealing for their harmony. A blend of 55% cabernet sauvignon, 35% merlot, 5% cabernet franc and 5% petit verdot. This is appealing now, but it will evolve wonderfully. Drink now or hold. 10 Years On retrospective.

96 Points - Wine Spectator

The core of fruit flavor here is sappy and dense, with lots of kirsch, raspberry pâte de fruit and plum reduction notes, yet this stays fresh and racy overall, with a bright iron spine, flashes of tea and tobacco and a long finish that shows a wonderful infusion of alder and tobacco flavors. Offers a lovely combination of prodigious fruit details, with a tug of earth. Best from 2024 through 2038.

96 Points - Wine Enthusiast

This elegant wine wears its firm tannic structure lightly. It is densely textured, just starting on its road to maturity. Black-plum and berry fruits give the wine its weight as much as the tannins. It will age well over many years. Drink from 2026.

94 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2016 Domaine de Chevalier is a blend of 55% Cabernet Sauvignon, 35% Merlot, 5% Petit Verdot and 5% Cabernet Franc. Deep garnet-purple colored, it rocks up with expressive warm plums, blueberry compote and cassis scents with suggestions of sandalwood, baking spices and potpourri. Medium-bodied and delicately styled yet with a rock-solid frame of grainy tannins, it sports restrained earth-laced fruit and a long finish.

drumshanbo-gunpowder-gin-cali-orange.title: Drumshanbo Gunpowder Irish Gin with California Orange Citrus
drumshanbo-gunpowder-gin-cali-orange.bodyHtml: Drumshanbo Gunpowder California Orange offers exotic layers of fresh citrus, oriental botanicals, and gunpowder tea with added subtle hints of California Orange citrus to create a gin like no other. Best served with your favourite tonic & a wedge of grapefruit.

vega-sicilia-macan-2018.title: Vega Sicilia Macan 2021
vega-sicilia-macan-2018.bodyHtml:
Vega Sicilia Macán 2021 is a prestigious Spanish red wine produced by Bodegas Benjamín de Rothschild & Vega Sicilia in Rioja. Crafted from 99% Tempranillo and 1% Graciano, this exceptional vintage combines the richness of carefully selected vineyards with refined winemaking. Matured in oak barrels and large wooden vats, it reveals layers of blackberry, ripe cherry, plum, licorice, and subtle spice. Full-bodied yet elegant, with polished tannins, refreshing acidity, and impressive depth, Macán 2021 showcases the sophistication and aging potential of modern Rioja.

Food Pairing: Roasted lamb, grilled ribeye, braised short ribs, venison, Iberian pork, mushroom risotto, aged Manchego, and slow-cooked beef.

 

96 Points - James Suckling

A depth of fresh dark berries and black plums is adorned with complex graphite, balsam, fine spices and cocoa powder with hints of bay leaves and minerals. Tannins are tense, nervy and chalky. Long and tightly wound but well-dissolved. One of the best examples of Macan. An exciting vintage.

95 Points - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2021 Macán is from a year that had above-average rainfall and some hail in June that lowered yields but good weather during harvest. It has 1% Graciano. It comes in at 14.5% alcohol, with a pH of 3.8 and five grams of acidity. This year, they used 100% indigenous yeasts, and the élevage was in new barrels (50%) and 4,000-liter oak foudres and lasted 12 months, followed by another six months in 20,000-liter oak vats. This is serious, harmonious and subtle, more elegant than any vintage before, reflecting the freshness from the year. It's nicely built, very proportioned, with balance, freshness and abundant but fine-grained tannins. It's one of the finest if not the finest vintages to date.

94 Points - Wine Spectator

A graceful red that expands on the palate, revealing lush layers of pureed mulberry, cherry and raspberry fruit, with violet, anise, thyme and sweet paprika accents, plus an underpinning of iron and graphite. Sculpted tannins are fine-grained and limber, providing supple definition for this long, refreshing red. Drink now through 2041.

kavalan-solist-port-cask-team-03.title: Kavalan Scotch & Ponder Solist Port Cask Taiwanese Single Malt Whisky
kavalan-solist-port-cask-team-03.bodyHtml:
Kavalan Scotch & Ponder Solist Port Cask Taiwanese Single Malt Whisky is a distinctive single-cask expression from Kavalan Distillery, selected for Scotch & Ponder and bottled at a powerful 54.8% ABV. Matured in a Port cask and presented at cask strength, it showcases the intensity created by Taiwan's subtropical maturation environment, bringing together concentrated dark fruit, rich sweetness, chocolate, warming spice and oak in a full-bodied single malt.

Food Pairing: Pair with roasted duck, grilled beef, glazed pork, mature cheeses, toasted walnuts, dried fruit or rich dark chocolate.

Tasting Notes: Rich and concentrated with dark berries, dried fruit and Port-driven sweetness layered with chocolate, nuts, oak and warming spice.

Nose: Intense aromas of ripe berries and dried fruit mingle with caramelized sweetness, dark chocolate, toasted nuts and seasoned oak.

Palate: Full-bodied and powerful with rich dark fruit, chocolate and caramel complemented by warming spice, nuts and structured oak.

Finish: Long, warming and persistent with lingering dark fruit, chocolate, spice and Port-influenced sweetness.

chateau-haut-brion-blanc.title: Chateau Haut-Brion Blanc 2020 750ml
chateau-haut-brion-blanc.bodyHtml:
98 Points - James Suckling

Very perfumed with floral, citrus and stone aromas, as well as hints of grapefruit. It’s full-bodied and seamless in texture. Extremely long and fine-grained. 72% sauvignon and 28% semillon. Normally 50/50. Barrel Sample: 97-98

98 Points - Jeb Dunnuck

The 2020 Château Hosanna is up there with the crème de la crème of the appellation and is a true gem. Awesome cassis, candied violets, truffle, chocolate, and underbrush-like notes define the bouquet, and it's full-bodied, with a seamless, silky texture, ultra-fine tannins, and a rock star of a finish. This is another magical Pomerol from the Moueix family that you couldn't have enough of.
Barrel Sample: 96-98

98 Points - Wine Enthusiast

Tightly textured, this is a wine whose future is assured. With intense white fruits, spice and touches of toast from the wood aging, the wine's concentration and taut character combine richness and structure.
Barrel Sample: 96-98

96 Points - Decanter
Grippy fresh, green-tinged flavors, a little more evident than in the Mission Haut-Brion Blanc, here you get more angular acidities, and yet it works. Sauvignon-dominant flavors and aromatics of rosemary, mint, turmeric, lime blossom and steely citrus. Excellent persistency and a deliciously mouthwatering finish.
Barrel Sample: 96

glenfarclas-family-cask-1973-w15.title: Glenfarclas 'The Family Casks' 1973 Winter 2015
glenfarclas-family-cask-1973-w15.bodyHtml:
Glenfarclas 'The Family Casks' 1973 is a single cask Highland single malt from the Winter 2015 release of the Grant family's celebrated vintage series, distilled and bottled at Glenfarclas Distillery on Speyside. Distilled in 1973, it was bottled at 48.6% ABV. It is presented in a 700ml bottle. The Family Casks collection exists thanks to the foresight of George S Grant: Glenfarclas holds casks from the last eight decades, and each release captures the character of a single year in the distillery's history. With the distillation year on the label, it makes a fitting choice to mark a birth year or anniversary.

Serve: Neat, at room temperature, in a nosing glass. Give it time in the glass and add water only a drop at a time, if at all.

lindores-friar-jon-cor-chapter-one.title: Lindores Friar John Cor Cask Strength Congregation Chapter One
lindores-friar-jon-cor-chapter-one.bodyHtml: A cracking cask-strength single malt from Lindores Abbey, matured in a charming congregation of casks. A combo of bourbon, Monbazillac sweet wine, STR, and sherry casks result in a rewardingly silky profile, with heaps of honeyed stone fruit, spiced nuts, figs, and dates.
